column1: '''Adelbert'''<ref name=""P5V5P"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 5]]. Prologue</ref> (アーデルベルト, ''Aaderuberuto''), often referred to by his title as the '''[[Aub Ehrenfest
column2: Sixth Aub Ehrenfest]]''', was the previous [[Nobility/Hierarchy#Archduke
column4: duchy of Ehrenfest]]. After his passing, leadership of the duchy passed to his eldest son and heir, [[Sylvester]].

column1: With his first wife [[Veronica]], Adelbert had three children: [[Georgine]], [[Constanze]] and [[Sylvester]]. He is also the father of [[Ferdinand]].

The fifth [[Aub Ehrenfest]] and his first wife had two sons: [[Bonifatius]] and Adelbert.  As the older and healthier of the two, Bonifatius was originally favored to become the next archduke. However, he had no interest in the position, renouncing his claim while supporting his younger brother as heir. The two boys also had a two paternal half-sisters, [[Irmhilde]] and another girl, who were born to their father's second or third wife.<ref name=""P5V8S6""/>
The latter married into the archducal family of the neighboring duchy Zausengas. Following the [[Civil War
column2: civil war]], she was executed in the purges.<ref name=""FB6QA""/>

column1: Irmhilde was decided to become her half-brother's second wife. When Adelbert brought Ferdinand back to Ehrenfest and Veronica refused to accept him as her child, Irmhilde was made his guardian and was intended to take him as her baptismal son, once the marriage was through, but she died before the wedding could take place.<ref name=""P5V8S6""/>

Early in his rule, Adelbert was stricken with a severe illness that left him close to death. To prepare for the worst-case scenario, Bonifatius was trained to take up his mantle and taught sensitive information usually known only to the ruling archduke. To everyone's relief, Adelbert eventually recovered. However, Bonifatius and his son [[Karstedt]] remained in line the of succession should the archduke die without producing any heirs. Adelbert assigned the archducal family's trusted attendant [[Rihyarda]] to train his Karstedt before his [[baptism]], after which he would enter the castle as an archduke candidate.<ref name=""P5V5P""/>

Adelbert went on to marry his cousin [[Veronica]] as his first wife, with whom he had three children: [[Georgine]], [[Constanze]] and [[Sylvester]]. Georgine, his eldest daughter, was born with a high quantity of [[mana]] and was widely expected to become the next archduchess.<ref name=""P3V4C17"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 4]]. Chapter 17: Georgine's Visit</ref> Her mother [[Veronica]] was extremely strict with her upbringing, fearing that any weakness might allow the older, male [[Karstedt]] to gain the advantage.

However, the battle for succession changed completely when Adelbert and Veronica gave birth to their youngest son [[Sylvester]].  Although Georgine was exceptionally talented and already nearing adulthood, her younger brother's greater mana capacity (coupled with her own disadvantage as a female archduke candidate) made him a strong rival for the archducal seat. After a long and bitter struggle for power, Sylvester was officially chosen as Adelbert's heir.

Devastated at having her political prospects crushed, Georgine turned to ever-worsening harassment of her younger brother. When Adelbert and Veronica began to fear for Sylvester's safety, they married Georgine out of the duchy to [[Ahrensbach]]<ref name=""P3V4C9"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 4]]. Chapter 9: The Archducal Couple Returns</ref> (the same duchy from which Georgine's grandmother [[Gabriele]] had originally married into Ehrenfest<ref name=""P3V4C17"" />). After becoming the third wife of [[Gieselfried
column2: Aub Ahrensbach]], she was no longer able to participate in politics, and Ehrenfest returned to a state of relative peace. At some point, Adelbert's second daughter [[Constanze]] was also married to [[Frenbeltag
column3: another duchy]], becoming the first wife of [[Aub Frenbeltag]].<ref name=""P3V4C9"" />

column1: After Sylvester was already established as future Aub, Adelbert's fourth and youngest child was baptized: [[Ferdinand]]. Unbeknownst to all but a few, Ferdinand was instead brought to Ehrenfest from the [[Sovereignty]] before his baptism. Although the circumstances surrounding the event are unclear, Adelbert attributed it to ""the guidance of the Goddess of Time."" He believed that raising Ferdinand as his son would greatly benefit the future of the duchy.<ref name=""P4V8C14"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 8]]. Chapter 14: Decisions</ref> In a gesture of loyalty, Ferdinand [[Nobility#Name-Swearing
column2: gave his new father his name]] before his baptism.<ref name=""P5V8S6"" />

column1: At the time, Adelbert was engaged to marry his paternal half-sister [[Irmhilde]] as his second wife, at which point he intended to have Ferdinand baptized as her legitimate son. However, Irmhilde died before either the marriage or baptism could take place.<ref name=""P5V8S6"" /> As Adelbert's first wife Veronica deeply resented having an outsider child brought into her family, she refused to adopt Ferdinand or have him baptized as her child. In the end, Ferdinand was introduced to noble society as the son of an unnamed mistress.

Although Ferdinand's status as a child not baptised under a legal wife, meant that he could not compete with Sylvester for the position of archduke, Veronica viewed him as a threat and treated him with open hostility. She directed similar abuse toward [[Florencia]], Sylvester's first wife, who married into Ehrenfest from Frenbeltag. Although Adelbert intervened to protect Ferdinand when possible, Veronica continued to torment him throughout his life, especially as the archduke's health began to fail. In the end, Ferdinand gave up his status as a noble and entered the [[temple]] to escape Veronica's persecution.
When it became clear that Adelbert would not live much longer, he had a final meeting with his son Ferdinand, in which he returned his [[Nobility#Name-Swearing
column2: name stone]] and had him swear to protect Ehrenfest and his brother Sylvester.<ref name=""P4V9E"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 9]]. Epilogue</ref> Adelbert succumbed to his illness shortly after. His funeral was attended by all his children, including Georgine, who returned home for the first time since marrying into [[Ahrensbach]]. Ferdinand, no longer considered a member of the archducal family, was not able to attend the funeral as a family member; he instead watched from a distance as a [[Temple Hierarchy#Blue Priest
column3: blue priest]].<ref name=""P3V4C17"" /> Adelbert was succeeded as archduke by his son [[Sylvester]], the seventh Aub Ehrenfest.

column1: '''Adolphine''' (アドルフィーネ, ''Adorufiine'') is an [[Nobility/Hierarchy#Archduke Candidate
column2: archduke candidate]] from [[Drewanchel]]. After graduating from the [[Royal Academy]], she married [[Sigiswald

column1: After the [[Lanzenave]] invasion is defeated and the consequent demotion of Sigiswald to an Aub, their marriage is dissolved and Adolphine returns to Drewanchel.<ref name=""P5V11C8""/> She is set to become a [[Nobility/Hierarchy#Giebe
column3: Sovereign]] land in her divorce deal to establish her own province.<ref name=""HP1V1C5"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]].'' [[Hannelore's Fifth Year at the Royal Academy]]. Chapter 5: Propositions</ref>

column1: Adolphine has amber eyes<ref name=""P4V6C9"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 6]]. Chapter 9: Dedication Whirling and Ordonnanz Brewing</ref> and wavy wine-red hair.<ref name=""P4V5C18"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 5]]. Chapter 18: The Second-Year Fellowship Gathering</ref> As expected of a high-ranking noble, she is always poised and elegant. She has a tendency to twist her hair with a finger when she is annoyed.<ref name=""RAS1C15"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Royal Academy Stories - First Year]]. Chapter 15: Ortwin - The Drewanchel Siblings</ref> Her graduation hairpin uses a design based on schentis flowers.<ref name=""P5V1C9"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 1]]. Chapter 9: Dedication Whirling (Third Year)</ref>

Although Adolphine always maintains a composed, dignified attitude in public, [[Rozemyne]] notes that she has something of a ""flashy, strong-willed aura"" in addition to her inner gracefulness.<ref name=""P4V7C10"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 7]]. Chapter 10: The Tea Party With Drewanchel</ref> Her true nature shows most in private discussions with close family, such as her brother [[Ortwin]], with whom she is much more direct, ambitious and authoritative.
Adolphine also has a strong sense of pride. Although she is happy for [[Eglantine
column2: Eglantine's]] marriage, she is furious that her engagement to [[Sigiswald
column3: Prince Sigiswald]] is treated as a consolation prize, and she bitterly resents having to give up on her own political prospects.<ref name=""P5V5S1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 5]]. An Unwanted Marriage</ref> In general, Adolphine likes people who are innovative and clever, but dislikes those who are shallow, lazy and self-centered. Although she has high standards for competence, she maintains that she ""permits three mistakes before she loses patience.""

column1: Determined to keep [[Drewanchel]] at the forefront of the nation's trends, Adolphine aggressively collects intelligence in the [[Royal Academy]] and talks to her brother about fashion and beauty at length (much to his disinterest). She personally engages in [[Magic Potions
column2: brewing potions]] and conducting research, both of which are considered unusual activities for [[Nobility/Hierarchy#Archduke Candidate
column3: archduke candidates]] outside of Drewanchel,<ref name=""P5V5S1"" /> and is an exceptionally skilled player of the chess-like game [[gewinnen]].<ref name=""RAS1C15"" />

column1: Adolphine was born in [[Drewanchel]] as the daughter of Aub Drewanchel's first wife. However, her duchy's unusual practice of having the archduke adopt any noble child with sufficient [[mana]] and skill meant that she grew up as one of a large number of archduke candidates, all vying for recognition and the right to become the next Aub.  Adolphine grew up closest to her younger brother [[Ortwin]], since they shared the same mother.
Like many of her siblings, Adolphine dreamed of becoming the next Aub Drewanchel. However, those hopes were dashed when her father and  [[Trauerqual
column2: King Trauerqual]] decided, without consulting her, to have her marry either the first prince [[Sigiswald]] or the second prince [[Anastasius]] when she came of age. Both princes were fervently courting [[Eglantine]] of [[Klassenberg]], a former princess of the deposed previous royal family, with the expectation that whomever she chose would become the heir to the throne. Adolphine would then face the humiliating prospect of marrying whichever prince who failed to become king.

column1: Adolphine cried bitterly after learning about her engagement, furious that her father gave her no say in her own future and devastated at having her ambitions crushed. She shifted her aim to raising her younger brother [[Ortwin]] to become the next Aub in her place, continuing to gather intelligence and lead research at the Royal Academy to maintain Drewanchel's influence in Yurgenschmidt.<ref name=""RAS1C15""/>
During Rozemyne's first year at the [[Royal Academy]], Adolphine's interest is piqued by the glossy hair of the [[Ehrenfest (Duchy)
column2: Ehrenfest]] students at the annual fellowship gathering. She initially disregards Rozemyne as an archduke candidate from a middling duchy, instead advising her brother to focus on outperforming [[Hannelore]] of [[Dunkelfelger]], whom they expect will come first in her year. Earning better grades than Hannelore would reinforce their duchy's standing and give Ortwin a more advantageous position for negotiating a marriage to Hannelore in the future.

column1: Both siblings are shocked when Rozemyne finishes all her classes in record time with impeccable grades. Throughout  the year, Adolphine and Ortwin routinely meet to discuss new Ehrenfest trends, including pound cake and rinsham. She urges him to form closer ties with Rozemyne and even consider her as a marriage prospect, but Ortwin, disconcerted by Rozemyne's strange behavior, is reluctant to comply. He instead strikes up a friendship with her brother Wilfried.<ref name=""RAS1C15""/>

column2: Ehrenfest]] sends out invitations to all duchies for a final tea party before the [[Interduchy Tournament]]. Due to a limit on the number of people they can accommodate, they ask that each duchy only send one person (and their retainers) to attend. [[Ortwin]] wants to attend, but Adolphine is eager to meet Rozemyne after hearing about her from their mutual friend [[Eglantine]], and claims the spot for herself. At the tea party, she compliments Rozemyne on achieving such high grades despite spending two full years asleep in a [[jureve]]. She also praises the taste of the new sweets invented in Ehrenfest and takes home a small jar of [[Inventions#Rinsham
column3: rinsham]] as a gift from Rozemyne.<ref name=""P4V3C11"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 3]]. Chapter 11: The Tea Party for All Duchies</ref>

column2: Prince Anastasius]] renounces his claim to the throne, cementing [[Sigiswald
column3: Prince Sigiswald's]] right to become the next king and allowing [[Eglantine]] to accept Anastasius's proposal. Although this compromise puts a peaceful end to the power struggle, Adolphine is thrust into the unexpected position of marrying not the unwanted prince, but the next king. Ortwin expects her to be pleased that her future standing in the royal family has improved, but Adolphine worries that Sigiswald will mistreat her in favor of his second wife [[Nahelache]].<ref name=""RAS1C15"" /> Nevertheless, Sigiswald formally proposes to Adolphine, and their engagement is made official at the spring Archduke Conference.

column1: When Adolphine returns to the [[Royal Academy]] the next year, her hair is almost as glossy as that of the Ehrenfest students using rinsham. Rozemyne hypothesizes that Drewanchel researched the rinsham sample they received at the previous year's tea party to create a near (but not quite perfect) approximation of their own. During the annual fellowship gathering, Adolphine also probes for information about the [[Plant_Paper#Verification_Paper
column2: verification paper]] utilized for merchant's permits. However, she misidentifies it as magic tool, suggesting that Drewanchel has yet to crack its secrets.<ref name=""P4V5C18"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 5]]. Chapter 18: The Second-Year Fellowship Gathering</ref>

column1: Despite Adolphine's high status and skill at whirling, she is slated to play the secondary role of the [[Schutzaria
column2: Goddess of Wind]] during the dedication whirl at her [[Royal Academy#Graduation Ceremony
column3: graduation ceremony]]. During whirling class, she admits to Rozemyne that she believes only Eglantine is fit to perform the leading role of the [[Goddess of Light]], suggesting that Adolphine  was given the opportunity to do so but turned it down.<ref name=""P4V6C9"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 6]]. Chapter 9: Dedication Whirling and Ordonnanz Brewing</ref> The lead role instead goes to [[Detlinde]], who is markedly less skilled.

column1: As an escort gift for Adolphine's graduation, Prince Sigiswald orders a [[Inventions#Hair_Ornament
column2: hairpin]] from Ehrenfest. When Rozemyne informs Drewanchel that she is able to deliver it during the main socializing season at the Royal Academy, Adolphine invites her and her sister [[Charlotte]] to a tea party primarily attended by students from greater duchies. The girls are delighted by the hairpin, but Rozemyne senses that Adolphine is insecure about being compared to Eglantine, who wore a hairpin at her own graduation last year. She reassures her that she is equally as beautiful in her own way.

column1: When [[Detlinde]] tries to pressure Rozemyne for a hairpin of her own, Adolphine steps in and sharply chastises her rudeness. Charlotte soon diffuses the tension and changes the subject to Ehrenfest's romance stories, but Detlinde appears to hold a grudge against Adolphine afterward. Adolphine arranges to exchange books with Ehrenfest and requests that Wilfried lend her brother a book of knight stories.<ref name=""P4V7C10"" />

At Adolphine's graduation ceremony, Detlinde's whirling causes the magic circle on the Royal Academy stage to briefly flash. Remors spread that the circle is a sign that someone is suitable to become the next Zent. Despite disliking Detlinde on a personal level, Adolphine vehemently hopes that this is true, as it would give her a basis from which to contest her engagement to Sigiswald.<ref name=""P5V5S1"" />

column2: Prince Sigiswald]] are due to be married at the [[Archduke Conference]], the prince informs her that his second wife [[Nahelache]] has recently given birth. Due to the importance of providing stable [[mana]] to a newborn child, he and Adolphine will need to postpone marital intimacy (which would alter Sigiswald's mana) for an indefinite amount of time. Insulted that Sigiswald would marry her while having no intention of treating her as his wife, Adolphine proposes they postpone the marriage until next year, as is considered courteous. However, Sigiswald insists that the marriage must take place so that Adolphine can contribute her mana as a member of the royal family in Nahelache's place. His disrespect in treating her as ""little more than a mana slave"" infurates her.<ref name=""P5V5S1"" />

column1: To quell the voices that call for [[Anastasius]] or [[Detlinde]] to become the next Zent, the royal family pressures Rozemyne into performing the [[Starbind_Ceremony#Royalty_and_Archduke_Candidates
column2: Starbind Ceremony]] and providing a true [[blessing]] at Sigiswald and Adolphine's wedding. Due to pressure from the Sovereign Temple, Rozemyne follows an older form of the ritual involving the [[Divine Instruments
column3: divine instruments]] of the [[God of Darkness]] and [[Goddess of Light]], to supernatural effect. In addition to the standard blessing for the couples, magic circles similar to Detlinde's appear on the stage beneath Sigiswald and Adolphine. The royal family seizes upon this phenomenon as evidence supporting Sigiswald's right to rule.<ref name=""P5V5C4"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 5]]. Chapter 4: Work in the Underground Archive</ref>

column1: The blessing Adolphine receives from Rozemyne motivates her to work hard for the sake of the country. While she still loathes Sigiswald and is reluctant to handle traditional wifely duties, she brews rejuvenation potions for him. At her retainers' insistence, she also compromises by making him a charm for divine protections, hoping that obtaining the blessing Gebordnung the Goddess of Order or Erwachlehren the God of Guidance might make him more responsible and considerate of others. She also makes her own charm to Jugeireise the Goddess of Separation, and prays ever more fervently for an escape.

She initially intends to make Sigiswald a near-replica of the highly effective potion Rozemyne distributed at the [[Dedication Ritual]] at the Royal Academy, which she developed through her own research. However, her retainer [[Oderkunst]] warns her that a more effective potion may simply prompt the royal family to work her even harder. She decides to keep the highly effective potions as a secret between herself and her retainers, instead preparing regular Royal Academy potions for Sigiswald.<ref name=""P5V5S1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 5]]. An Unwanted Marriage</ref>

column2: [[Hannelore's Fifth Year at the Royal Academy]]}}

column1: As compensation for the breach of the marriage contract with Sigiswald, Adolphine not only got a divorce from the former prince turned archduke, but also received at least some of the land turned over from the Sovereignty to Drewanchel to rule over as compensation. Inspired by Lady Rozemyne, she intends to build a research city in her new province.<ref name=""HP1V1C5"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]].'' [[Hannelore's Fifth Year at the Royal Academy]]. Chapter 5: Propositions</ref>
*'''[[Lisbeth]]''' - An attendant who served Adolphine even before her marriage to Sigiswald and accompanied her to the Sovereignty upon her engagement to the prince.<ref name=""P5V5S1""/>
*'''[[Oderkunst]]''' - A sovereign scholar, formerly of Drewanchel, who was assigned as her retainer upon her marriage to Prince Sigiswald.<ref name=""P5V5S1""/>

*'''Research:''' Unlike most other duchies, the archduke candidates of Drewanchel commonly do research of their own. Adolphine is quite skilled in developing and reverse engineering projects of other duchies. Among other things, she was able to create a new potion recipe with similar effects, albeit of lesser efficiency, as the rejuvenation potions given out by Rozemyne at the [[Dedication Ritual]] in a manner of weeks, despite having none of Rozemyne's potion to analyze.<ref name=""P5V5S1""/>
*Adolphine almost always beats her brother when the two of them play [[gewinnen]].<ref name=""RAS1C15""/>

*Although Adolphine has spent relatively little time with [[Rozemyne]], she thinks highly of her and sympathizes with her struggles as a fellow archduke candidate subject to the whims of royalty. She comments that if the two of them had been in the same grade, her student days would have been ""eventful and deeply entertaining.""<ref name=""P5V5S1""/>
*Adolphine was born in autumn, a season associated with wisdom and the arts, which is fitting for an avid researcher. At her [[Royal Academy]] graduation, she also plays the role of the [[Schutzaria
column2: Goddess of Wind]], a goddess closely identified with autumn.<ref name=""P5V1C9""/>

column1: Adrett takes the shape of a large, upright walking [[Shumil]], like the originals [[Schwartz and Weiss]] and has light-green fur.<ref name=""P5V7C13""/>
Adrett was built to the single purpose of looking for books and documents and is incapable of speech. As such it has no personality to speak of.<ref name=""P5V7C13""/>

At the start of Lady Rozemyne's fourth term at the [[Royal Academy]], she is to participate in a research project with Professor Hirschur to create a magic tool derived from on Schwartz and Weiss. Before they can start their work, Rozemyne mysteriously disappears while donating mana to the statue of [[Mestionora]] in the [[Royal Academy/Library
column2: Royal Academy Library]]. In Rozemyne's absence, Hirschur begins the groundwork for creating the magic tool, but gets stuck, when she finds out that only someone omni-elemental can create such a magic tool. column1: The country of Lanzenave came into being about 400 years ago. Shortly before it's founding, Yurgenschmidt was ruled by [[Aeussewahl
column2: Zent Aeussewahl]] and three of his sons managed to obtain a [[Grutrissheit]]. Ultimately [[Aeussewahl]] chose his son [[Heileind]] as his successor. Unable to accept being passed over, his brother [[Tollkuehnheit]] took his magic tool and went looking for a new land to settle. Accompanied by his wife and retainers, he sailed through the southern country gate and eventually happened across an inhabited land, with a comparatively poor population, unable to use any magic. While the area didn't appear to be rich in any valuable natural resources, it was able to sustain the local population, which was good enough for [[Tollkuehnheit]]. He used his [[Grutrissheit]] to create a duchy foundation and raise an entire ivory city before the eyes of the stunned locals. Having never seen any magic of this scale, or potentially any magic at all, this awed the locals so much that many of them took to worshipping Tollkühnheit as an emissary from the land of gods, making it easy for him to crown himself the king of this new land and crism it [[Lanzenave]].

column1: At an unknown point in [[Yurgenschmidt]]'s history, [[Albsenti
column2: Zent Albsenti]], who was an expert in the creation of magic tools, had many children, but doted on a single son in particular. This son, [[Neigenheit]], lacked one element and the drive to obtain it via prayer, yet his mother was still determined to make him her successor. For this purpose, she created physical magic tool version of the [[Grutrissheit]], that even someone not omni-elemental could use. With this book and her all her political power behind the move, the nobility had no choice but to accept [[Neigenheit]] as the next Zent. Seeing this magic tool as the crystallization of his mother's love, [[Neigenheit]] chose to bestow it upon his own son [[Rundsein]], rather than have him obtain his own [[Grutrissheit]] through proper means, despite [[Rundsein]] being omni-elemental. He also neglected to tell his son about the book teleporting to the room, should the owner die.<ref name=""P5V8C9""/>

Alexis was born in the province of [[Kirnberger]] in [[Ehrenfest (Duchy)
column2: Ehrenfest]] as the son of [[Giebe Kirnberger]] and his second wife, who was a [[Ehrenfest (Duchy)#Leisegang Faction

column1: To protect Alexis from Veronica's persecution, his parents and his father's first wife worked together to minimize his relationship to his Leisegang relatives in public. When visiting the archduke's castle before his winter debut, he was introduced as Giebe Kirnberger's son, and spent his time with his father and his father's first wife rather than his own mother. The family's caution paid off, as Veronica considered him not a member of the Leisegang faction, but merely the son of a neutral giebe. She only spoke to him once and overlooked him afterward.

Growing up, Alexis was told little of this and only learned the story by piecing it together himself. He never formed a strong opinion of Veronica, and struggled to empathize with either the Leisegang or Veronica factions.<ref name=""P5V4E"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 4]]. Epilogue</ref> After Veronica was imprisoned and her grandson [[Wilfried]] had his winter debut, Alexis was approached by [[Lamprecht]] and asked to serve as a [[knight

column1: When [[Rozemyne]] and [[Wilfried]] enter their first year in the [[Royal Academy]], Alexis is introduced as one of Wilfried's guard knights. The much more experienced Alexis typically comes out on top.<ref name=""RAS1C11"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Royal Academy Stories - First Year]]. column2: divine protections]] through prayer, the royal family gives special permission to the graduates of that year to redo the ritual at the end of their final year. Alexis participates in the ritual and manages to acquire the divine protection of both Angriff the God of War and Steifebrise the God of the Gale.<ref name=""P5V3C16""/>

column3: Leisegang faction]] rises in power. Because many of the Leisegang nobles are bitterly resentful of Wilfried, he becomes isolated and unpopular despite his supposed position as the new aub. Insecure about Rozemyne's much stronger political base, and spurred on by his new retainer [[Barthold]], he sends Alexis to visit his father in [[Kirnberger]] and ascertain whether Rozemyne is planning a bid for the archducal seat.

column1: To Alexis's relief, [[Giebe Kirnberger]] reports that Rozemyne has no intention of becoming the next archduchess. However, he also notes that he finds Rozemyne a more compelling candidate, and challenges his son's belief that she is too unconventional for the role. As they discuss the matter, Alexis realizes that Wilfried's perspective is heavily influenced by his upbringing under [[Veronica]] and his attachment to his former head attendant [[Oswald]], who was forced to resign during the purge.

Seeing Wilfried's increasing jealousy and paranoia frustrates Alexis so much that he ""wishes for nothing more than to resign and return to Kirnberger."" His father reprimands him for giving up so easily. He urges him to do what it takes to protect Wilfried, even from Barthold's influence, and drag him onto the right path. Failing that, he should gather enough evidence to have Wilfried disinherited and his retainers relieved of duty. With new motivation, Alexis returns to the castle.<ref name=""P5V4E""/>

column2: civil war]], the newly crowned Zent [[Trauerqual]] gave in to the pressure of his allies and enacted a massive purge throughout the entire country, which saw not only the current Aub Frenbeltag and his first wife executed, but also their chosen successors, leaving only him to take up the mantle of rule in the devastated and mana-starved duchy.<ref name=""P5V3E"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 5 Volume 3]]. Epilogue</ref>

column1: With him being the older brother of Aub Ehrenfest's first wife and his own first wife being the older sister of Aub Ehrenfest, Frenbeltag is generally capable of gaining the upper hand in most negotiations with their neighboring duchy, despite having fallen below them in duchy ranking as a result of the civil war.

column1: Aurelia is somewhat soft-spoken and withdrawn. Growing up as an unfavored child in Ahrensbach, she was ostracized by her family, making her cautious and slow to form new relationships. After moving to Ehrenfest, she is afraid to show her face in public due to insecurities about her appearance; however, she strongly hopes to find acceptance and build a positive relationship with her new family, especially her mother-in-law [[Elvira]] and sister-in-law [[Rozemyne]].

Although archnobles are expected to be composed at all times, Aurelia is unusually expressive. Her emotions often show on her face even when she is fully veiled, revealing her nervousness and uncertainty in unfamiliar situations.<ref name=""P4V5C9"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 4 Volume 5]]. Chapter 9: The Dyeing Competition</ref>

column3: Aub Ehrenfest]] refused their requests for a marriage.

column1: Aurelia is the daughter of Aub Ahrensbach's younger brother and his third wife. Her mother was born in [[Frenbeltag]]. Due to taking different sides during the civil war, the treatment of her mother and by extension her mother's children worsened considerably, and in Aurelia's case, this was further exacerbated by her appearance, leading to her being treated very poorly by the majority of her family. Her younger sister [[Martina]] managed to avoid the worst of this treatment due to being smart and friendly, to the point of even being described as ""loved by all.""

From early childhood, Aurelia was bullied and mocked on account of her appearance. The shape of her eyes led others to say that she always looked like she was scheming something awful and carried the cruelness of some base villain.

Aurelia wanted to become a scholar or attendant, but due to her precarious social position was denied the chance to choose her own path. With the Aub's first wife having been ill for some time and getting weaker, Aurelia's father expected Lady Georgine to rise in status and thus tried to ingratiate himself with her. Since Georgine's daughter [[Alstede
column2: Lady Alstede]] was lacking in apprentice guard knights at the time, he forced Aurelia to pick the knight's course to become Alstede's knight, even though it was already clear that Alstede would be marrying into another duchy after coming of age and leave the archduke's family two years later at most. Having to lock her future into a career not of her choosing was very frustrating for Aurelia. Furthermore, she was unable to fit into the friend-groups of her fellow students and retainers, leading her to spend much time in the knight's building on the excuse of training.

column1: It was there that she met Lamprecht, who initially only wished for the three year younger girl to introduce him to other female Ahrensbach students, since [[Veronica
column2: Lady Veronica]] had decreed he was to marry someone from Ahrensbach. At the time, Ehrenfest was much lower in rank than Ahrensbach, so Aurelia remarked that she didn't believe anyone would be willing to marry into the lower duchy, unless they were willing to escape their homes like her. This caused Lamprecht to ask her if she would be willing to go with him, which Aurelia agreed to. Despite not spending much time together, the two quickly developed feelings for each other.

column1: Initially, her father vehemently opposed allowing his daughter to marry into a duchy as low in the rankings as Ehrenfest. After intense negotiations, he only allowed Lamprecht to escort Aurelia at her graduation to serve as one last memory before their final farewell. And following an incident at the Ehrenfest temple involving [[Count Bindewald]], [[Sylvester
column2: Aub Ehrenfest]] wouldn't let anyone from Ahrensbach marry into Ehrenfest. Furthermore, their mana was far enough apart that Lamprecht could not sense Aurelia's mana at their first meeting.

column1: '''Barthold''' (バルトルト, ''Barutoruto'') is a mednoble apprentice scholar of the [[Veronica Faction
column2: Former Veronica Faction]] and eventually becomes one of [[Wilfried]]'s retainers.<ref name=""P5V1S1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 1]]. Fantasy versus Reality</ref>

column1: Barthold is an attention seeker, who is always trying to be the center of any group he is part of and controlling of anyone of a lesser status than himself. He is practically a worshipper of Veronica, and as such, has a very strong dislike of [[Sylvester]] for imprisoning her.<ref name=""P5V1S1""/>

Prior to the purge of the former Veronica faction, Barthold's family was close to [[Muriella]]'s family. As such he was considered a strong candidate for marriage for her. Whenever they were together, he would always try to command her around.<ref name=""P5V1S1""/>

In the beginning of Rozemyne's third year at the Royal Academy, the students are informed about the coming purge of the Veronica faction. Barthold decides to give his name to Wilfried. When he learns that Muriella intends to give hers to [[Rozemyne]], he demands that she changes her mind and serve Wilfried as well, but with their parents soon to be out of power or dead, Muriella ignores his demands.

Several days later, the students learn that the purge claimed the lives of far fewer nobles than anticipated - only five of them have lost their parents and are thus required to give their names, including Barthold. Lady Rozemyne organizes a trip to the gathering spot, during which Barthold is able to acquire all the necessary ingredients to make his name-swearing feystone, and soon after, he gives his name to Wilfried.<ref name=""P5V1S1""/>

His sister Cassandra initially leans toward giving her name to Rozemyne, but Barthold manages to talk her into choosing [[Charlotte]]. To her, he mentions Rozemyne's poor health and how Charlotte will most likely marry into another duchy, implying the much better marriage prospects that his sister would have there, after moving with her lady, than in Ehrenfest, where everyone knows them to be the children of criminals, but inside the primary reason for his advice is that he is straight up disgusted by the thought of his sister serving a Leisegang.

His own decision to join Wilfried is partially fuelled by this same hated for the Leisegangs, and an even bigger hatred for Sylvester. While he doesn't hold any grudge against the three archduke candidates, he has no particular sympathy for them either.

Due to him vowing himself to Wilfried and talking his sister out of joining Rozemyne - and his arguments swaying other girls, who had been listening in, to do the same - he is taking into [[Oswald]]'s confidence and the two conspire to build up Wilfried and rebuild the former Veronica faction around him in the future<ref name=""SSC2C12""/>.

column1: '''Benno''' (ベンノ, ''Benno'') is the owner of the [[Plantin Company]] and a highly successful merchant. He is [[Lutz]]'s teacher and boss, and [[Myne]]'s business partner. He formerly operated the [[Gilberta Company]].
His instrumental role in spreading the [[printing]] and [[Plant Paper
column2: plant paper]] industries led Myne to name him among her [[Honorary Titles#Gutenberg (Title)

column1: Benno has curly, milk-tea colored hair that gives him a soft impression at first glance. However, his dark red eyes are ""brimming with confidence,"" and he reminds Myne of a CEO running a venture capital firm.<ref name=""P1V1C24"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 1 Volume 1]]. Chapter 24: Meeting with the Merchant</ref> He dresses in finer clothes than the average merchant.

Benno seems cold and menacing at first glance. He is hot-blooded and confrontational as a merchant, always taking challenges head on and never backs down when facing rivals and authorities alike. He also has a hot temper and tends to yell at people.

However, he shows concern for his family and friends, willing to go the extra length to protect those he cares about. Concerned about Myne's health, he paid her three small gold coins for information on [[Inventions#Rinsham
column2: rinsham]], which was enough to buy a magic tool used to ease the symptoms of the [[Devouring]].

column1: Benno is said to have softened a little due to Myne’s influence.

After his father was killed by bandits, Benno took over the operation of the [[Gilberta Company]], abandoning his dream in order to protect his family’s store.<ref name=""P1V3SS4"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 1 Volume 3]]. Mark - The Master and I</ref> At the time, his mother was bedridden with grief, and Benno had recently reached adulthood. With the future of the company in doubt, the majority of [[lehange]] chose not to renew their contracts. Among those that remained, [[Mark]] assisted Benno in rebuilding the store, becoming his trusted right-hand man.<ref name=""P1V3SS4"" />

Around that time, Benno came into conflict with [[Gustav]]. Gustav proposed marriage to Benno’s mother shortly after she became a widow. He also attempted to arrange a marriage between his daughter and Benno shortly after the death of Benno’s lover [[Liz]], and later suggested a marriage between his sons and Benno's two younger sisters, causing one of the sisters to flee to another city. Benno interpreted his offers as insensitive, thinly veiled attempts to take over the company and developed a lasting dislike for Gustav.<ref name=""P1V3SS3"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 1 Volume 3]]. Benno-Pound Cake Sampling</ref>

*'''Negotiation:''' Benno is a ruthless haggler, who never fails to make a profit, given the opportunity. Although Myne successfully haggles against him a few times, her success is largely due to Benno's fondness for her.

*'''Product Development:''' While most merchants buy and sell goods that are already being produced, Benno has a tendency to invest in product concepts and start new lines of business. This can be both an asset and a liability. Even though most of his ventures are profitable, Myne worries that he spreads himself too thin.
*Both the Japanese and English voice actors of Benno are known for voicing Sett from League of Legends.

**His Japanese voice actor, Takehito Koyasu is well-known for voicing antagonist masterminds, like Dio Brando from Jojo's Bizarre Adventure, Sugou Nobuyuki from Sword Art Online, and Zeke Yeager from Attack On Titan.

**His English voice actor, Xander Mobus is well-known for voicing villains, either schemers like Tanzo Kubo from Neo The World Ends With You, or an immature madman like Telence/Terence D'Arby from Jojo's Bizarre Adventure Stardust Crusaders. His most recognized role, however, is Ren Amamiya/Joker from Persona 5 series.
*Benno's dream was to become a world-influential merchant.<ref name=""P1V3SS4""/>

column2: paper-making]], he was even worse than Myne with her tiny hands.<ref name=""P1V3C14"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 1 Volume 3]]. Chapter 14: Tools and Selecting a Workshop</ref>

column1: '''Bezewanst''' (ベーゼヴァンス, ''Beezevansu'') is the former High Bishop of the [[temple]] of [[Ehrenfest (Duchy)
column2: Ehrenfest]]. He bears a strong grudge against the commoner [[Myne]].
noble]], he is the younger brother of [[Veronica]] and a relative of Ehrenfest's archducal family.

column1: Bezewanst is a large old man with long white hair and beard, and usually wears the white robes of the High Bishop. Unlike most Blue Priests, he does have a noble's ring.

The High Bishop leaves most of the work of actually running the temple to Ferdinand and spends most of his time simply enjoying the perks of his position. Due to his older sister [[Veronica]] (mother of the current [[Sylvester
column2: Aub Ehrenfest]]) covering for the numerous crimes he commits as High Bishop and their unusually close relationship, he takes a dark sense of joy using the connection to elevate his position in noble society.

column1: His true personality is scarred by a deep inferiority complex over not being recognized as a true noble despite his archduke's blood. He is well aware that most true nobles disrespect him as a person and only put up a show of respect due to his connection to his older sister, which is a great source of frustration and anger to him. This constant barrage of negative emotions have made him into a very vengeful and cruel person, who seeks to release his pent up anger on those of lesser status than him, whenever he thinks he can get away with it. Due to his sister's protection, he could get away with a shocking amount of crimes and abuse, which made him arrogant on top of his other vices.
He is also very vengeful and will go to great length to avenge himself upon those he deems to have wronged him, prioritizing his revenge over the good of the temple and duchy.
He is able to quite competently hide his character flaws and project an air of benevolence and kindness much in contrast to his true self, if he deems it beneficial to himself.

Bezewanst, born with pure-blood of the archduke's family as the youngest son of the fifth Aub Ehrenfest ([[Sylvester]]'s grandfather), possessed relatively low mana in comparison with his kin, and was therefore raised, since his baby years, in the temple as a priest and continues his life there. His mother died when she gave birth to him, so nobody could protect him from his fate. With his mother's death, the position of his father's first wife fell onto the second wife, who belonged to the Leisegang faction. Giebe Leisegang demanded that Bezewanst was to be put into the temple. As his daughter became Bezewanst's father's first wife, Bezewanst's fate was sealed. Bezewanst was [[Veronica]]'s last living blood relative, which made her protect her little brother as much as possible. He was granted the position of the High Bishop in the temple, and his embezzlement and further small crimes were covered up by Veronica.

Since he was never officially recognized as a noble, he was never sent to the [[Royal Academy]], and thus neither acquired a [[Schtappe]] nor learned to properly use his mana. He also never learned how to form a [[highbeast]], and thus had to rely on coaches, much to his displeasure. His sister Veronica gifted him with a noble's ring, but due to his lack of training, he was unable to make proper use of it.

column1: '''Bonifatius''' (ボニファティウス, ''Bonifatiusu'') is [[Rozemyne]]'s noble grandfather and the father of [[Karstedt]]. His brother was the previous Aub Ehrenfest, [[Adelbert

column3: Ehrenfest]] and a former commander of the [[Knight's Order]], Bonifatius is a highly skilled [[knight]] and trained [[Angelica]] as his disciple. Bonifatius has become the acting Aub in the event of [[Sylvester]]'s absence.

column1: Bonifatius has light blue eyes and blond, almost chestnut-colored hair.<ref name=""FB2CharacterDesign"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Fanbook 2]]. Character Design Sheets</ref> He closely resembles his son, [[Karstedt]]. He is a ""big guy,"" with a more muscular build than most men his age. Rozemyne thinks he has a sharp gleam in his eye.<ref name=""P3V4C7"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 4]]. Chapter 7: Let’s Print More Stuff</ref>

column2: nobles]], Bonifatius greatly dislikes putting up a false face and will generally show his emotions completely openly, though he is fully capable of hiding them should the situation require it. He is very devoted to his family, particularly the only girl among his grandchildren, [[Rozemyne]], though he tries to keep his distance from her for fear of accidentally injuring or killing her.

column1: While he prefers to trust his instincts and tends to leave the thinking to other people, he is still an intelligent and well educated man.

Bonifatius was born as one of the sons of the fifth [[Aub Ehrenfest]]. Since he was older and healthier than his brother, and had all the necessary qualities, talents and skills to fulfill the role, he was supposed to become the next [[Nobility/Hierarchy#Aub
column2: Aub]]. But he had absolutely no interest in leading the duchy, and thus advocated to have his younger brother become the successor. Their father was reluctant, but eventually gave in, but only in exchange for Bonifatius training the future Aubs of the duchy, naturally starting with his younger brother.<ref name=""P5V5P"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 5]]. Prologue</ref>

column1: Apart from his brother, Bonifatius had two sisters, Irmhilde and an unnamed girl. The latter married into Zausengas's archducal family, prior to the [[Civil War
column2: civil war]] and was then executed, presumably along with her husband, in the post-civil-war purges.<ref name=""FB6QA""/>

column1: Imhilde, Bonifatius and Adelbert's half-sister from another mother, presumably the Fifth Aub Ehrenfest's second or third wife, was engaged with her half-brother Adelberg to become his second wife. When Adelberg brought Ferdinand back to Ehrenfest and his first wife Veronica refused to accept him, Irmhilde was made his guardian and also intended to accept him as her son after the marriage, but she died before the pair could be wedded.<ref name=""P5V8S6""/>

In contrast to what many people might believe, Bonifatius seems to have behaved like a rather normal archduke candidate in his days at the [[Royal Academy]]. Even during [[ditter]], he didn't charge blindly ahead, but instead took charge and commanded his troops, only rarely having the chance to bring his personal combat prowess to bear. He was good friends with students from [[Dunkelfelger]] and the now defunct Werkestock. He did manage to accidentally destroy a shrine during a ditter match, but reported the damage immediately after.
Like most archduke candidates, he never went to the library personally, instead opting to send scholars on the few occasions he required books or documents.

Considering how [[Rihyarda]] appears to have some considerable insight into Bonifatius' behaviour at the Royal Academy, it is very likely that they attended the Royal Academy at the same time.<ref name=""P4V8C11"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 8]]. Chapter 11: Sitting Out the Archduke Conference</ref>

When his brother fell seriously ill before having any children capable of taking up the scepter, Bonifatius was trained to become the next Aub, if needed. However, his brother recovered and was able to rule until his children had become able to succeed him.

When Veronica dropped [[Georgine]], after [[Sylvester]]'s birth, Bonifatius was sympathetic with his niece and wished he could console her, but due to his first wife being one of the people ostracized by Veronica and the overall political situation, he was forced to keep his distance.<ref name=""P5V5P"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 5]]. Prologue</ref>

Following the advice of his family, Bonifatius kept himself at a distance from [[Rozemyne]], as he is quite expressive and she is quite fragile. Everyone - including himself - feared he may harm her accidently. He is the former commander of the [[Knight's Order]] of Ehrenfest.
*'''Enhancement Magic:''' Bonifatius is a master of [[Magic#Enhancement Magic
column2: enhancement magic]]. He's so proficient and used to the skill that he often activates the enhancement on instinctively, without consciously being aware. This combined with his outgoing, emotional personality means he often goes overboard on opponents. He is not only able to enhance his strength and speed, but can also enhance his senses to superhuman levels.

column1: *'''Mana Capacity:''' As an archduke candidate, Bonifatius has enough mana capacity to liberally perform enhancement magic, despite its mana cost being high enough to make it unpopular even among archnobles.

*'''Mana Elements:''' His natural affinities are not known, but he became omni-elemental, through gaining the divine protection of gods, after redoing the ritual in Ehrenfest's temple, after Rozemyne's third year at the Royal Academy.<ref name=""P5V5C2""/>

*'''Divine Protections:''' It isn't known how many divine protections Bonifatius obtained at the Royal Academy. After redoing the ritual at the Ehrenfest temple, he managed to gain the divine protection of seventeen gods and subordinate gods in total. He only stated that he mostly gained the favour of fighting related gods, and that he became omni-elemental, but did not go into any details.<ref name=""P5V5C2""/>

*'''Water Gun''': Despite some initial difficulty with the correct pronounciation, Bonifatius was eventually able to learn Rozemyne's Watergun spell. But due to his mana capacity being lower than Rozemyne's and Ferdinand's and the spells high mana requriements, he can't use is as effectively them.<ref name=""FB6QA""/>
*'''Combat:''' Despite being in his sixties, Bonifatius is still one of the strongest knights in Ehrenfest. Very few could match him in direct combat.
*'''Instinct:''' Although Bonifatius is not a thinker nor planner, he has very sharp instinct that allows him to find out important clues, and his guesses are right most of the time.

*'''Training:''' Bonifatius is very good in training knights. His training regimen is notoriously brutal, but those who could survive his training like [[Angelica]] and [[Cornelius]] turn out to be excellent.
*'''Strength:''' Bonifatius is extremely strong physically even without using enhancement magic. He could easily lift and toss Cornelius, who's almost fully grown as an adult.

*Due to ""Bonifatius"" being long and difficult to pronounce, studio staffs shorten his name and refer to him as ""Boni"" (ボニ) during the recording session of [[Drama CD]].<ref>''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Fanbook 2]]</ref>

*Bonifatius cultivated a [[manablade]] during Rozemyne's coma after hearing about [[Stenluke]] from [[Angelica]], just so that he could have Rozemyne imbue mana into it. It is for naught however, since [[Ferdinand]] forbade her from pouring mana into manablades before she learns about the fundamentals in the [[Royal Academy]].
*While Bonifatius does not consider Rozemyne to be Elvira's child, he firmly believes that Karstedt is her father.<ref name=""FB2QA"" />

column1: Brigitte's became engaged to [[Hassheit]] soon after her father died and Helfried became the next Giebe Illgner. However, Brigitte discovered that her fiancé and his family were plotting to have her brother eliminated after the wedding, so they could take over Illgner. Brigitte furiously cancelled the engagement of her own accord, without observing the proper protocols and manners expected. This brought much shame upon her and the entire province of Illgner, allowing Hassheit and his family to relentlessly mock and harass Brigitte at every opportunity. As a result, she was escorted by her brother during her graduation because she couldn't find another partner.<ref>''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 5]]. Two Marriages</ref>

The scandal was bad enough that the majority of nobles in Illgner left the province, fostering a near self-sacrificial spirit in Brigitte, where she was ready to sacrifice her own happiness for the sake of her homeland. Her reputation was so maligned that she agreed to take on the task of serving as [[Rozemyne
column2: Rozemyne's]] guard knight even though it meant entering the [[temple]] and the lower city.

column1: *[[Nadine]] is Brigitte's [[attendant]].<ref name=""P3V2E"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 2]]. Epilogue</ref>

Brigitte begins serving as a guard [[knight]] for [[Rozemyne]], when she is adopted by the archduke. Later, Rozemyne hears about Brigitte's family circumstances and thinks it's unfortunate that she has little hope of getting married. To help her show off her beauty, Rozemyne designs a new [[Inventions#Halter-Top Dress
column2: halter-top dress]] designed to suit Brigitte's well-built body type for the next Starbind Ceremony in hopes that she can find a new husband. The dress is part of Brigitte's reward for helping  [[Angelica]] pass her studies from the [[Royal Academy]].

column1: As Rozemyne gathers ingredients for her [[jureve]], Brigitte becomes closer with her other guard knight, [[Damuel]]. When the two of them next attend the Starbind Ceremony together, Brigitte is approached by her ex-fiancé [[Hassheit]]. He proposes to her mockingly, saying that she can't possibly hope to marry anyone else at this point. However, Damuel stands up for her and proposes himself, promising to raise his mana to the level expected of a mednoble. Brigitte interprets this offer as a kindhearted attempt to save her from humiliation, but to her surprise, Damuel later insists that he meant it and truly intends to propose.

[[Elvira]] invites Brigitte to her tea parties, which helps reduce some of the scorn other nobles show toward Brigitte. However, Elvira is unimpressed when Brigitte says she wants to go back to her Illgner once she is married, understanding that to mean that Rozemyne is secondary to Illgner.

Brigitte continues to help Rozemyne gather all the ingredients for her jureve, and later goes with [[Rozemyne]] to visit her home province of [[Illgner]]. She is delighted when Rozemyne says she intends to set up the [[Plant Paper
column2: paper-making]] industry there. However, Rozemyne warns her that the way the [[Nobility
column4: commoners]] interact in Illgner, with little to no formality, could cause trouble as more nobles visit the province. Brigitte thanks her for her warning and promises to help the citizens of Illgner prepare for the change.

column1: While [[Rozemyne]] recovers from poisoning in her jureve, Brigitte and her other [[Knight
column2: guard knights]] train under [[Bonifatius]] to improve their skills. As promised, Damuel works hard to increase his [[mana]] capacity and proposes to Brigitte at the next [[Starbind Ceremony]]. However, the two of them have very different expectations about what will happen after they marry. She expects to resign from service and return to Illgner, while Damuel expects to continue serving Rozemyne in the [[temple]]. Despite her brother specifically warning her of the possibility of Damuel being unwilling or unable to leave Rozemyne's service, Brigitte does not try to talk about this with Damuel and just lets events unfold as they would. As a result, Damuel ends up turning down the engagement with Brigitte.<ref name=""P3V5S3"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 5]]. Two Marriages</ref> Brigitte is well aware of Damuel originally being assigned to guard Lady Rozemyne as punishment and the affront that leaving her service would entail, so she hold no hard feelings toward him and feels responsible for the situation escalating to the point it had in the first place. At Lady Elvira's suggestion, Brigitte resigns from Lady Rozemyne's service a few days later, supposedly to concentrate entirely on finding a suitable husband before she turns twenty, though in all due likelihood Brigitte would put her own need to help Illgner above the needs of Rozemyne proved her unsuitable to remain a guard knight for her daughter in Elvira's eyes.<ref name=""P3V5S6"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 5]]. The Laynoble Guard Knight</ref>

column1: To prevent Rozemyne from making rash decisions in order to support her knights' marriage, Elvira soon finds a suitable [[Viktor
column2: mednoble husband]] for Brigitte. After their marriage, she returns to support the [[Plant Paper
column3: paper-making]] industry in [[Illgner]], while Rozemyne remains asleep.

column1: In the autumn before Rozemyne's third year at the Royal Academy, Brigitte and Viktor are blessed with the birth of a healthy girl, they name [[Lilaroze]].
When the girl is one and a half years old, Illgner is informed by [[Florencia
column2: Lady Florencia]] via letter of an impending invasion by [[Ahrensbach]] forces, led by [[Georgine
column3: Lady Georgine]]. Soon after, Brigitte receives an [[Ordonnanz]] by Rozemyne, giving more details. Somehow the archducal family learned that [[Ferdinand
column4: Lord Ferdinand]] was near fatally wounded in an assassination attempt and that Georigne and her forces are already arrayed somewhere near the border, making it extremely likely that they will invade within a day or two. Despite being retired, Brigitte joins the patrols and is there, when the first enemies are spotted. A group of four nobles wearing Ahrensback capes, uses black weapons to drain mana from Illgner's ground. The Illgner patrol launchers a couple of offensive magic tools at them, causing two of them to dispell their black weapons to defend the group with shields. Brigitte senses many other mana wielders hidden in the surrounding woods and thus orders a retreat. While still on their way back to the Giebe's mansion, they send warnings ahead of them via Ordonnanz.

column1: At the meeting of Giebe Illgner and his advisors, Brigitte states that she will join the fighting. Viktor tries to make her reconsider, for the sake of their daughter, but Brigitte is adamant. Her brother, the giebe, reluctantly allows her to join their small corps of knights. While he too would like to keep his sister safe, with so few knights at his disposal, he just can not afford to let a trained knight stay on the side lines. Much to everyone's surprise, an Ordonnanz arrives informing them that reinforcements led by [[Bonifatius
column2: Lord Bonifatius]] will not be dispatched to arrive via highbeast, as they expected, which would have taken around a full day, but will arrive in a matter of minutes via teleportation.

column1: As stated in the message, at exactly fifth bell, a contingent of about fifty knights is teleported in, along with a group of about a dozen scholars, who provide the majority of the mana for the teleportation and [[Sylvester
column2: Aub Ehrenfest]] personally, since this kind of teleporter can apparently only be operated by the archduke himself. After some encouraging words and some final orders, Aub Ehrenfest teleports back to the capital.

column1: The local knights join Bonifatius' force and quickly overwhelm the Ahrensbach attack force, capturing and killing many, and causing the others to scatter and flee. They also manage to capture the [[Divine Instruments#Small Chalices
column2: Small Chalice]] the enemy used to store the mana stolen from the province. The following day, the neighboring province Griebel also comes under attack and having blunted the attack on Illgner, Bonifatius moves on with most of his knights to fight there, leaving only a small contingent to bolster Illgner's defenses. As a parting gift, he and his knights send forth a volley of mana attacks, that cuts down all the trees on the short border between Illgner and Ahrensbach, to create open ground that won't allow the enemy to sneak in unnoticed or have any cover on their approach.

column1: Over the course of the next few days, hostile forces repeatedly attack Illgner, but since they are made up of nobles of so little mana they don't even trigger the alarms of the border barrier, they are easily dispatched by the defenders. The frequency and weakness of these harassing attacks confirms Bonifatius theory, that Illgner was only attacked as a distraction, to draw away forces from the main front line, further to the east.

In the course of the defense, Illgner gets word from a commoner merchant, that he saw suspicious people, likely nobles, book passage on a boat to the capital. Brigitte prompty tries to inform Lady Rozemyne and her guard knights about this, but is unable to send any Ordonnanzes to her former lady, [[Cornelius]] or [[Angelica]]. Only when she sends a message to [[Damuel]] does the spell take flight. After some tense messages, her fears of something bad having happened to Rozemyne are put to rest by her former colleague, who informs her that the Ordonnanzes didn't get through, because Lady Rozemyne and most of her guard knights are in Ahrensbach and that he has passed the message about the boat on to the archducal family.<ref name=""P5V8S2""/>

Staying in Illgner</ref> She is the primary point of contact for [[Lutz]] and [[Gil]] when communicating with [[Giebe Illgner]] and others who live there while teaching and researching papermaking. She serves as servant in Giebe Illgner's mansion.<ref name=""P3V4CSS3""/>

During the stay of the grey priests and Plantin Company personnel, Carya and the priest [[Volk]] fall deeply in love with each other and want to get married, though his position makes that a bit complicated since grey priests are not allowed to marry. They can, however, be sold to nobles.

Due to his love for his people, Giebe Illgner prepares to buy Volk, so he could marry his love, but due to his extensive skillset, his price is far in excess of what the local lord can afford. Rozemyne would like to enable Volk to marry right away, but because of how selling him below his price could effect all other grey priests and shrine maidens under her care, she reluctantly has to insist on the full price. Rozemyne indirectly encourages Volk and Carya to work hard through the winter to make paper to earn the necessary money, though neither the pair nor Giebe Illgner believe it possible to earn so much money in such a short time.<ref name=""P3V5C6"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 3 Volume 5]]. Chapter 6: Illgner's Harvest Festival</ref>

Despite not expecting not to meet their goal in just a single year, Carya and Volk worked hard throughout the winter and following spring and against their expectations manage to earn the sum just like Rozemyne said they could, in even less than an entire year. The following summer, Giebe Illgner is able to buy Volk, when he visits the capital for the [[Starbind Ceremony]].
Two years later, the happily married couple is expecting their first child.<ref name=""P4V1P"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 4 Volume 1]]. Prologue</ref>

Charlotte has silver-blond hair curled into ringlets and indigo eyes. She is an exceptionally cute girl, to the point that [[Rozemyne]] described her as a life-sized doll. She was slightly shorter than Rozemyne during her debut, but had grown taller than her by the time Rozemyne entered the [[Royal Academy]]. She is still on the short side however, and was dwarfed by Rozemyne again after her growth spurt from Anwachs' power.<ref>[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 7]]. Chapter 8: I’m Back</ref>

Charlotte is a caring and good-natured person, with a great dedication to her duties as an archduke candidate. Seeing her elder brother falling so much short of the standards expected for her gave her plenty of self-confidence, without going to her head. While not exactly humble, she is not arrogant or over-confident.
She holds deep gratitude and admiration towards Rozemyne, who saved her and brought a lot of positive changes to Ehrenfest. Unlike Wilfried and Rozemyne, she's much more socially adept.

Charlotte was born as the second child of [[Sylvester]], the seventh [[Aub Ehrenfest]], and his first wife [[Florencia]]. Her older brother [[Wilfried]] was one year older than her, while her younger brother [[Melchior]] was four years younger.
At some point when Charlotte was young, [[Wilfried]] was formally announced to be the next Aub Ehrenfest. While Charlotte retained the position of [[Nobility/Hierarchy#Archduke Candidate
column2: archduke candidate]], she and Melchior were effectively out of the line of succession.

Aub]], Charlotte grew up living in a mansion separate and to the north of the main castle complex until her [[baptism]].<ref name=""P3V1C9"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. column1: After [[Rozemyne]] had been adopted and had managed to turn Wilfried's education around, he heaped lots of praise upon Rozemyne during his visits to his siblings. Charlotte was eagerly looking forward to finally get to meet this amazing new older sister upon moving to the main building.

Charlotte greatly admires [[Rozemyne]] for her various achievements. She felt deeply indebted to Rozemyne for saving her from [[Viscount Joisontak]]'s abduction, and she is always looking for opportunities to repay her.

column1: Christel is the member of a minor noble house, which out of necessity, tries to stay neutral in the ever-shifting faction politics of [[Ehrenfest (Duchy)

In the last few years, they have slowly inched closer to the [[Veronica]] faction, while her influence was at its zenith. They even married Christel's older sister to a man of the Veronica faction. Since the Leisegang faction was so severely suppressed and ostracized, Christel's parents even forbade her from associating with their members. Despite this she became friends with the Leisegang noble Helmina at the [[Royal Academy]], but had to make sure her family wouldn't find out.

When Veronica was imprisoned out of nowhere, the family fell in a panic and started trying to get closer to the Leisegang and Florencia factions to equal out their Veronica faction closeness and secure their neutral status. In these attempts, Christel's friendship with [[Helmina
column2: Lady Helmina]] paid off, allowing Christel and her mother to participate in [[Rozemyne

column1: Initially, Christel's mother only agreed to participating solely for the opportunity to get closer to the [[Leisegang Faction
column3: Florencia]] factions, but once Ferdinand played the love song dedicated to [[Geduldh]], she fainted like many other noble ladies, while Christel just barely avoided falling completely unconscious and being carried out for medical attention by a knight. Together with her daughter, she bought three illustrations of Ferdinand, as well as some [[Culinary#Cookies
column4: cookies]]. Due to each illustration costing five large silver coins, Christel's father was very angry, but his wife managed to calm him by claiming this was to get closer to the Leisegangs and restore their neutral position.<ref name=""SSC1C9"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Short Story Collection 1]]. Christel - A Tea Party with My Older Sister</ref>

column1: In a tea party with her older sister, the two discuss how much [[Sylvester
column2: Aub Ehrenfest]]'s imprisonment of his own mother has thrown all of [[Ehrenfest (Duchy)
column3: Ehrenfest]]'s noble society into chaos. When prompted by her sister, Christel tries to describe the concert - or the harspiel tea party as she calls it - as well as she can, but finds it difficult to describe at times. For reasons she can't quite put into words, Lord Ferdinand's performance caused most of the female listeners to burst out in emotion, which is usually unthinkable for nobles. Christel and her mother even had to resort to using [[feystone]]s to pour their upwelling [[mana]] into. She also shares one of her few remaining tea-leaf flavored cookies with her. Christel herself tries to pace herself to eat only a single cookie per day to make them last as long as she can, usually while reading the program given out at the concert and letting the events replay in her mind.

column1: When showing off the illustrations, Christel's sister asks to be given one of them, but Christel has to refuse, since they belong to their mother and were so costly.

The sisters also discuss Christel's future. To regain their fully neutral status, the house would like her to marry a noble from the Leisegang faction, so Christel plans to get close to one and have him escort her at her graduation. The timing is a bit tight, since she is about to enter her final year at the Royal Academy the coming winter, leaving her only a few months time.
During their tea party, an Ordonnanz from [[Helmina
column2: Lady Helmina]] arrives, inviting Christel and her mother to another tea party organized by [[Elvira
column3: Lady Elvira]], exclusive to all those that have bought illustrations of Ferdinand, which Christel remarks makes the original investment even more worth it and will help to calm their father down. At the tea party, Christel learns that Ferdinand has forbidden Rozemyne from printing any more illustrations of him, much to all the present women's dismay.<ref name=""SSC1C9""/>

Their meeting was somewhat overshadowed by the collapse of the [[Previous Count Leisegang]] and an incident with one of Rozemyne's retainers, which caused Rozemyne to excuse herself as soon as social norms allowed, preventing any interactions between Giebe Leisegang and her beyond greetings and the teaching of the compression<ref name=""P4V3C16""/>.

column1: In the spring following Rozemyne's second year at the [[Royal Academy]], she and her adopted siblings visit [[Leisegang]] for [[Spring Prayer]] and establishing the printing industry. When drawing up the contracts, the merchant [[Benno]] of the [[Plantin Company]] voices concerns on whether the province will be able to recuperate their considerable investments, considering they intend to only do printing as winter handiwork, while concentrating their workforces on their main focus of agriculture during the rest of the year. Count Leisegang assured that such concerns are unnecessary, and he has no intention of canceling their contracts, regardless of the financial returns, since income is not the only concern for him in regards to printing.

Once the business talk is over and the merchants have been dismissed, the discussions turn toward the future of the duchy. Rozemyne and Wilfried manage to convince the Giebe that Rozemyne is absolutely unwilling to ever become Aub and that despite appearances [[Wilfried]] is actually better suited to be the next archduke than she would ever be. Count Leisegang accepts this and is heartened by Wilfried's assurances that he will not repeat his forebearer's mistakes, but is very concerned about how his grandfather will take this, when getting the information directly from Rozemyne herself, rather than through messengers<ref name=""P4V8C9""/>.

column1: '''Deid''' (ディード ''Diido'') is one of [[Myne]]'s neighbours. He is the father of [[Lutz]]. He works as construction worker.
Deid is a tall man and strong due to his profession.

In private matters, Deid is for the most part a very reserved and stoic person and has trouble showing or explaining his feelings. He barely ever talks about personal matters, even to the point of letting problems pile up in the absence of talking things out. He has a very loud voice and is quick to shout when something gets under his skin. When he has reasons to be grateful to others, he will usually not say anything and just help them in some way to let his actions speak for him.

When Lutz ran away from home, Deid was summoned to the temple with [[Karla]] to discuss Lutz's issues. He is of the opinion that Lutz behaves like a baby. After solving Lutz's issue, they make up and leave the temple together.

Later when he learns from Lutz by chance that Myne's family is helping with the orphanage's winter preparation, he decides to help as well in the pig butchering, likely to show his thanks for the High Priest's help in solving their family issue.
