column1: '''Detlinde''' (ディートリンデ, ''Diitorinde'') was an [[Nobility/Hierarchy#Archduke Candidate
column2: archduke candidate]] of [[Ahrensbach]], being the daughter of [[Gieselfried]] and [[Georgine]]. After the death of her father, she was temporarily appointed as the successor of Aub Ahrensbach.

column1: As she participated and aided the [[Lanzenave]] invasion, she was stripped of the position, imprisoned, and her schtappe was permanently destroyed.<ref name=""P5V12C11""/>

Detlinde has dark green eyes and beautiful blonde hair.<ref name=""P4V1C9"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 1]]. Chapter 9: The Advancement Ceremony and Fellowship Gatherings</ref> She takes after her mother, [[Georgine]], and is said to look even more like her grandmother, [[Veronica]].<ref name=""P4V3C3"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 3]]. Chapter 3: Winter Socializing</ref>

column2: archduke candidate]] of a greater duchy, Detlinde is used to getting what she wants. This makes her extremely narcissistic and self-centered, thinking that the world revolves around her. She often makes unreasonable demands to get what she wants, blatantly disregarding the atmosphere and people around her.<ref name=""P4V3C11"" /> When things aren't going her way, she starts throwing tantrums and lashes out against her retainers.<ref name=""P5V3E"" />

column1: Detlinde is warm to those she likes, but contemptuous to those she sees as inferior to her.<ref name=""P4V1C10"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 1]]. Chapter 20: Dedication Whirl</ref> She uses backhanded compliments and false concern to insult those she dislikes, and often plays the victim in social situations. However, her ploys are usually more convincing to boys than other girls.<ref name=""P4V3C11"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 3]]. Chapter 11: The Tea Party for All Duchies</ref>

Detlinde is quite prone to throwing out veiled or even open insults to others without appearing to consider the consequences of her words, even when such unkind words will clearly place her in a worse position.<ref name=""P4V8C20"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 8]]. Chapter 20: Ferdinand’s Estate</ref> She is also extremely cruel towards people who oppose her, such that she gleefully conspired with [[Lanzenave
column2: Lanzenavians]] to slaughter and abduct nobles of [[Letizia]]'s faction.<ref>''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 7]]. Epilogue</ref>

column1: Despite all her unnoble-like traits, Detlinde is obsessively protective of her chastity before marriage, to the extent that she was not willing to share the same building as [[Leonzio]], whom she recognized as her lover.<ref>''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 10]]. Prologue</ref>
Detlinde was born as the youngest daughter of [[Gieselfried
column2: Aub Ahrensbach]] and [[Georgine]], his third wife. When his first wife died, Georgine became the new first wife. Because her mother is the older sister of [[Sylvester]], Detlinde is also a cousin to [[Wilfried]] and his siblings (as well as [[Rudiger]] from [[Frenbeltag]]).

column1: She has several older sisters who are all married, including [[Alstede]] who was married to her half-brother Blasius. Her only brother Wolfram died shortly after the purges following the [[Civil War
column2: civil war]]. While she has a claim on the title of Aub, her niece [[Letizia]] has already been selected as the successor.<ref name=""P4V4E"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 4]]. Epilogue</ref>

column1: Throughout her entire childhood, Detlinde barely had any contact with her father. On the few times they met, Detlinde can only remember him chastising her with a disgusted look on his face without doting on her even once.

Likewise, she doesn't seem to feel particularly close to her mother either, who not once in Detlinde's life followed any of her daughter's suggestions and who didn't seem to care when Detlinde was sick. Even when ill, Detlinde had to keep working and studying.<ref name=""P4V8E"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 8]]. Epilogue</ref>
*'''[[Fatiehe]]''' - A former [[Werkestock]] noble working as Detlinde's attendant as a way to repay her lady's [[Georgine
column2: mother]] for her perceived kindness.<ref name=""P5V3E"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 3]]. Epilogue</ref>

Professor Solange]] remarked that a ""young lady from Ahrensbach"" inquired rather insistently how to became the new master of the magic tools. While it is not confirmed, it is strongly implied to be Detlinde, planning to take the shumils away from Rozemyne.<ref name=""P4V2C10"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 2]]. Chapter 10: The Prince's Summons</ref>

column1: *Both [[Wilfried]] and [[Charlotte]] remarked that Detlinde strongly resembled [[Veronica]], but their reasons are entirely different.

*Her name is a German name, usually spelled as ""Dietlinde"" or ""Dietlind"". Detlinde was chosen in official translations to prevent the audience from associating her name with the English word ""diet"" and mispronounce it.

**""Dietlinde"" is derived from ""thiot"" (people) and ""lind"" (soft, tender) in Old High German, which is ironic considering the fact that she acts like a bully who couldn't care less about people beneath her.
'''Dhorme''' is a traveling merchant, mostly journeying between [[Ehrenfest (Duchy)
column2: Ehrenfest]] and [[Frenbeltag]] and an old friend of [[Otto]].<ref name=""SSC2C7"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Short Story Collection 2]]. Chapter 7: Otto — Winter Preparations and a Traveling Merchant’s Request</ref>

column1: Back in his days as a traveling merchant, Otto and Dhorme became friends and helped each other out. When Otto managed to gain [[Corinna]]'s hand, Otto asked him, to tell his parents about how he managed to marry his new wife and what he did with the money he earned, which Dhorme did. Even after the marriage, Otto and Dhorme met in Ebb's bar to drink and chat. When the [[Plantin Company]] split from the [[Gilberta Company]] and Otto took up a position in his wife's company, he mostly stopped going to his old haunts.<ref name=""SSC2C7""/>
In the autumn after the reconstruction of [[City_of_Ehrenfest#Lower_City
column2: Ehrenfest's lower city]], Otto is contacted by Dhorme and the two meet at Ebb's bar, with Otto donning his old, ""poor people's clothes"" for the first time in a while. The first chat a little about the massive changes the city has gone through recently, before getting to the actual point of their meeting. Dhorne is in a bit of a bind, since the daughter of the mayor, who agreed to let him stay with them in the winter, wanted him to procure a [[Inventions#Hair Ornament
column3: hairpin]] in red, but he was unable to find a fitting one in any of Ehrenfest's stores. Otto informs him that this is the result of other duchies buying up essentially the whole stock of hairpins in the summer, and all the craftswomen being busy dealing with the backlog this caused to build up.

column1: Usually Otto would have to turn down the request, since every single craftwoman of every single story is too busy, but since the request comes from a friend and due to the hardships of a traveling merchant, Dhorme's very life might depend on his ability to stay on good terms with the mayor, Otto agrees to see if he can help by contacting [[Effa]], who is the only person Otto knows of, who has the ability to make a hairpin of sufficient quality, without being caught up in the post-summer sale time crunch, albeit only for a hefty urgency fee.
Thankfully for Dhorme, Effa is able to make the time and delivers a finished hairpin of sufficient quality just two days later.<ref name=""SSC2C7""/>
'''Dimo''' (ディモ, ''Dimo'') is a [[commoner]] who works as a [[Leherl
column3: Ingo's]] carpentry workshop.<ref name=""P3V3S2"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 3 Volume 3]]. The High Bishop's Exclusive Business</ref>

column1: Dimo first comes into indirect contact with Myne, when the first prototype of the [[Printing#Printing_Press
column2: printing press]], albeit they are not introduced to each other.

column1: Dimo and his fellow [[leherl]] [[Linus]] are enthusiastic to hear that their workshop was chosen to outfit the [[Hasse]] monastery with furnishings, but dismayed when [[Ingo]] explains that the order came through the Carpentry Guild, not directly from [[Rozemyne]].<ref name=""P3V3S2""/>

Due to having been involved with printing presses from the very start, Dimo is second only to Ingo himself when it comes to experience with them. For this reason Dimo is chosen to represent the workshop, in place of his foreman Ingo in the province of [[Kirnberger]].

That by itself however is not enough to repair Ferdinand's thread, so Dregarnuhr and Wendtuchte send Rozemyne back into the past, to the moment, when Ferdinand's thread was severed. Losing his beloved wife and unborn child hit Eckhart so hard, that he wanted to commit suicide, but due to being name-sworn, his life was not his own to end. Ferdinand ordered Eckhart to live for his wife's sake and to find something to fill the void left by her passing. With Heidemarie being fanatically devoted to Ferdinand and the two of them having sworn they would serve him as a married couple, Eckhart made it his entire live's purpose to live for Ferdinand, for both his own and Heidemarie's sake.<ref name=""P5V8P"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. Despite despising Veroncia as well, his father still didn't want this to come to pass and when he learned of Eckhart's plans intervened by keeping him busy with paperwork for the knight's order and training of new recruits, while restricting him to their estate in his free time, thus the offer went to Lamprecht who took up the position to protect their family.<ref name=""SSC1C10"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. A good-natured and hard-working woman, Effa is a loving wife to [[Gunther]] and a supportive mother to [[Tuuli]], [[Myne]] and [[Kamil]]. She is respected by her neighbors in the lower city as a skilled textile worker and seamstress.

Effa has a lot in common with her oldest daughter, Tuuli. Both are creative designers, who have a knack for working with thread and fabric, and both are kind, considerate, and practical by nature. While Effa is generally even-tempered, she sometimes becomes exasperated at Myne and Gunther’s eccentricities. She also dislikes when people are wasteful.

Like the rest of her family, Effa is deeply protective of her loved ones. Although Myne was frequently bedridden with illness and often threw tantrums, Effa cared for her tirelessly and was overjoyed when her condition improved. Later, she risked execution by defying a noble to protect Myne.

Effa is the daughter of a former commander of the gate in the [[city of Ehrenfest]]. Through her father, she met her future husband [[Gunther]], who was a apprentice soldier under her father's command. Gunther pursued her with enthusiasm, and eventually won her consent and the blessing of her father for the marriage.

The two would later raise three children: her oldest daughter, [[Tuuli]], her second daughter, Myne, and her youngest son [[Kamil]]. Effa also had two miscarriages, and their first son died shortly after he was born.

Effa works at the Heuss Workshop<ref name=""P4V5S4"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 5]]. The Road to Exclusive Business</ref> as a dyer. She is also an excellent seamstress, although she does not sew for a living. By commoner standards, which place a high value on health, strength, and household skills, she is considered a “beauty”. In addition to her work, Effa spent a lot of time caring for Myne, who was a very sickly child.

*'''Sewing.''' Effa is a very good seamstress. Her self-made outfits like Tuuli's baptism dress were the envy of the neighborhood. She also picked up crocheting from Myne from just watching her for a short time.

*Effa admires Benno's younger sister, [[Corinna]], for her ability as a seamstress. Corinna is an influential member of the seamstress guild, so Effa becomes very flustered when Corinna asks to see her sewing work on Myne's baptismal dress.

*Many of the neighborhood women still can't believe Effa agreed to marry Gunther. Effa was considered a very desirable marriage candidate with many options, while Gunther was considered very goofy and a dreamer.

*The line that made Effa fully fall in love with Gunther was: ""I became a soldier because I genuinely want to protect this city and my family. You didn't laugh at that, Effa, and I love you for it. I want you by my side.""<ref name=""P1V2S2"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 1 Volume 2]]. Gossiping by the Well</ref>

column1: Ella has a matter-of-fact, cheerful personality. In spite of her difficult circumstances, she looks for constructive and practical ways to improve her future. An ambitious chef, Ella loves her job and works hard to improve her cooking skills.

Ella's father died when she was young, and her mother was forced to become a prostitute to make ends meet. Growing up, Ella found work as an apprentice chef in her uncle's night-time bar. However, her uncle was a cruel, callous man who hired out his own daughter, Lea, to serve as a ""waitress"" and visit paying male clients in their rooms.

Ella believed that the same thing would happen to her when she came of age, so she was eager to find anywhere else to work -- especially if she could find work as a chef. When her uncle sent her to ask for an extension on the bar's taxes from the Eatery Guild, she encountered [[Benno]] talking about how hard it was to find a chef who was willing to work in the temple.

While Ella had heard unsavory rumors about the temple, she reasoned that it couldn't possibly be worse than working for her uncle. She persuaded Benno to let her take the job. Her uncle protested, but her mother supported her, happy to see that her daughter was finding a new path through life.  Ella signed a contract with the [[Gilberta Company]] at the Eatery Guild. That was also where she met Hugo for the first time.<ref name=""P2V2S2"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 2 Volume 2]]. Apprentice Chef in the Temple</ref>
*Her hands are covered with calluses due to her passion for cooking.<ref name=""P2V2S2""/>

*When Myne first met Ella, Myne thought she was 10.<ref name=""P2V1C10"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 2 Volume 1]]. *When Ella came of age, Rozemyne gave her a portable meat grinder as a gift, which was one of her new inventions. column1: '''Elvira''' (エルヴィーラ, ''Eruviira'') is [[Rozemyne]]'s noble mother. She is the first wife of [[Karstedt]] and the mother of [[Eckhart]], [[Lamprecht]], and [[Cornelius]]. She is also the grandmother to [[Siegrecht]].

column2: archnoble]], Elvira took responsibility for introducing [[Rozemyne]] to noblewomen’s society.<ref name=""P3V1P"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 1]]. Prologue</ref> She is the leader of the [[Florencia]] [[Florencia Faction

column4: Ehrenfest]].<ref name=""P4V3C2"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 3]]. Chapter 2: Mother and Printing in Haldenzel</ref>

column1: Elvira has dark green hair gathered up in complex bundles, has almost black eyes<ref name=""FB1CDS"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Fanbook
column2: Fanbook1]]. Character Design Sheets</ref> and she wears elaborate clothing covered in embroidery of all colors. According to [[Rozemyne]], she seems to be in her mid-thirties. She has a dignified aura even when standing still, and her every gesture “exudes grace and refinement”.<ref name=""P3V1C1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 1]]. Chapter 1: Examination Results and the Noble’s Quarter</ref>

column1: Elvira is fashionable, intelligent, and socially adept. Rozemyne describes her as a role model: someone who “secures that which benefits her, pays back into society, receives praise from all around her, and is unrelenting when it comes to her hobbies”.<ref name=""P4V1C12"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 1]]. Chapter 12: History, Geography, and Music</ref>

column2: Ehrenfest]], Elvira loyally supported those who faced persecution, including [[Ferdinand]] and [[Florencia]].<ref name=""P4V3C2""/> She has so much trust in Ferdinand that she was willing to baptize Rozemyne as her daughter on his request.<ref name=""P3V1P""/> True to her promise, she treats Rozemyne with as much support and affection as her blood-related children.
Veronica’s]] half-sister, Elvira faced political persecution and harassment throughout her life. She attended the [[Royal Academy]] and graduated from the [[Scholar
column3: scholar's]] course, and was subsequently married to [[Karstedt]] in hopes that it would offer her protection from Veronica's abuse.

column1: However, she worked methodically to gather allies among the other noblewomen who suffered at Veronica’s hands and prepared a counter-faction. When [[Sylvester]] married his first wife, [[Florencia]], she was also targeted by Veronica and eventually joined Elvira’s faction. The name of the faction changed accordingly to the Florencia faction, despite Elvira still being the leader.<ref name=""P4V3C2"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 3]]. Chapter 2: Mother and Printing in Haldenzel</ref>
Elvira’s husband [[Karstedt]] also married a second wife, [[Trudeliede]], and a third wife, [[Rozemary]]. However, Rozemary’s [[Nobility/Hierarchy#Mednoble
column2: mednoble]] family began making unreasonable demands of the family, and Trudeliede took to bullying Rozemary in turn. The situation spiraled into a fierce familial conflict.

column1: Karstedt failed to view the situation objectively and sided solely with Rozemary, forcing Elvira to side with Trudeliede in an attempt to balance the conflict. Their constant fighting exacerbated Rozemary's already poor health and eventually led to her death. Even years later, Elvira and Karstedt’s relationship remains strained as a consequence.

In spite of her misgivings, Elvira is willing to accept Rozemyne into the family and baptize her as her own child, mainly because she is asked to help as a personal request from [[Ferdinand]].<ref name=""P3V1P"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 1]]. Prologue</ref>

*'''[[Muriella]]''' - Formerly the retainer and name-sworn of [[Rozemyne]], she recently got permission to give her name to her idol Elvira.<ref name=""P5V4C11"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 4]]. Chapter 11: Reobtaining Divine Protections</ref> Serves Elvira in Ehrenfest, but is lent to Rozemyne at the Royal Academy.<ref name=""P5V7C2"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 6]]. Chapter 2: The Winter Playroom and Another New Term</ref>

*'''Politics:''' Elvira is talented at political maneuvering and has a wide network of informants and allies. She is also good at gathering  sensitive information due to her training as a [[scholar]].

*'''Writing:''' In her free time, Elvira enjoys writing romance novels. She has a voracious appetite for new stories and doesn’t hesitate to take inspiration from the personal lives of her family and friends. Her [[Printing#Storybook
column2: romance stories]] are very popular among Ehrenfest's noblewomen.

'''Erwaermen''' (エアヴェルミーン, ''Airvermeen'') is the former God of Binding and the one [[Schwartz and Weiss]] refer to as ''Gramps''.<ref name=""P5V7C6"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 7]]. Chapter 6: Meeting Gramps</ref>
While taking on a Human-like appearance Erwaermen looks like a tall and slender man in his thirties, except that his skin has the colour and texture of ivory.<ref name=""P5V7C6""/>

When [[Ewigeliebe]] fell in love with the Goddes of Earth, Erwaermen assisted him in his proposal to [[Geduldh]] and acquiring the [[God of Darkness]]' permission to marry her. But soon after the happy wedding, Ewigeliebe changed. Twisted by his fear of losing his wife, he froze her in ice to keep her only for himself and jealously guarded her.

Confronted with how Ewigeliebe treated his new wife and her subordinates, Erwaermen was outraged. He gathered Geduldh's subordinate goddesses and guided them to [[Flutrane]], determined to save their mistress. In the guilt and shame of his role in binding the threads that led to Geduldh's suffering, Erwaermen retired from his position as god and passed both his duties and his powers to [[Gods and Subordinate Gods
column2: Liebeskhilfe]].<ref name=""P5V2C9"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 2]]. Chapter 9: Tea Parties and Negotiations</ref>

column1: It isn't clear how it ended up like this, but today Erwaermen is linked to the Foundation of [[Yurgenschmidt]]. Should the Foundation ever run dry, the former god will disappear along with it and the kingdom.<ref name=""P5V11P"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 11]]. Prologue</ref> Since the beginning of the country, Erwaermen stays in the [[Royal Academy#Garden of Beginnings
column2: Garden of Beginnings]], taking the shape of a tree made from ivory most of the time. He is able to take on his old, albeit still retaining the colour and texture of ivory, when communicating with Zent Candidates, who enter the Garden of Beginnings. This is primarily to grant Zent Candidates, who have already fulfilled the necessary steps, [[Mestionora]]'s Wisdom, filling their [[Grutrissheit]].

column1: It was Erwaermen who invented [[Magic Tools#Ivory Buildings
column2: Ivory Buildings]], for the purpose of providing mana-wielders with a place to live, which shields them from Ewigeliebe's detection, who would otherwise steal their mana, which would result in their deathes.<ref name=""FB7QA"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Fanbook 7]]. Q&A with Miya Kazuki</ref>

column1:
In the past, when there was enough mana available for Erwaermen to take on his Human-like shape at will, he would at times do so to converse with the people who came to the Garden of Beginnings, be they omni-elemental students obtaining their divine will, zent candidates being granted Mestionora's Wisdom or royals seeking to consult the gods on important decisions. This more regular contact allowed past zent candidates and royals to have a much closer and mutually respectful relationship with the former god than any person in modern days.
The first person to call Erwärmen ""gramps"" was the zent candidate Rauchelstra.
At some point in the history of [[Yurgenschmidt]], a princess creates the shumil-like magic tools [[Schwartz and Weiss]] to both help the librarians of of the [[Royal Academy/Library
column2: Royal Academy Library]] and aid Zent candidates on their path to obtain the Grutrissheit, in a slightly different way, that is accessible only to member of the royal family. With Erwaermen being their spiritual predecessor, the princess made the two shumil refer to Erwaermen as ""Gramps."" Erwaermen himself seems to have warm and nostalgic feelings toward being called by this name.

column1: During his time in the [[Royal Academy]], [[Ferdinand]] - or Quinta, as he is known to Erwaermen due to this being his true name - rather than properly praying and donating mana through proper rituals and ceremonies, forecully charged the magic circle that appeared after praying at the [[Royal Academy#Large Shrines
column2: Large Shrines]] with mana and forced his way through the opening above the Garden of Beginnings. Despite this exceptionally rude behaviour, Erwaermen still began the process of loading Mestionora's Wisdom into the boy's mind, but [[Ferdinand]] refused the knowledge, which broke off the process after only about 30 to 40 percent was put into his mind, much to the chagrin of Erwaermen.<ref name=""P5V7C6"" />

column1: Ten years later, [[Rozemyne]] - during her fourth year at the [[Royal Academy]] - fulfills the prerequisites to obtain the Grutrissheit and is summoned to the Garden of Beginnings, the proper route. Since he is unable to see the physical world and only perceives it through mana, Erwaermen is convinced that Ferdinand returned to get the remaining knowledge, rather than a new person. The former god appears still a bit sore about the mortal's previous misbehaviour, but is glad that this time 'he' has come the proper way and is showing the appropriate manners. Erwaermen is surprised that ""Quinta's"" vessel had regressed to a smaller size, to the point were it could no longer contain ""everything"" and wonders of he suffers from some kind of curse. He calls upon Anwachs for help, which the God of Growth provides, growing Rozemyne to a state a person her age should have. Apparently pleased with her vessel now once again having the necessary size, he makes the mortal go through the process of obtaining Mestionora's Wisdom and transfers the remaining 60 to 70 percent of it, into their mind. Due to his forceful and commanding presence, Rozemyne temporarily forgoes any questions and protestations and follows the former god's instructions, without resistence.<ref name=""P5V7C6"" />

Only after the process is finishes, does she speak up and state that she is not the same person who came here ten years ago. This initially confuses Erwaermen, sicne their mana is nearly identical, but after some back and froth, in which Rozemyne reveals that she was once dyed by Quinta and realizing that this dying stuck to this day, on account of Rozemyne being a child with the Mark of Ewigeliebe, she is able to convince the former god of the truth of her statement. This means that now the Wisdom of Mestionora is split between them. He commands Rozemyne to gain the parts that she is missing, by killing Ferdinand and absorbing his feystone, before going back to being a silent, inanimate statue of a tree.<ref name=""P5V7C7"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 7]]. Chapter 7: The Book of Mestionora</ref>

column1: '''Ewigeliebe''' (エーヴィリーベ, ''Eeviriibe''), the '''God of Life''' (命の神, ''Inochi no Kami''), is one of the [[Gods and Subordinate Gods#Eternal Five
He presides over winter and is the source of life in the world. His [[Divine Instruments
column3: sword]],<ref name=""P2V3Ch4""> [[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 2 Volume 3]]. Chapter 4: Winter Hibernation and Handiwork.</ref> and his [[Divine Colour
column4: divine color]] is white, which symbolizes snow and ice.

column1: When the [[God of Darkness]] married the [[Goddess of Light]], they had four children. In order, they were [[Flutrane]], the Goddess of Water; [[Leidenschaft]], God of Fire; [[Schutzaria]], Goddess of Wind; and [[Geduldh]], the Goddess of Earth.

Ewigeliebe, the God of Life, fell in love with Geduldh. The God of Darkness gave the two permission to marry, hoping they would fill the world with new life. But Ewigeliebe's jealous love - edged on even more by the [[Gods and Subordinate Gods#Caocipher
column2: Goddess of Chaos]]<ref name=""P2V3C4"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 2 Volume 3]]. Chapter 4: Winter Hibernation and Handiwork</ref> - consumed him, and he froze Geduldh in ice, so their child could never be born.

column1: The world fell into winter, and The Goddess of Light began to worry about her daughter. She found Geduldh trapped and melted the ice with her rays of sunlight, and Flutrane caused the water to flood away, bringing spring to the world. Geduldh's other siblings, Leidenschaft and Schutzaria, fought to protect her from Ewigeliebe, bringing summer and autumn.

However, they could not fully defeat Ewigeliebe without preventing all new life from being born. Each year at the end of autumn, the God of Life once again traps Geduldh in ice, and her siblings must fight to free her in spring.

In noble euphemisms, Ewigeliebe is usually referenced to mean ""one who passionately loves or yearns for another,""<ref name=""P3V4S2"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 3 Volume 4]]. Damuel's Proposal</ref> often in a jealous or possessive way.
The phrase ""Ewigeliebe in the spring"" is used an insult to call someone useless.<ref name=""P4V8C20"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 4 Volume 8]]. Chapter 20: Ferdinand's Estate</ref>

The Royal Academy contains a shrine dedicated to the Ewigeliebe and him twelve subordinates, which grants a tablet, and a special word required to obtain the [[Grutrissheit]], after one has prayed and dedicated enough mana to him. He also guards the equivalent shrine to Geduldh, whose doors will only open with his approval. The word Rozemyne was granted was Neigunsch.<ref name=""P5V5C8"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 5 Volume 5]]. Chapter 8: Circling the Shrines</ref>
Compared to the other [[Gods and Subordinate Gods#Eternal Five
column2: primary and subordinate Gods]], Ewigeliebe is not as often invoked in [[Religious Ceremonies]] and [[Blessing
column3: blessings]]. One problem is the strained relationship between the Geduldh's siblings and Ewigeliebe, which results in the failure of any spell or blessings, were life mana is combined with water, fire or wind. Only by adding earth as a mediator, can life be linked with any other kind of mana, as is demonstrated by the yearly [[Dedication Ritual]] or the blessing located at the back of the High Bishop's bible.<ref name=""P4VC9C14"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 4 Volume 9]]. Chapter 14: Separation</ref>

column1: Praying to Ewigeliebe while wielding his sword will summon subordinates of the [[Lord of Winter]]. This drains almost all the wielder's mana, and weakens Schutzaria's Shield when nearby.<ref name=""P5V2C12"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 5 Volume 2]]. Chapter 12: Bride-Taking Ditter</ref>

Ewigeliebe has twelve subordinate gods, including Beischmacht the God of Sex, Cuococalura the God of Cooking, Dauerleben the God of Longevity, Schneeahst the God of Ice and Blizzards, and Schlaftraum the God of Dreams.
*His name is most likely derived from the German words ""ewige"" and ""liebe"" which translate to ""eternal love"".
*When [[Myne]] adapted her playing cards to [[Yurgenschmidt]], Ewigeliebe, represented by the sword, was used in place of the Jack.<ref name=""P2V3Ch4""/>

column1: Fatiehe was born in the duchy of [[Werkestock]]. She was still a child when the [[Civil War
column2: civil war]] broke out and saw her home defeated. In the aftermath, Werkestock was dissolved and the northern part in which Fatiehe lived was placed under [[Ahrensbach]]'s management.<ref name=""P5V3E""/>

column1: When she was old enough to participate in the general politicking and factions of the nobility, she joined [[Georgine]]'s faction and eventually managed to land the position of attendant to [[Detlinde]]. This job is both a blessing and curse for her. A blessing since she greatly admires Georgine and her willingness to help the disrespected former [[Werkestock]] nobles. For Fatiehe, this is a way to repay her perceived kindness. The position is also a curse since Detlinde is not a pleasant person at times and causes trouble for everyone around her with constant antics and abrasive personality. Her lady's troubling tendency to blunder time and again often without even realizing she messed something up also had a negative effect on her apprentice attendants' grades, since certain failings of the master negatively reflects on their attendants at the Royal Academy.<ref name=""P5V3E""/>

Fatiehe envies her younger fellow apprentices like [[Martina]] who get to experience at least one semester at the royal academy without Detlinde present, while she had the misfortune to graduate at the same time as their lady. She is already engaged and will marry into another duchy come next Spring, which in turn makes Martina envious of her, since Martina being one of Detlinde's favorites is unlikely to ever be able to leave her lady's service.<ref name=""P5V3E""/>

column1: Ferdinand has light gold eyes and pale blue hair that falls to his shoulders. He is tall and has a slender build. Generally, his face reveals little emotion.<ref name=""P1V3C20"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 1 Volume 3]]. Chapter 20: Rejection and Persuasion</ref> In noblewomen's society, Ferdinand is considered very attractive.<ref name=""P3V1C2"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 1]]. Chapter 2: Preparing for the Baptism Ceremony</ref>

When [[Myne]] first encounters him, she thinks he looks around the same age as [[Benno]], although he is actually about ten years younger. His worn appearance is primarily due to overwork, and he tends to look closer to his real age when he has more time to relax.<ref name=""FB2QA"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Fanbook 2]]. Q&A with Miya Kazuki</ref>

Ferdinand grew in height rapidly when staying at the [[Royal Academy]], and eventually surpassed [[Sylvester]] in height upon his coming-of-age.<ref name=""FB6QA>''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]].'' [[Fanbook 6]]. Q&A with Miya Kazuki</ref>

As Ferdinand often says himself, he does not have a naturally “likeable” personality. He treats most people coldly, unless he has reason to believe they are valuable to him, and only bothers with politeness when it benefits him.<ref name=""P4V2C1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 2]]. Chapter 1: Meeting for the Tea Party</ref> As an opponent, Ferdinand is calculating and ruthless. He exploits every weakness without restraint to secure the best possible result for himself.<ref name=""P4V2C9"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 2]]. Chapter 9: Treasure-Stealing Ditter</ref> Due to the abuse he suffered at the hands of [[Veronica]], he is especially distrustful, cold, and impatient with women.<ref name=""P3V1P"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 1]]. Prologue</ref>

However, Ferdinand is deeply loyal and will go to great lengths to protect and support the few people he cares about. Despite his often solitary life, he values personal relationships highly, and he admits to Myne that he envies the unconditional love and support she receives from her family.<ref name=""P1V3C24"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 1 Volume 3]]. Chapter 24: Confrontation</ref> Due to his difficult upbringing, Ferdinand rarely expresses his emotions outwardly. When he does show kindness or concern, he tends to do it in a roundabout and hard-to-understand manner.<ref name=""P4V3C18"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 3]]. Chapter 18: The Book Fair and the Follow-Up Meeting</ref> He also is good at hiding discomfort and pain: the more upset he is, the brighter he smiles.

An exceptionally competent and hardworking person, Ferdinand values those same qualities in others. However, he has no patience for those who cannot meet his standards. [[Myne]] reflects that he often tries to do everything himself rather than rely on others. Ferdinand also loves research and often forgets to eat or sleep when he’s studying a fascinating topic.<ref name=""P4V3C1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 3]]. Chapter 1: The Dedication Ritual and Returning to the Castle</ref>

Ferdinand is described as a cold-blooded pragmatist, who cares about almost nothing but efficiency. Ironically, his extreme pragmatism can lead to unnecessary delays and difficulties: When he is reluctant to ""waste time"" teaching noble etiquette to Ehrenfest commoners, [[Rozemyne]] points out that punishing commoners for breach of etiquette is much more wasteful and time-consuming.<ref name=""P3V3C17"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 3]]. Chapter 17: The Spring Ingredient and Discussing Spring Prayer</ref>
Ferdinand's true origins are known to extremely few people. He was born under the name ""Quinta"" in the [[Royal Academy#Adalgisa Villa
column2: Adalgisa Villa]] in the [[Sovereignty]] as the son of Adelbert and [[Seradina]].<ref name=""FB2FamilyTree"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Fanbook 2]]. ""Noble Family Tree"" Illustration</ref> Seradina served as the ""Flower of House Loweleier,""<ref name=""P5V9E"" /> where her role was to produce children with a high level of [[mana]]. However for Ferdinand, he was conceived with the intention of producing a balanced all-attributes feystone.<ref name=""P5V7C7"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 7]]. Chapter 7: The Book of Mestionora</ref>

column1: Ferdinand was able to escape the villa and find safety in [[Ehrenfest (Duchy)
column2: Ehrenfest]] under the care of [[Adelbert]] and his half-sister [[Irmhilde]].<ref>[[Part 5 Volume 12]] chapter - Memories</ref> The circumstances surrounding this event are unclear even to nobles (like [[Raublut]]) who were closely involved at the time, but Aub Ehrenfest attributed it to ""the guidance of the Goddess of Time."" As Yurgenschmidt still needed to provide a feystone to Lanzenave, Ferdinand's mother Seradina was executed and turned into a feystone in his place.<ref name=""P5V9E"" />

column1: When Ferdinand first came to Ehrenfest, he was accompanied by Imrhilde. She lived with him as a caregiver and maternal figure in her estate before his baptism. Irmhilde was planned to become Ferdinand's baptismal mother, but she died before either her marriage or his baptism could take place.<ref name=""P5V4C10"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 4]]. Chapter 10: Preparing the Ritual</ref>

Because Veronica refused to adopt Ferdinand or have him baptized as her child, he was introduced to noble society only as the son of Aub Ehrenfest and a mistress.<ref name=""P4V8C14"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 8]]. Chapter 14: Decisions</ref> Ferdinand began living in the archduke's castle after his baptism. When he later returned to the villa where he was raised, Irmhilde was gone. Ferdinand assumed that Veronica had eliminated her.<ref name=""P5V4C10"" />

Growing up, Ferdinand was routinely harassed and ostracized by his stepmother, who viewed him as a threat and rival to her own son and preferred heir, [[Sylvester]]. She tormented him continually, assigning him untrustworthy retainers and having his meals poisoned or tampered with.<ref name=""P4V9C3"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 9]]. Chapter 3: The Farewell Supper</ref> By contrast, Sylvester was eager to have a good relationship with his new half-brother.<ref name=""P4V9S1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 9]]. Irreplaceable</ref>

At age ten, Ferdinand enrolled in the [[Royal Academy]], where he excelled in his studies. After [[Justus]] told him it was possible to enroll in multiple courses, he decided to simultaneously take the [[scholar]] course, the [[knight]] course, and the archduke candidate course. Unlike most students, he viewed the Royal Academy as a respite from his difficult life in Ehrenfest and stayed there year-round, only returning home when summoned.
During his school years, Ferdinand studied as a disciple of [[Hirschur
column2: Professor Hirschur]], an avid researcher of magic tools. He also became widely known among the other students for his skill in [[Ditter
column3: treasure-stealing ditter]] and [[harspiel]], and routinely received the top grades in his class.<ref name=""P4V2C1"" /> Fellow students like [[Henrik]] and [[Eckhart]] were immensely impressed by his achievements, and [[Heisshitze]] of [[Dunkelfelger]] came to view him as a rival.

column1: At some point in his time at the Royal Academy, Ferdinand fulfilled most of the trials to become a Zent candidate and then used mana to brute-force his way into the Garden of Beginnings and reach [[Erwaermen]]. Although the god disapproved of his unconventional methods, Ferdinand was qualified to obtain the [[Grutrissheit#True Book of Mestionora
column2: Book of Mestionora]] and began absorbing the knowledge it contained. However, he broke off the transfer process when his Book of Mestionora was only about a third complete.<ref name=""P5V7C7"" />

column1: Ferdinand also accepted [[Justus]], [[Eckhart]] and [[Lasfam]] as his retainers after joining the Royal Academy. However, his deep-seated distrust of others meant that he was unwilling to rely on them until they [[Nobility#Name-Swearing
column2: gave him their names]] in a show of unwavering loyalty. Eckhart's wife [[Heidemarie]] also served as his retainer, but was killed by poisoning shortly after her marriage. After graduating from the Royal Academy, Ferdinand briefly served with the Ehrenfest [[Knight's Order]], where he left a lasting impression on the apprentice knight [[Damuel]].

column1: Ferdinand briefly served as the Ehrenfest's knight commander, for roughly half a year, before becoming a priest.<ref name=""FB6QA>''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]].'' [[Fanbook 6]]. Q&A with Miya Kazuki</ref>

As the archduke's health worsened, so did Veronica's paranoia; she began persecuting Ferdinand more and more harshly. When he began to feel he was in danger of losing his life, he followed Sylvester’s advice and joined the [[temple]], giving up his status as a noble. In a particularly cruel gesture, Veronica forced him to leave behind the ocher Ehrenfest cape he had been given by his father; from that point onward, he began wearing the blue Dunkelfelger cape he had won from Heisshitze in a ditter match at the Royal Academy.<ref name=""P4V7C12"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 7]]. Interduchy Tournament (Second Year)</ref>

When the Sixth Aub Ehrenfest lay on his deathbed, he returned Ferdinand's name to him. Before his father's death, Ferdinand promised that he would do everything in his power to make his half-brother [[Sylvester]] the archduke and aid him henceforth.<ref name=""P4V8C14"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 8]]. Chapter 14: Decisions</ref> When his father's funeral was held, Ferdinand was only able to attend as a blue priest, rather than as a relative of the deceased.<ref name=""P3V4C17"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 4]]. Chapter 17: Georgine's Visit</ref>

When Ferdinand first came to the temple, he only took on just two attendants. Wary that the High Bishop [[Bezewanst]] would attempt to poison him, he hired a chef only to make food for his attendants and returned to his estate in the Noble's Quarter to eat his own meals. His fear turned out to be justified when he caught a grey shrine maiden tampering with the food his chamber, not realizing that Ferdinand did not eat there.

After interrogating the shrine maiden, Ferdinand diluted the poison into a nonlethal dose and had it added to Bezewanst's own food in an overt threat, warning him of the consequences should he make a second attempt. This conflict resulted in a new rule forbidding attendants from entering the kitchens of blue priests or shrine maidens other than their master, and there were no further poisoning incidents in the temple.<ref name=""P4V9S8"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 9]]. Memories and Farewells</ref>

Initially after joining the temple, Ferdinand was frequently bored and had little to occupy his time besides reading and research. Upon hearing this, his brother Sylvester sent a rather significant part of his own work to Ferdinand, in part so he would not have to work so much himself and in part to help his younger brother stave off the boredom.
However, the serious mana shortage caused by the [[Civil War
column2: civil war]] in the [[Sovereignty]] and subsequent political purges had a significant impact on temple life. Young [[Temple Hierarchy#Blue Priest
column3: blue priests and shrine maidens]] were called back into noble society, while those with enough mana were sent to the Sovereignty temple. Due to his mana and family status, Ferdinand was the only one left who was qualified to become the [[Temple Hierarchy#High Priest
column4: High Priest]].<ref name=""P2V1P"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 2 Volume 1]]. Prologue</ref>

column1: Shouldering his temple responsibilities and Sylvester's requests from the castle, Ferdinand soon became exhausted, working late into the night and using [[Magic Potions#Rejuvenation Potion
column2: rejuvenation potions]] to compensate for his lack of sleep. However, his aversion to admitting weakness or asking for help prevented him from mentioning these difficulties to his brother.

Considering the fact that he has been dedicating mana to the divine instruments in the temple for years, it can be assumed that he could use the divine instruments of all primary gods.

**'''Grutrissheit:''' Ferdinand obtained an incomplete copy of the Book of Mestionora when he was enrolled in the Royal Academy, currently shared with Rozemyne. After copying content from Rozemyne's copy, he has enough content to carry out duties as a Zent.

*'''Enhancement Magic:''' Although his proficiency isn't specifically mentioned, Ferdinand is skilled enough in body enhancement magic that he doesn't need assisting magic tools to perform it.<ref name=""P4V1C1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 1]]. Chapter 1: Just Call Me Urashima Taro</ref>

*'''Mana Affinities:''' Ferdinand has all seven [[Mana Elements
column2: elemental affinities]], making his mana appear pearl-white.

column1: *'''Mana Capacity:''' Ferdinand has an exceptionally large amount of [[mana]], unmatched in Ehrenfest. Learning [[Rozemyne Mana Compression Method]] improved it even further.
*'''Medicine:''' Ferdinand has extensive knowledge of medicine, which qualifies him to serve as [[Rozemyne]]'s physician.

*'''Magecraft:''' Ferdinand is a highly skilled researcher with in-depth knowledge of [[mana]], magic circles, magic tools, and potions, as well as [[feybeasts]], [[feyplants]], ancient dialects, and many other subjects. He has also personally invented many new [[Magic Tools

*'''Combat:''' As a [[knight]], Ferdinand can wield a wide range of weapons with ease, including a bow, sword, scythe, thrown cast net, and even a water gun invented by Rozemyne. Very few people in Ehrenfest are able to match him in combat.

*'''Commandership:''' Ferdinand is an exceptional strategist, tactician and field commander, both in real battles and in [[ditter]]. He was infamously referred to as ""the Lord of Evil in Ditter"" in the Royal Academy, due to his devious strategies that rendered all preparations and predictions by other duchies useless, throwing the battlefield into chaos.<ref name=""P4V5C13"" />

*'''Education:''' Ferdinand is an excellent teacher capable of training knights, scholars, temple attendants, and archduke candidates. Although his teaching style is exceptionally strict and demanding, those who are able to survive his training are guaranteed to be outstanding, like [[Fran]] and [[Rozemyne]].

*'''Intellect:''' Ferdinand has genius level intellect and is a prodigy in almost all aspects. When he was enrolled in the [[Royal Academy]], he took the knight’s, scholar’s, and archduke candidate’s courses simultaneously and earned the title of best-in-class in all curricula every year. He has exceptional memory and analytical ability that allows him to remember tiny details and draw connections from seemingly unrelated facts.

*'''Music:''' While all nobles can sing, dance, and play the [[harspiel]], Ferdinand’s musical skills are widely considered to be among the best in Ehrenfest and even earned him praise in other duchies.

*'''Poison Resistance:''' Due to being poisoned often during his childhood and doing various experiments, Ferdinand is resistant against many toxins. His resistance is strong enough that he survived a direct hit by Lanzenavian instant death poison in an enclosed space.

*'''Politics:''' Ferdinand can quickly grasp the political landscape and act to turn it to his advantage, staying several steps ahead of his opponents. He's also good at manipulating others to do what he wants.

*'''Wealth:''' By receiving various allowances for performing temple, knight, and archduke duties, as well as selling his inventions to powerful duchies and people, Ferdinand became extremely wealthy, even by archduke candidate standards. He considers a few [[Lion (Currency)

column1: '''Florencia''' (フロレンツィア, ''Furorentsia'') is the first wife of [[Sylvester]], the [[Aub Ehrenfest
She is the mother of [[Wilfried]], [[Charlotte]], [[Melchior]], and [[Henriette]]. She is also the adoptive mother of [[Rozemyne]].

Florencia has indigo eyes and straight, light-blonde hair that is close to silver. She has a peaceful smile and gives off the impression of a gentle, refined beauty.<ref name=""P3V1C4"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 1]]. Chapter 4: Adoption</ref>

In contrast to her demure appearance, Florencia has a cool head and a firm attitude. She is a strict, no-nonsense mother and is one of the few people who can keep tabs on [[Sylvester]] and [[Wilfried]].<ref name=""P3V1C4""/> Even when she is deeply upset or angry, she can maintain perfect composure.

column1: At age ten, she entered the [[Royal Academy]]. Two years later, [[Sylvester]] entered the academy as well. During their school years, he fell in love with her. Although it is considered very rare for a noblewoman to marry a younger man, he went to great lengths to persuade her and her family to accept his courtship. Finally, he won their approval to escort Florencia at the graduation ceremony.<ref name=""P4V2C6"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 2]]. Chapter 6: Tea Party with the Music Professors</ref>
After Sylvester came of age, Florencia married him and moved to [[Ehrenfest (Duchy)
column2: Ehrenfest,]] as his first and only wife. His decision not to take a second wife frustrated nobles of the Leisegang faction, who for several generations had wanted an archduke candidate with more Ehrenfest blood.<ref name=""FB2S5"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Fanbook 2]]. A Tea Party With My Older Sister</ref> To make matters worse, Florencia was immediately ostracized by [[Veronica]], her new mother-in-law. She found sympathy and support with [[Elvira]] and joined her political faction. Although Elvira remained the leader of the faction, it came to be called the ""Florencia"" faction due to her higher rank.<ref name=""P4V3C2"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 3]]. Chapter 2: Mother and Printing in Haldenzel</ref>

column1: When Florencia gave birth to her first child [[Wilfried]], Veronica claimed that it would be dangerous to trust him to someone who had just married into the family. As a result, Florencia was denied control over her son's upbringing and was only able to see him briefly during family dinners. Because her time with her son was so limited, she didn't realize that Wilfried's education was going very poorly.<ref name=""P3V2C9"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 2]]. Chapter 9: Switching Places</ref>

Satisfied with her control over Wilfried, Veronica had no interest in Florencia's other two children, [[Charlotte]] and [[Melchior]]. Florencia was able to raise the two of them with all the love and strictness they needed to become proper archduke candidates. Her education was seemingly very effective. Charlotte's skills and capabilities soon matched and then exceeded her older brother's.

column2: civil war]], Frenbeltag was one of the losing duchies. While Florencia was safe due to having wedded into the neutral Ehrenfest, her father, the previous Aub Frenbeltag, was executed in the [[Civil War#Political Purge

column1: '''Flutrane''' (フリュートレーネ, ''Furyuutoreene''), the '''Goddess of Water''' (水の女神, ''Mizu no Megami''), is one of the [[Gods and Subordinate Gods#Eternal Five
She presides over spring, healing, change, and new life. Her [[Divine Instruments
column2: divine instrument]] is a [[Divine Instruments#Staff of Flutrane
column4: divine colour]] is green, which symbolizes new leaves in spring.

column1: When the [[God of Darkness]] married the [[Goddess of Light]], they had four children. The oldest was Flutrane, followed by her younger siblings: [[Leidenschaft]], God of Fire; [[Schutzaria]], Goddess of Wind; and [[Geduldh]], Goddess of Earth.

The God of Life [[Ewigeliebe]] fell in love with Flutrane's younger sister, Geduldh. The God of Darkness gave the two permission to marry, hoping they would fill the world with new life. But Ewigeliebe's jealous love consumed him, and he froze Geduldh in ice, so her child could never be born.

The world fell into winter, and The Goddess of Light began to worry about her daughter. She found Geduldh trapped and melted the ice with her rays of sunlight, and Flutrane caused the water to flood away, bringing spring to the world.

Her siblings Leidenschaft and Schutzaria worked with her to protect Geduldh from Ewigeliebe, bringing summer and autumn. However, they could not fully defeat Ewigeliebe without preventing all new life from being born. Each year at the end of autumn, Ewigeliebe once again traps the Goddess of Earth in ice, and Flutrane must fight to free her in spring.
The phrase ""Goddess of Water"" is a [[Noble Euphemisms
column2: euphemism]] commonly understood to mean ""lover"" or ""one who moves the heart"". However, it is also used by commoners to mean one who brings new ideas or prosperity.

column1: Flutrane's subordinate Bluanfah is often invoked as a euphemism for blossoming love.
The phrase ""Flutrane and Heilschmertz heal in their own ways"" is a euphemism usually meaning ""everyone has their own way of doing things"".
In blessings and greetings, merchants often refer to Flutrane as the ""Goddess of Spring"" rather than her usual title.

The Royal Academy contains a shrine dedicated to Flutrane and her twelve subordinates, which grants a tablet, and a special word required to obtain the [[Grutrissheit]], after one has prayed and dedicated enough mana to her. The word Rozemyne was granted was Rombekur.<ref name=""P5V5C8"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 5 Volume 5]]. Chapter 8: Circling the Shrines</ref>
Flutrane is invoked in several [[Religious Ceremonies
column3: blessings]] involving healing, water, and springtime.

column1: During Rozemyne's second term at the royal academy, Fraularm continues her attempts to undermine Ehrenfest. When all the Ehrenfest second year students manage to not only all pass the history exam on the first attempt, but manage to do this after also being the first duchy to turn in all their tests and all get not just passing, but actually good marks on it, she raises a fuss about this being highly suspicious.

While her fellow proctors see nothing suspicious in this, she still manages to cause a discussion that lasts long enough that two other duchies who turned their tests in after Ehrenfest are announced to also reach all passing marks before a conclusion can be made for the tenth.

Eventually her colleagues overrule Fraularm and announce that Ehrenfest also reached all passing marks, frustrating the former Ahrensbach noble so much that she completely fails to conceal her frustration to the point out audibly shrieking.<ref name=""P4V6C1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 6]]. Chapter 1: The Beginning of Classes</ref>

This attempt at undermining Ehrenfest was by no means a snap decision. She started to gather documents pertaining to her predecessors syllabus right after the students left the academy in the previous year.<ref name=""RAS1C17""/>

Her attempts to sabotage Ehrenfest do not stop there either. Under the pretense of wanting to make sure that Ehrenfest was indeed not cheating, she manages to push through a change in the syllabus of sociology class to that taught before the civil war. Due to the exam covering topics not taught for more than a decade the students who were prepared to pass their exam on the first day were caught completely off guard. When [[Ortwin]] of [[Drewanchel]] questions why the first problem was something that did not appear in the previous year's syllabus, she explains that this topic was taught to students in the past, so she chose to incorporate it to convey the wisdom of their forbearers. Despite supposedly giving a neutral explanation to Ortwin, Fraularm clearly smirks in amusement toward the Ehrenfest students, leaving no one in the room with any doubt as to who her true target in this is.

This change prompted the majority of students to give up on passing the exam on the first day and handing their tests in early. Despite the surprise change the students of Ehrenfest managed to answer all the questions and once again every single one of them received passing marks on the first day, the very thing Fraularm tried to disrupt. The other professors commented on how splendid Ehrenfest had done and how this proved beyond a doubt that Ehrenfest did not cheat, leaving Fraularm no other choice than to announce Ehrenfests passing marks, failing to conceal how vexed she feels.<ref name=""P4V6C6"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 6]]. Chapter 6: Everyone Passing on the First Day</ref>

Due to the danger of the beast, the Ehrenfest students call upon the professors for help and [[Rauffen]] goes to summon the sovereign knight's order to deal with it.<ref name=""P4V6C17"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. column1: Following the incident it was decided that an investigation was required. Not only was it important to assure that no others of its kind were lurking around, the behavior of the slain beast was also quite unusual. After arriving and escaping the [[Werkestock]] dormitory, the beast should have homed in either on the closest or the strongest [[mana]] source, but did neither. Instead it ignored the much more mana-rich grounds of the greater duchies and even went right past both the Ahrensbach and Fernbeltag gathering spots to charge in a straight line toward Ehrenfest.

The professors chosen for this task are Rauffen, due to being the one who called upon the knight's order, [[Hirschur]] on account of being the supervisor of the attacked duchy's dormitory, [[Gundolf]] who volunteered and Fraularm.

The trail of destruction left behind by the beast started at the now abandoned former Werkestock dormitory, so they reopened it to investigate. To make sure the professors would stay impartial and not try to steal any magic tools left behind by the fallen duchy two members of the sovereign knight's order were assigned to accompany them into the dormitory after unlocking the main gate at the king's behest.

Gundolf and Fraularm arrived at the dormitory door right on time, while Rauffen went to Hirschur's lab to pry her away from her research in the expectation that she would either arrive with a big delay or not at all otherwise.
While Rauffen managed to do so, the pair still arrives a little after the decided time.
In the meantime Gundolf and Fraularm already enter the dormitory and upon entry Fraularm immediately cast [[Spells and Prayers#Waschen
column2: waschen]] to clean the entry hall and the connecting corridor, stating she could not be expected to enter such a dirty place, since it would ruin her clothes. This sparked an argument with her colleague Gundolf, during which Hirschur and Rauffen arrive.

column1: Fraularm tried to get Hirschur on her side in the argument, as she thought that, as a fellow woman, Hirschur would understand her aversion to dirtying her clothes, but Hirschur flatly stated that was what brewing clothes were for.

After this discussion had come to an end, the present people split into two teams of two professors and one knight each. Hirschur and Rauffen investigated the cellar, while Gundolf and Fraularm went to the second and third floors.

During the investigation neither team turned up any disturbances of the thick dust-layer or anything else suspicious. Gundolf also stated that they found no evidence of the teleportation circle being used. He volunteered to help the knights compile the report for the [[Trauerqual
column2: King]] and told Hirschur and Fraularm they could leave if they wished, adding that Ahrensbach had been proven to not be involved, though he insisted on Rauffen staying with him for the report for administrative purposes, since he was the one who called upon the knight's order.<ref name=""P4V6S2"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 6]]. Investigating the Former Werkestock Dormitory</ref>

column1: Since she prioritized the archduke candidate course, Rozemyne missed the first day of several scholar course lessons. In order to not have to wait for the final exam at the end of the semester, she writes messages to the professors holding those lessons to schedule for personal exams. She easily breezes through all of them until only Professor Fraularm's class remains.

Initially Fraularm ignores Rozemyne's messages, but some time later Hirschur prods her by indirectly questioning her ability to properly communicate by pointing out how Ehrenfest was going to do joint research with two other greater duchies, but Ahrensbach was being left out despite supposedly being close to Ehrenfest now that Detline and Ferdinand are engaged.

Once Rozemyne arrives at Fraularm's laboratory the professor immediately begins prodding Rozemyne about her cooperative research projects and the possibility of doing the same with Ahrensbach, but Rozemyne delays this discussion by stating that she wants to finish her classes first and thus they move on to the exam. After she finishes and before the grading, Rozemyne summons Hirschur under the excuse that she needs her duchy's dormitory supervisor present to discuss a joint research project with Ahrensbach and Hirschur arrives almost immediately.

That Rozemyne would talk about the cooperation right after the test makes Fraularm suspicious for a moment, until Rozemyne tells her that this was the last subject she had to pass this semester and that once the professor finished grading her, she would be free to consider the research and so Fraularm moves to grade the test with Hirschur looking over her shouler. It is at this point that Hirschur points out that Fraularm ""accidentally"" gave Rozemyne the wrong test, since this one is meant for fifth-year students. Hirschur asks how Rozemyne managed to answer the questions and Rozemyne replies that Ferdinand had drilled the entire syllabus into her at once to the point where she doesn't even know which part is supposed to be taught in which year. Hirschur is impressed that Rozemyne was able to keep up with Ferdinand, while Fraularm only mutters ""this isn't normal"" over and over in befuddlement. Rozemyne is worried that she needs to re-take the correct test, but clearly frustrated with how spectacularly her ploy failed Fraularm gives Rozemyne a passing grade to be done with the sorry affair.

With some team-work Rozemyne and Hirschur are able to get Fraularm on board for the joint research to be a cooperation between Rozemyne and Raimund in Hirschur's laboratory, with the communication to Ahrensbach going through Fraularm. Rozemyne is also able to get Fraularm to agree to have Ferdinand involved under the not entirely wrong excuse that Hirschur and Raimund will very likely get so engrossed into their work that they'll surely fail to file proper reports sooner or later, something Fraularm has already experienced personally and thus readily accepts. Since this arrangement would not only give Fraularm full insight into the research that is being done, but also has great potential to improve her reputation she is only too happy with this outcome.<ref name=""P5V1C15"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 1]]. Chapter 15: Professor Fraularm’s Class</ref>

When Rozemyne disappears from the public eye during her fourth year at the Royal Academy, Fraularm is highly critical about Ehrenfest's explanation of her having fallen ill. She repeatedly insists that Rozemyne has been absent for far too long and that can only mean that the girl has died and Ehrenfest is lying to everything. Her repeated tantrums get so bad, that eventually a committee of her peers unanimously votes to have her removed from her position as professor and sovereign noble and she is sent back to Ahrensach.<ref name=""P5V7S1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. column1: '''Freida''' (フリーダ ''Furiida'') is the granddaughter of [[Gustav]], the guildmaster of [[Ehrenfest (Duchy)
Freida is a very cute girl with brown eyes, a peaceful smile, and light, rose-colored hair that [[Myne]] describes as “as fluffy as it is soft-looking.” Due to [[Devouring
column2: her illness]], she is small for her age.<ref name=""P1V2C13""/>

column1: Several years later in part 4, she grows to about as big as girls of similar age.<ref>''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 5]]. Chapter 4: Evolved Cooking</ref>
Freida has a mature and dignified demeanor, partly because she was required to learn formal etiquette in preparation for moving to the Nobles’ Quarter.

Inwardly, however, she is an ambitious merchant with a keen nose for profit. She has a knack for seeing opportunities that are overlooked by others. When money is at stake, Freida often becomes aggressive and straightforward, forgetting her demure demeanor.

column2: the Devouring]] and was a sickly child. Her grandfather [[Gustav]] was determined to save her life, and he used his vast wealth and connections as the leader of the [[Merchant's Guild]] to buy magic tools that could prolong her lifespan.

column1: Due to his status and wealth, Gustav managed to secure multiple offers for submission contracts and even adoptions for his granddaughter, leaving him the luxury of being able to choose one to his liking. With Freida's wish being to remain a merchant, rather than become a noble, Gustav chose to sign a submission contract with [[Henrik
column2: Lord Henrik]], a very gentle and calm layscholar, who is unusually respectful to commoners for a noble.

column1: According to the terms of the contract, Freida will be provided with a [[Magic Tools#Mana Draining Magic Tool
column2: magic tool]] in the shape of a bracelet to drain her mana until she comes of age at 15. During this time, Freida had to regularly visit her master's mansion, where the mana stored in the bracelet would be drained to be used to power the mansion's magic tools. Once she comes of age, she will then become Henrik’s mistress and live in the Noble's Quarter, where she plans to continue working as a merchant and open up a store in the Noble's Quarter.<ref name=""P2V4S1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. column1: '''Gabriele''' was a former [[Ahrensbach]] noble who married a son of the fourth [[Aub Ehrenfest]].

During their time at the [[Royal Academy]], Gabriele fell deeply in love with the son of the fourth Aub Ehrenfest. Due to her having a rather small [[mana]] capacity for an archduke candidate of a greater duchy her prospects of marrying into an archducal family were low, but since at the time [[Ehrenfest (Duchy)
column2: Ehrenfest]] was just a minor duchy with a much lower average in mana capacity among it's nobles, this was not an issue in this case. She used her position as the daughter of a greater duchy's archduke to force the marriage through, disregarding what her future husband or his family might wish.

column1: At the time the marriage happened, her husband was already married to a noblewoman of Leisegang. That woman was demoted to second wife, with Gabriele becoming the new first wife.

Despite now being a noble in a lesser duchy, near the bottom of the rankings, Gabriele did not change her behaviour and attitude as she was supposed to do, but kept acting like a member of a greater duchy, near the top of the ranks. If such a woman was allowed to participate in diplomatic meetings, it could have catastrophic results for her new home. Between this and the fear of the political dissent from the demotion of her husbands former first wife (the Leisegangs being the most powerful faction in Ehrenfest at the time), as well as worries about increased influence from Ahrensbach, Aub Ehrenfest negotiated directly with Aub Ahrensbach and the two archdukes agreed that Gabriele's husband would be given land and made into a giebe, thus demoting him and by extension Gabriele to archnobles and removing them from the succession, thus removing the external political risks, while reducing the inner-duchy turmoil to some degree. As compensation a contract was signed that would ensure that Gabriele's child would become either the next Aub or the next Aub's first wife.<ref name=""FB6QA"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Fanbook 6]]. Q&A with Miya Kazuki</ref> Gabriele would later find the life in such a backwater to be undesirable and longed to go back to her former home.

Gabriele deeply loved for her husband, but the newly minted Count Groschel did not reciprocate those feelings, since he was equally deeply in love with his former first, now second wife. Their marriage remained solely businesslike throughout their entire time together.

She encouraged the retainers that had come with her from Ahrensbach to marry into Ehrenfest families, but since essentially all archnobles had at least tenuous blood-ties to the Leisegang family, they chose to marry mednobles with particularly high mana capacity. This was the birth of what would later become the Veronica faction.<ref name=""P4V5C6"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 5]]. Chapter 6: My Brother Lamprecht's Wedding</ref>

Gabriele gave birth to three children, two boys and one girl. Her firstborn son became a candidate to succeed Count Groschel due to his mana capacity and support from Ahrensbach, but he died too early to succeed the position. Her second child was [[Veronica]], who as agreed in the contract between the Ehrenfest and Ahrensbach, would go on to marry the sixth Aub Ehrenfest and give birth to [[Georgine]], [[Constanze]] and [[Sylvester]].

During her final pregnancy, Gabriele fell ill and ultimately died soon after child labor, though her second son [[Bezewanst]] survived the ordeal. However his mana capacity was far below what was expected of an archnoble and thus he was sent to the temple to later become the [[Temple Hierarchy#High Bishop
Her daughter Veronica was eventually married to Aub Ehrenfest and inherited the leadership of the faction Gabriele had built.

column1: '''Georgine''' (ゲオルギーネ, ''Georugiine'') is the former first wife of [[Gieselfried]], known as [[Gieselfried
column2: Aub Ahrensbach]]. She is the mother of [[Detlinde]], [[Sylvester]]'s older sister and a former [[Nobility/Hierarchy#Archduke Candidate

column1: Georgine has dark green eyes and blue hair that is close to purple, much like her brother [[Sylvester]]. She has sharp, pointed facial features and is considered very beautiful.<ref name=""FB2CharacterDesign"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Fanbook 2]]. Character Design Sheets</ref> In [[Ahrensbach]] fashion, she wears a thin, translucent veil over her face. She bears a striking resemblance to her mother, [[Veronica]]<ref name=""P3V4S1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 4]]. A Tea Party (after Epilogue)</ref>.

Georgine is an intelligent, diligent and strong-willed person, but she tends to hold grudges for long period of time. She deeply resents her younger brother Sylvester, believing that he stole the position of [[Aub Ehrenfest]] that was rightfully hers. She shows open contempt for him and revels in her newfound position of power over him.
A charismatic leader, Georgine has attracted the loyalty of many [[Ehrenfest (Duchy)#Veronica Faction
column2: former Veronica faction]] members. Her cunning intellect also allows her to develop sophisticated political schemes, leaving no traces of evidence that lead back to her.

column1: When Georgine talks to people it often feels to the person as if she wasn't really looking at them, but rather through them to some distant point at the horizon, with her focus entirely on her future goals.<ref name=""P4V9S4"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 9]]. Out of Time</ref>
Georgine was born the eldest child of [[Adelbert]], the Sixth [[Aub Ehrenfest]], and [[Veronica]], his first wife. Growing up, she was widely expected to become the [[Nobility/Hierarchy#Aub
column3: Ehrenfest]].<ref name=""P3V4C17"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 4]]. Chapter 17: Georgine's Visit</ref>

column1: Since the Aub only had a daughter, Georgine had to compete with her male cousins for the seat of successor, particularly [[Karstedt]]. To make sure her daughter wouldn't lose to someone else's children, Veronica brutally trained Georgine from a very young age, accompanied often by beatings. Only [[Rihyarda]] would at times step in to hold Veronica back, when she went too far, though Georgine enjoyed a deep connection with her uncle [[Bezewanst]] who doted on her, albeit they were only able to meet rarely on account of their respective positions.

Veronica's second child [[Constanze]] was born a girl and the mother didn't even make an attempt to hide her disappointment of having only another girl and neglected her almost entirely. Feeling sorry for her sister, Georigne tried to pass the archduke candidate lessons on to her, but soon found that without any hope to ever become the Aub, Constanze lacked the drive to live through the brutal lessons.<ref name=""P5V8E""/>

Once Veronica gave birth to a boy [[Sylvester]]. From that moment on, all of Veronica's attention and love was given exclusively to the boy and she completely spoilt him rotten. Instead of having to work hard, like Georgine had to, Sylvester was allowed to run away from his lessons and anyone who spoke out about this was in turn dressed down by Veronica. This included Georgine too. If she tried to make her little brother behave according to his station, Veronica would scold her and make her apologize to the boy, stating that he was too young for harsh lessons, despite having already put Georgine through brutal training when she was that age. For this reason, Georgine never started to care for her little brother and even sometimes wished he would just die. Veronica made it no secret, that she wanted to make her son the next Aub, and for that purpose reassigned Rihyarda - who've been more of a mother to Georgine than her actual mother ever was - to him and stopped training her daughter in archduke candidate lessons.

Upon her entry into the [[Royal Academy]], Georgine found that Veronica had reserved all the children she wanted as retainers for Sylvester, further fouling Georgine's chances to become archduchess. However her father still arranged an engagement with an archduke candidate who would marry into Ehrenfest, which kept her hope of becoming the successor alive for a little longer.

At Sylvester's baptism, Veronica declared before the entire nobility of Ehrenfest, that he would be the next Aub, despite no such decision having been made by the current Aub. Not wishing to show division within the archducal family, Adelbert decided to not immediately call her out in public and instead try to solve the issue later in private. But apparently instead of him sorting things out, Veronica managed to sway him and soon after Gerogine's engagement was dissolved, since it was dependent on her becoming the successor. They told her in no uncertain terms that they wanted her to dedicate her all to supporting Sylvester.

Despite this, Georgine initially decided to make Sylvester into a worthy Aub, trying to give him the same brutal lessons, she received from Georgine, but Sylvester tried to run away at every opportunity and loudly proclaimed he didn't want to be Aub and that she should do it, if she cared so much for the position. This caused [[Grausam]], her most loyal servant, to state that they were better off eliminating Sylvester. He was also the one telling her about [[Nobility#Name-Swearing
column2: name-swearing]] and about how Veronica's used it and others methods to eliminate anyone she could not be absolutely sure of being loyal to her, to establish her own power-base, before offering Georgine his own name.

column1: As Grausam suggested, she began poaching people of her age, who had been reluctant to give their names to Veronica due to her advancing age and made them swear to her instead, while also covertly sowing rumours about Sylvester to undermine him. Despite her skill, her parents found out and this is when they decided to marry her off into [[Ahrensbach]], where she was going to become the [[Gieselfried
column2: Aub]]'s third wife, a man as old as her own father.

column1: Soon after Sylvester proclaimed his love for Florencia and that he would take no other wife than her. This finally made Gerogine snap and she finally went from only thinking and wishing about her brother's death, to actively trying to assassinate him, with the same kind of poison that her mother had used so often herself. She had one of her name-sworn put the poison into Sylvester's food and he started to choke at their next dinner. While Veronica despaired, Georgine felt utterly elated, only regretting that his death throes didn't last longer. But against all expectations Sylvester survived. While Veronica was frozen in terror, one of her attendants had immediately sprung into action and administered an antidote.

After her move to Ahrensbach, Georgine fell into depression and just did nothing but survive. She reckoned that she could take power, but didn't care enough to try. One day she had the thought that, if she were to become the first wife, she could stand over Sylvester during archduke conferences and this finally gave her the motivation to do something again. She worked hard and plotted and eventually made it, but found that just humiliating Sylvester, satisfying as it was, wasn't enough for her. She became despondent again, until she received a letter from Bezewanst, which apparently contained information of how she might be able to steal Ehrenfest's foundation.<ref name=""P5V8E""/>
She left for Ahrensbach before [[Ferdinand]] first came to live in the castle, so they did not encounter each other until their [[Adelbert
column2: father's]] funeral. Since Ferdinand was serving as a [[Temple Hierarchy#Blue Priest
column3: blue priest,]] they did not exchange greetings.<ref name=""P3V4C17""/> Throughout her time in Ahrensbach, Georgine remained in close communication with her uncle, the former High Bishop [[Bezewanst]].<ref name=""P3V4C17""/>
