Although Georgine's original position was third wife to Aub Ahrensbach, she rose to the rank of first wife in the year following Bezewanst's death. In her first year attending the [[Archduke Conference]], she was able to learn about the true circumstances of the Bezewanst incident that occurred the year prior, and negotiated to secure a visit to Ehrenfest to see his grave. There she got permission from Sylvester to visit Veronica in prison, under the condition that she not speak a single word, which Georgine adhered to. Gerda (ゲルダ ''Geruda'') lives in [[Myne]]'s neighborhood and works as a babysitter.
She looks like a nice elderly woman.
She is quite carefree seen how she treats the toddlers when babysitting them.

[[Myne]] is brought over to Gerda when nobody is at home to look after her. Gerda is not a professional, but watches over the toddlers of her neighbors to help the community in a non-official capacity.<ref name=""FB1QA"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Fanbook

While Myne thinks about making papyrus, one day comes, where her whole family has to work. As they do not trust Myne to stay home alone [[Effa]] takes Myne to Gerda before she goes to work. When they arrived at Gerda's place other toddlers are already present. Gerda sits by her table and watches over the toddlers and Myne, who runs around looking after the toddlers.

Myne is shocked at how little Gerda actually does. She does nothing when a child puts a dirty toy in it's mouth and doesn't even intervene when one of the toddlers starts to hit another, only saying ""My, my"". Only when one of the children pees itself does she get up to wipe it and the floor.
Due to this Myne hates being at Gerda's and immediately charges straight into [[Tuuli]]'s arms when she comes to get Myne.

While Myne abhors this treatment of the children, she dares not complain to anyone about it, since she doesn't know enough about this world yet to know whether such behavior is normal here and she's the odd one out with her Earth-made common sense.
*Myne describes Gerda's babysitting as ''child neglect'' and got a little traumatized.

column2: Adalgisa Villa]], with the assigned number Terza, the boy had the highest mana capacity out of all the children of his generation and thus was chosen to be sent back to [[Lanzenave]] to become its next king upon coming of age and consequently was given his proper name Gervasio. To keep the whole deal between [[Lanzenave]] and [[Yurgenschmidt]] secret, he was only allowed to leave the Adalgisa Villa and enter the rest of the Royal Academy, during the seasons, when no students were around. The staff of the academy was told that he was a member of a royal family branch and could not attend the regular curriculum due to poor health. During the springs, summers and autumns he often visited the [[Royal Academy/Library
column3: Royal Academy Library]] and got along very well with [[Solange

column1: His supposed poor health was again used, when it became time for Gervasio to leave for Lanzenave. The people who had come into contact with him at the academy, were told, that he had to leave the [[Sovereignty]] due to his health.

Gervasio first met [[Raublut]], when the young sovereign knight was assigned to guard house Loweleier as his first assignment as a knight. The two quickly developed deep respect for each other, with the latter coming to believe that Gervasio, would have made a much better Zent than the one ruling the country at the time or his successor [[Waldifried]].

Apart from brothers, who were all eventually executed and sent to Lanzenave as feystones, he had two sisters. His older sister [[Seradina]] was the flower of House Loweleier, and thus he had no contact with her. He had a very close relationship with his younger sister [[Valamarlene]], with whom he grew up in the side building. He also had a third sister, who was a gardener, but it is unclear how close he was to her.

Due to how close he was with Valamarlene, he tried to get her out of the Adalgisa villa by arranging a marriage between her and Raublut. Against all odds, this plan seemed to succeed and the Zent agreed to the engagement. However, before the marriage could happen, [[Seradina]] and [[Adelbert]] of [[Ehrenfest (Duchy)
column2: Ehrenfest]] managed to get their son [[Ferdinand]], whom Gervasio only heard of by his designated number Quinta, out of the villa, at the cost of [[Seradina]] taking his place to become a feystone. In her place, Valamarlene was chosen to become Loweleier's next flower, which automatically canceled the engagement and dashed any hope of her freeing her from the villa, as well as preventing any contact between the siblings. No longer having any way to protect or even see his younger sister, Gervasio asked his loyal retainer Raublut to keep her safe, which he vowed to do.

column1: After the civil war, the Adalgisa villa was closed by the new Zent [[Trauerqual]] and all its remaining inhabitants were executed, including Valamarlene, which would eventually set off Gervasio and Raublut's plans to conquer [[Yurgenschmidt]], so they could abolish the inhumane Adalgisa deal for good and never let anything like it happen again.<ref name=""P5V9E""/>

column1: When it comes to politics, Giebe Kirnberger takes an entirely neutral stance, preferring to stay as far away from faction politics as he possibly can, while still keeping a vigilant eye on the squabbling of the other nobles and the goings-on in the castle.<ref name=""P5V4E""/>
He often personally patrols his duchy, leading to his office usually being quite busy with the backlog, whenever he is home.<ref name=""P5V4E""/>

Giebe Kirnberger's father was quite fond of Bonifatius and openly wished that [[Bonifatius]] would have become the sixth Aub Ehrenfest, in place of his younger brother Adelbert. This respect for and inspiration by Bonifatius seems to be something that is shared by Giebe Kirnberger as well.

His second wife is a former Leisegang noble, who was severely abused by [[Veronica]]. At the advice from [[Bonifatius]]' first wife, she tried to marry into a far away province to escape her fate and eventually managed to marry into Kirnberger, where she gave birth to a son, Alexis.

When their son became old enough to visit the castle, Giebe Kirnberger made sure he stay close to him and his first wife, rather than his mother, so he would not suffer the mistreatment that Veronica and her faction heaped upon anyone associated with the Leisegangs.

column2: Lord Wilfried]] lost many of his retainers, giving Alexis the chance to become his guard knight, at [[Lamprecht]]'s invitation. Upon learning this, Giebe Kirnberger assigned one of his veteran knights to give Alexis extra lessons and training, so he would be a worthy retainer to a member of the archducal family.<ref name=""P5V4E""/>

column2: Lady Rozemyne]] visits Kirnberger for [[Religious Ceremonies#Spring Prayer
column3: Spring Prayer]], and to have her Gutenbergs help the province in establishing printing, paper-making and ink workshops. At the occasion Giebe Kirnberger shows Rozemyne the country gate and tells her the history of the province back to the days of [[Eisenreich]]. At Rozemyne's prompting, he explains that while written records do exist, the history is passed down mostly orally, since barely anyone is able, or willing to read the texts written in the ancient dialect. As an expert in ancient language and an avid lover of anything written down, Rozemyne eagerly requests access to those texts, so she can transcribe them and compare them with both the local oral history and what she was taught as a member of the archducal family, with the Giebe gives.

column1: '''Gieselfried''' (ギーゼルフリート, ''Giizerufuriito'') was the last archduke of [[Ahrensbach]]. He was the husband of [[Georgine]], and father of [[Detlinde]].
<!-- This paragraph really needs to an overhaul. To Do List-->
Gieselfried's first wife was from [[Drewanchel]].<ref name=""P4V5C6"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 4 Volume 5]]. Chapter 6: My Brother Lamprecht's Wedding</ref>
His second wife was the little sister of Aub Werkestock.

During the civil war, Gieselfried positioned his duchy on the side that would eventually win the conflict, putting him in direct confrontation with the former home of his second wife.
Even so, Ahrensbach was not spared from the purges that the victorious royal family and [[Klassenberg]] insisted on. Despite being married to an active ally and not directly implicated in any disloyal acts, Gieselfried's second wife was still executed, solely due to being the little sister of Aub Werkestock, who was a supporter of the first and later the fourth prince. Gieselfried was able to successfully negotiate with the king to spare her two sons under the condition that they would be demoted to archnobles and thus eliminated from the race for succession.

A short time after the purge, his only other son Wolfram died. With [[Detlinde]] being the only archduke candidate left, Gieselfried approached the duchies into which his daughters had married to try to adopt his own grandchildren to gain more archduke candidates, but due to the mana shortage affecting the entire country, only [[Drewanchel]] agreed to allow the adoption of [[Letizia]], the granddaughter of him and his first wife.<ref name=""P4V4E"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 4 Volume 4]]. Epilogue</ref>
Around the time [[Rozemyne]] was adopted into [[Ehrenfest]]'s archducal family, Gieselfried's first wife died, and his former third wife [[Georgine]] was promoted to first wife.
He has several daughters of whom only the youngest, Detlinde remains unmarried.

Right now, Gieselfried and Georgine are looking for a suitable husband for Detlinde. Since the Aub successor has already been decided and they want to avoid strife within their duchy, they are looking for someone who lacks the ambition or standing to push Detlinde to try to take the title of Aub successor away from [[Letizia]]. With his tarnished reputation and family ties to Ahrensbach, Wilfried appears to be a perfect candidate, but unfortunately he has recently been announced to be betrothed to Lady Rozemyne with the king's approval, dashing their hopes of arranging a marriage between the cousins.<ref name=""P4V4E""/> They start pondering the possibility of getting [[Ferdinand]], who is talented but is infamous for staying in the temple, to marry Detlinde.
At the [[Archduke Conference]] following Rozemyne's second year at the [[Royal Academy]], Gieselfried approaches [[Sylvester
column2: Aub Ehrenfest]] about marrying Ferdinand to Detlinde, but after listing a row of counter-arguments Ehrenfest refuses. To address claims and worries by Ahrensbach, [[Dunkelfelger]], and [[Drewanchel]] about Ferdinand being mistreated in his home and forced to serve in the [[temple]] against his will, Ferdinand is summoned to the Archduke Conference and refutes these false claims and misguided worries, seemingly settling the issue of this marriage.<ref name=""P4V8C12"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 4 Volume 8]]. Chapter 12: Report on the Archduke Conference (Second Year)</ref>

column1: Despite being quite thoroughly refused by both the Ehrenfest archducal couple and Ferdinand himself, Gieselfried petitions the [[Trauerqual
column2: King]] for help in forcing the engagement through, causing Ferdinand to be summoned again some days later. Without further consultation with Aub Ehrenfest, the King announces that Ferdinand and Detlinde will be married right after the girl comes of age, without the usual one-year preparation period.

column1: According to rumors, this desperate action was due to Gieselfried not having long to live and being expected to die even before this forced marriage is supposed to take place.<ref name=""P4V8C13"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 4 Volume 8]]. Chapter 13: A More Private Meeting (Second Year)</ref>

In the summer before Detlinde's final year at the Royal Academy, Gieselfried's health took another turn for the worse. Fearing he would not live to see the marriage, he urgently requested that Ferdinand come to live in Ahrensbach prior to winter socializing, rather than in spring as initially planned, so he would still be around to introduce Ferdinand to Ahrensbach's noble society and help him settle in. column2: Ehrenfest’s]] nobles were called to the Sovereignty. To make up for the loss, Ehrenfest recalled many [[Temple Hierarchy#Blue Priest
column3: blue priests and shrine maidens]] back to the nobility, including Shikikoza. Shikikoza was granted the status of a mednoble and allowed to serve in the [[Knight's Order]], and Gloria began planning once again to make him his father’s heir.

column1: Some time later, Shikikoza participated in a [[Trombe
column2: trombe]] extermination as a [[knight]], where he was assigned to guard [[Myne]]. However, he put his charge in danger due to his prejudice against commoners. He was later sentenced to death for going against orders.

Aub Ehrenfest]] signed an agreement with Viscount Dahldolf that pardoned the rest of his family from collective punishment in exchange for their promise never to approach Myne again, and half the cost of Myne's ceremonial robes.

column1: Despite her best efforts, Gloria was unable to overturn her son's death sentence. However, she managed to spare Shikikoza's reputation by having the official announcement altered to say that he had died in the line of duty, rather than been executed as a criminal.<ref name=""P2V3C6""/>

Gloria developed a strong grudge against Myne and [[Ferdinand]], holding them personally responsible for her son's death. She holds great contempt for commoners, and considers it unjust that her son was be executed for harming someone lower in status.

After [[Shikikoza]]'s execution, Gloria dedicates herself seeking revenge on [[Myne]]. Her options are limited by the magic contract signed by the nobles of Dahldolf, which prevents any member of the family from approaching Myne. However, she continues to look for a way to circumvent the contract.
When [[Rozemyne]] enters noble society, Gloria holds her in contempt and often slanders her reputation at tea parties and social gatherings.
As a member of the [[Veronica]] faction, Gloria is sympathetic to [[Georgine]] and is involved in plans to bring her back to [[Ehrenfest (Duchy)
column2: Ehrenfest]].<ref name=""P3V4E""/> She informs [[Georgine]] that Rozemyne used to be a commoner, and explains that she was responsible for the death of [[Bezewanst]], Georgine’s uncle. Later, she is complicit in plans for [[Charlotte]]'s kidnapping and Rozemyne’s poisoning.

column1: Six years after Shikikoza's execution, Gloria tries to finally enact her revenge on Rozemyne. With the help of the blue priest [[Egmont]], who's family are entirely under Dahldolf's influence, she is able to find out about Ferdinand and Rozemyne being absent from the temple for a visit at the [[Italian Restaurant]] and makes Egmont invite her to have a reason to enter the temple. To keep her visit as secret as possible, she has her coach driver pretend to be from the [[Plantin Company]]. Being well acquainted with the Plantin Company's driver and the general attitude of all their personnel, which stands in stark contrast to the dismissive behaviour the viscountess' driver displays, the gray priests guarding the gate are not fooled by this lie, prompting Gloria to show herself from the coaches window and personally order the gray priests to announce her arrival to Egmont, which they dutifully do.
Once the gate has been opened, Gloria restrains the four gray priests with magic and has them sent south by her driver, likely to later interrogate them about [[printing]] and [[Plant Paper
column2: paper-making]]. She then proceeds to meet with Egmont.

column1: To gain his help for her plot, Gloria tells him how she intends to switch the [[Bible#High Bishop's Bible
column2: high bishop's bible]] with an empty fake so that once the next ceremony comes up Rozemyne would be humiliated and surely dismissed from her position in the temple as a result, when it became known she has lost her bible. She promises that once this comes to pass, she will advocate for Egmont to become the new [[Temple Hierarchy#High Bishop
column3: high bishop]]. She presents Egmont with a [[Commoner_Magic_Utilities#Contract_Magic
column4: magic contract]] to make this promise binding, but secretly presents him with a double-layered parchment with a standard submission contract underneath. Egmont does not notice this duplicity and thus happily signs his freedom away and agrees to help her. Gloria gives him a magic ring, stating that it was a gift to commemorate them getting rid of Rozemyne and that he was now a true noble, since he could now make use of the mana within himself. In truth the ring was a trojan horse meant to give Gloria the ability to kill him at any moment of her choosing, or if certain conditions are triggered, effectively turning him into a devouring soldier without him even noticing. The ring carried [[Grausam
column5: Giebe Gerlach]]'s crest, making it likely that he was the one who manufactured it and then gave it to Gloria.

column1: Egmont's attendants manage to successfully distract and draw away all of Rozemyne's attendants, sneak into the high bishop's chambers through the servant access points and unlock in from inside, allowing Gloria and Egmont to enter. Once inside, Gloria uses a [[Magic Tools#Duplication Magic Tool
column2: magic tool]] to make a fake bible that from the outside is indistinguishable from the original and registers the bible's key with her own mana. Unbeknownst to Egmont she also applies poison to the fake bible.

column1: After her visit concludes, she sends her coach off to the south with the captured gray priests and flies to the Dahldolf winter estate in the [[City of Ehrenfest#Noble's Quarter
column2: noble's quarter]] on her [[highbeast]].<ref name=""P4V9C9"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 9]]. Chapter 9: New Perspectives</ref>

column1: Once there, she has one of her attendants wrap the stolen bible in a piece of cloth bought from the [[Gilberta Company]] and brought to the [[City_of_Ehrenfest#The_Archduke's_Castle
column2: castle]] to be sent to [[Ahrensbach]], disguised as a gift for Ferdinand and [[Detlinde]]'s wedding.

column1: Just a relatively short time later Rozemyne, Ferdinand and their retainers arrive at the estate to apprehend Gloria, apparently having discovered her plot. Knowing that by her actions she has already doomed herself and unwilling to even attempt to beg for mercy, Gloria quickly scribbles a note re-stating her loathing for Rozemyne and taunting her that she will find it very difficult to find what was stolen. Rather than allowing herself to be captured alive and have her memories searched, she first executes her two present female attendants by exploding their heads and then does the same to herself, committing suicide, before Rozemyne and Ferdinand's knights can get to her.<ref name=""P4V9C10"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 9]]. Chapter 10: Viscount Dahldolf's Estate</ref>

column3: Yurgenschmidt's]] religion. He and his wife, the [[Goddess of Light]], are said to rule over the heavens.

column1: He presides over darkness and marriage. His [[Divine Instruments
column4: divine color]] is black, which symbolizes the night sky.<ref name=""P2V1C1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 2 Volume 1]]. Chapter 1: Attendants and the Fealty Ceremony</ref>

column1: For a very long time, the God of Darkness lived by himself. When he met the [[Goddess of Light]], they married and had four children: [[Flutrane]], the Goddess of Water; [[Leidenschaft]], the God of Fire; [[Schutzaria]], Goddess of Wind; and [[Geduldh]], Goddess of Earth.<ref name=""P1V3C18"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 1 Volume 3]]. Chapter 18: A Quiet Commotion</ref>
When the God of Life [[Ewigeliebe]] fell in love with Geduldh, the God of Darkness gladly consented to the marriage, hoping the two would fill the world with new life.
Unlike all the other gods below them, the names of the King and Queen gods are not known to mortals, and they are always referred to only by their title, even in prayers and within the [[Bible]].

The vast majority of people in Yurgenschmidt are not even aware of the names of the supreme gods and even those that are, will almost always use only their titles. Only archduke candidates are permitted to learn the names at all. This is not due to societal norms however, but appears to be part of the gods' own design. The one time an archnoble researcher managed to make an archduke candidate tell him the names of the king and queen gods, the archnoble was consumed by black and golden flames until nothing remained, and the archduke candidate lost his divine protections of light and darkness, unable to ever regain it, even when invoking the names of the gods, which ultimately led to him being demoted to archnoble status.
While the story might have been made up to justify the secrecy, the fact that their names are even omitted from the [[Bible#High Bishop's Bible
column2: High Bishop's Bibles]] gives it quite a bit of credence.

column1: Due to this incident, students are strictly warned against ever uttering the names when someone else might be listening, and even the ritual to learn them is held alone, without even a professor being present in the room. Due to everyone learning the names in such private ways and never talking with others about them, nobody really knows whether the ones they themselves know are the true, unchangeable names or something personalized for or interpreted by them.
The names of the God of Darkness and Goddess of Light are an absolute necessity to successfully use [[Large-scale Spells#Entwickeln
column2: Entwickeln]]. If only their titles are invoked, the structure with crumble back to dust within a couple of hours. Only with the names of the supreme gods can lasting structures be created. If everything is done correctly, the person performing the prayer will hear whispers and have the names appear in their minds with a blast of radiant fire, as if searing themselves directly into the brain. The ritual is very mana-intensive to the point that even [[Rozemyne
column3: Lady Rozemyne]] had to use two rejuvenation potions to provide the mana and to cope with the aftereffects.

column2: Commoners]] believe that the door to the land of the dead opens only at dawn, when the God of Darkness and the [[Goddess of Light]] meet. Epilogue</ref> For that reason, commoner funerals are held at night, and the loved ones of the deceased share stories about them until the next day when their spirits have moved on.

Chapter 22: Trombe Extermination</ref>

*'''Mana-Draining Haze:''' Conjures a black haze that drains mana from spells that touch it.<ref name=""P2V3C16"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 2 Volume 3]]. Chapter 16: Ambush</ref>

*'''The High Bishop's blessing''' Located at the very end of the High Bishop's bible, this blessing involves praying to all of the gods at once. It can only be used for another.<ref name=P4V9C14"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 9]]. Chapter 14: Separation</ref>

column1: '''Gretia''' (グレーティア, Gurētia) is an apprentice [[Nobility/Hierarchy#Mednoble
column2: med]][[attendant]]<ref name=""P5V14"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 5 Volume 1]]. Chapter 14: Gretia's Circumstances and Gathering Ingredients</ref> who serves as one of [[Rozemyne]]'s name-sworn<ref name=""P5V14"" /> retainers.

column1: Gretia's eyes are a pleasant shade of bluish green. Her hair is gray and usually worn in a single braid down her back, with bangs long enough to completely hide her eyes while she looks down. She generally wears very plain clothes, giving Rozemyne the vibes of a gloomy shut-in trying to avoid standing out. For a girl her age she has an unusually well developed chest.<ref name=""P5V14""/>
Gretia is exceptionally shy and timid for a noble of her rank. On her first interaction with Rozemyne she practically hides behind her class-mate [[Judithe]].<ref name=""P5V14""/>

The abuse of her brothers left deep scars on Gretia's soul, to the point where the mere presence of men near her is making her uncomfortable. As such she has a hard time dealing with Laurenz' joking and teasing, despite them being done in good nature and fun.<ref name=""P5V4C11""/>

Gretia was born in the temple to a secret romance of a blue priest and shrine maiden of mednoble descend. When her mother showed signs of her pregnancy their secret affair became public and she inquired about the possibility of her and her lover's families taking them back in so they could marry, but was only mocked for making a request so far above her station. Eventually her family did take her and her newborn daughter in, but considered her a disgrace and confined her to a side building. Before as a shrine maiden Gretia's mother received money and gifts, traveled around for rituals, was with the man she loved and had loyal gray priest attendants, but in the noble estate she was effectively a prisoner who only ever saw displeased guards, leading to some resentment toward her daughter and regular, mumbled complains about how much better her life was before giving birth to her daughter.
While living in the side building Gretia was brought up to become a servant. However when the [[Civil War#Political_Purge
column2: purge]] happened and the consequent mana crisis hit the duchy, her family tested Gretia's mana and found it of a suitable level for a mednoble. At her [[baptism]] she became the daughter of her uncle and his first wife. From the very beginning they were very clear about their intentions to marry her off for political gains and outright called her a tool to her face, never showing her even a trace of warmth or affection. Her brothers even went a step further refusing to even call her by her name and always calling her only ""temple girl"". When her womanly features began to set in, they upped their bullying by calling her a cow over her above average chest-size. All this neglect and verbal abuse has caused Gretia to actually look forward to the day when she would be married off, even if it was to a man old enough to be her father.

column1: When Gretia learned of the political purge of the former Veronica faction and how the children would be spared, even if the parents were put to death, she was secretly happy. The thought of being taken away from her abusive family and serving the compassionate Saint of Ehrenfest felt like the gods themselves had intervened and deliver her from her suffering. Having to [[Nobility#Name-Swearing
column2: give her name]] was a small price to pay for this salvation.<ref name=""P5V14""/>

column1: A day after the archducal couple visited the dormitory for a meeting with [[Hirschur
column3: Lord Wilfried]] informed the students of the current state of the purge. Only the five students who's parents were executed were still required to give their names, while the other children would be either able to return to their families right away, or live in the castle dormitory until the criminals finished their sentence of menial labour. While it is not yet clear whether Gretia's father will receive any punishment, he did escape the death sentence at least for now.

column1: Where the other children are greatly relieved about their family's survival, for Gretia comes as very unwelcome news, since it is pretty much the worst-case scenario for her. She had seen her father struggle with being unable to refuse the orders of those higher in the faction's hierarchy than him, form which she is sure that even though he was doing as he was told he was surely involved with a serious crime against the duchy. As the daughter of a convicted criminal any marriage prospects she might have had before would surely evaporate, resulting in her family most likely being ready to accept even the most desperate proposals which would only lead to more suffering for Gretia.

Seeing no other way to have even a chance at happiness Gretia approaches her class-mate Judithe to tell Lady Rozemyne that despite not being required to, she still wishes to give her name to her. Rozemyne is surprised about this and takes Gretia to a meeting room to hear her reasoning. There - under the privacy of [[Magic_Tools#Sound-blocking_Magic_Tool
column2: sound-blocking magic tools]] Gretia tells Rozemyne about her birth in the temple and her traumatic past. Even after Rozemyne tells her about what it means to be name-sworn and the demerits to be bound to her specifically, Gretia still wishes to go through with it. She had already done her research and even before talking to Rozemyne was well aware that she would be completely signing away her life to Rozemyne. But to Gretia signing her entire life away and even serving her for the rest of her life without ever getting married was preferable to returning to the neglect and abuse of her family. She wishes for nothing more than to be completely cut off from them, just like Rozemyne did for Roderick. Seeing the determination and desperation in her eyes, Rozemyne accepts.

column1: The next Earthday nearly the entire student body of Ehrenfest goes to the gathering spot together and Gretia is able to acquire all the materials she needs to make her name-swearing feystone.<ref name=""P5V14""/>

Soon after Gretia has finished her feystone and gives her name to Rozemyne. Despite the intense pain the ceremony causes Gretia merely grimaces for a bit, but doesn't even let a single grunt escape her lips, showing an exceptional tolerance for physical pain.<ref name=""P5V1C20"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 5 Volume 1]]. Chapter 20: Replies</ref>

Soon after they return home from the Royal Academy, Rozemyne enacts an experiment to see if the ritual for divine protection acquisition can be performed in the Ehrenfest Temple. She offers all her retainers the chance to participate and Gretia is one of those that accepts. Since at this point she has not yet hear of how Roderick became omni-elemental after giving his name to Rozemyne, she is greatly surprised when all the elemental symbols produce pillars of light during her own ritual. Though not nearly as surprised as she is when coming face-to-face with [[Bonifatius
column2: Lord Bonifatius]] upon exiting the chapel. To everyone's surprise the burly knight invited himself in to witness someone doing the ritual and to spare Gretia, Rozemyne reluctantly offered up Damuel to do this.

column1: Gretia is very grateful for not having to endure Bonifatius storming into the chapel during her own ritual and remarks that she wishes to thank Damuel. When Rozemyne replies that she could agree to marry Damuel, since he would surely be overjoyed by that, Gretia quickly declines, stating that she wishes to never marry anyone and rather serve Rozemyne for the rest of her life.
Apart from gaining all elements, Gretia is able to receive the divine protection of Verbergen, God of Concealment.<ref name=""P5V4C11""/>
*'''Mana Affinities:''' Gretia's natural affinities are currently now known, but she became omni-elemental from being name-sworn to Rozemyne.<ref name=""P5V4C11""/>
*'''Divine Protections:''' The only known divine protection of Gretia is of Verbergen, the God of Concealment.<ref name=""P5V4C11""/>

column1: Gundolf is a researcher through and through, with a near insatiable hunger for knowledge and discovery.

Much like his colleague [[Hirschur]], his laboratory is a mess with papers piled on any available surface. The only place that he keeps meticulously clean is the brewing area.<ref name=""P5V1C13"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 1]]. Chapter 13: Passing Professor Gundolf's Classes</ref>

Gundolf, like many nobles from Drewanchel, is a scholar and appears to be quite renowned. Even so, according to [[Anastasius]], [[Hirschur]] has made some breakthroughs that even Gundolf ""could make neither head nor tail of it."".<ref name=""P4V2S1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 2]]. Honest Courting</ref>

In his youth, Gundolf was an archduke candidate and took archduke courses at the Royal Academy.<ref name=""P4V6S2"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 6]]. Investigating the Former Werkestock Dormitory</ref>

To escape the pressure and constant distractions of the cutthroat politics among the archduke candidates of his home duchy, he arranged for himself to be adopted by an archnoble to lose his archduke candidate status shortly after his graduation, so he could dedicate himself to his research. Later, he became a professor at the Royal Academy.<ref name=""RAS1C15""/>
During Rozemyne's second year at the Royal Academy, Professor Gundolf during one of his lectures speaks very enthusiastically about the potentials of [[Plant Paper#Verification Paper
column2: Verification Paper]] that has only recently been invented and revealed by [[Ehrenfest (Duchy)
column3: Ehrenfest]] and used to facilitate inter-duchy trade. He is very eager to start researching this new invention, which he, as well as many other researchers from Drewanchel, presume to be a magic tool.

column2: Divine Protection Acquisition]]. The majority of students who pass the required [[Royal Academy/Curriculum#Theology 3
column3: theology]] exam, and thus are able to participate on the first day, are from Ehrenfest and Drewanchel.

column1: Upon seeing the lengthy prayer, [[Rozemyne]] and [[Wilfried]] point out how it is almost the same as prayers in the temple and the one they use to replenish their duchy's [[Large-scale Spells#Foundation Magic
column2: Foundation Magic]]. This surprises the other people present, since as [[Ortwin]] points out, in Drewanchel, they do not use a prayer for that, but just pour the mana in like they would with any magic tool. Before this can turn into an argument between Wilfried and Ortwin, Professor Hirschur steps in and tells them to discuss this ""research"" after class.

column1: Since they already know the majority of the prayer, Rozemyne and Wilfried finish memorizing it first, and consequently also enact their respective rituals before any other student, with Rozemyne going first. When Wilfried comes back, he announces that he managed to gain the protection of twelve gods, which naturally means he must have gained the protection of several subordinate gods in addition to primary deities. This causes quite a stir. As [[Hannelore]] of [[Dunkelfelger]] points out, it is very rare for any student to gain more than one protection per elemental affinity, and with the exception of those serving [[Leidenschaft]], subordinate gods rarely ever grant their blessing to students. The only one not surprised at her brother's success is Rozemyne herself, who states that based on what she read the likelihood of gaining the attention of a god depends on the person's deeds, and thus it is only natural for the pair to gain the protection of so many gods, without giving away how many she got.

The third person to finish memorizing the prayers is Ortwin, whom Gundolf accompanies into the chapel. To the boy's disappointment, however, he only manages to gain the protection of the primary gods he has aptitude for. Though he is far from alone in this, since all other non-Ehrenfest students, except for one, end up with the same results. Hannelore reports that she gained the protection of Angriff, the God of War, and Dregarnuhr, the Goddess of Time, albeit she is very confused how she could possibly have gained the attention of either. Once Hannelore leaves the hall, only Ehrenfest students remain, since their med- and laynobles chose to not step forward when they memorized their prayer and instead decided to wait until all those of higher ranked duchies and higher status had finished their rituals to avoid their ire, despite having no actual obligation to do so. By unspoken agreement, they enact their rituals in order of social rank, with the exception of the mednoble [[Roderick]], who chooses to go last.

The first four finish theirs without any issue and got the expected outcome of gaining one protection per element they have. [[Philine]], however, comes running back from the chapel, so overjoyed that she entirely drops her noble façade and happily tells Lady Rozemyne that she gains the protection of [[Mestionora]] the Goddess of Wisdom, despite not even having an affinity for wind or the protection of [[Schutzaria]]. This greatly intrigues Gundolf, and he unleashes a torrent of questions, under which the laynoble girl wilts. This causes Rozemyne to step in and make the professor ease up on her. Philine tries her best to answer all of Gundolf's questions and lays out how hard she worked on transcribing books for Lady Rozemyne, making translations of ancient writings into modern vernacular and her work as an apprentice scholar, but Gundolf is unable to pinpoint any significant difference between what she did and the students of his own duchy.

Before he can finish his questioning, Roderick returns and reports that he somehow gained the protection of all seven major gods. This outright shocks Gundolf. At no point in recorded history did any student with just two elemental affinities manage to become omni-elemental through this ritual, and thus it was thought entirely impossible up to now. Unfortunately, neither the professor nor Roderick himself seem to have even the slightest clue as to how this happened, so questioning him appears to be a rather fruitless endeavor. At Rozemyne's urging, Gunfolf congratulates the students and gives them leave. Before they move out, Professor Hirschur cautions them to not tell anyone about Roderick's success, since it is such a great outlier it could potentially throw the entire Royal Academy into chaos.<ref name=""P5V1C6"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 1]]. Chapter 6: Music and Everyone’s Rituals</ref>

A few days later, Gundolf is contacted by Rozemyne. Due to prioritizing her archduke candidate lessons, Rozemyne was unable to attend the initial scholar's course lessons and thus has to personally schedule appointments for her exams. While Rozemyne brews the required potions in Gundolf's lab, the two talk. Gundolf learns of Ehrenfest's research into divine protection and their cooperation with Dunkelfelger on the issue, but is unable to gain much information from Rozemyne, since the royal family is also involved. Gundolf also tries to headhunt Rozemyne for his own laboratory, but she refuses and sticks with Hirschur. She does however indicate a willingness to cooperate with Drewanchel on the research of magic tool paper, in particular a search for alternative methods of creation that do not come from feybeasts, an idea that fascinates Gundolf. In the course of their discussions, the professor learns that Rozemyne is currently trying to do all the research she comes up with all by herself. He advises her to concentrate on the sensitive parts and topics of particular personal interest, and to delegate the rest to the other scholars of her duchy, so the entire duchy can benefit from her pursuits. The Ehrenfest girl also inquires about access to documents pertaining to the old curriculum, from the times before the schtappe was acquired in the first year.

Despite the wealth of discussions they had on the side, Rozemyne is able to pass all three of her exams with flying colours.<ref name=""P5V1C13"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 1]]. Chapter 13: Passing Professor Gundolf's Classes</ref>

column1: '''Gunther''' (ギュンター, ''Gyuntaa'') is the father of [[Myne]], [[Tuuli]], and [[Kamil]], husband of [[Effa]], and head of [[Myne's Family
column2: Myne's family]]. He worked as a captain for the [[City of Ehrenfest
column3: Ehrenfest]]'s city gate, but was promoted to gate commander, shortly after the birth of his son, and was in charge of the northern gate.<ref name=""P4V4S2"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 4]]. Preventing Destructive Reconstruction</ref>

column1: He moves to [[Alexandria]] with his family, the Gutenbergs, and Merchants as they set up their new home at the end of the series.

Gunther has blue hair and light brown eyes. [[Myne]] initially describes him as a ""mean-looking, muscular guy"" who is very strong thanks to his work as a soldier.<ref name=""P1V1C2"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 1 Volume 1]]. Chapter 2: Exploring My Home</ref> His work uniform consists of a blue tunic.

Gunther is a doting and devoted father and loves to talk about his family, especially about his daughters to anyone who will listen. He is quite aggressive if his family is threatened and will put himself at risk to defend them. This is shown among other times when defending Myne against the [[Bezewanst
column2: High Bishop]] twice, even though he knows that attacking a noble would cost him his life. Gunther is described as being like a child, that can't tell reality and dream apart. He charges head-on without considering his surroundings or consequences, and feels frustrated if he doesn't reach his goal.

column1: He easily gets jealous or pouty when his daughters praise other men in his presence without also praising him, but is easily put back into a good mood once they acknowledge his ""greatness.""
His greatest treasure is his family, and he became a soldier to protect them.

When Myne started to learn her letters from [[Otto]], Gunther also started to secretly study to maintain his pride as a father.<ref name=""FB2S2"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Fanbook 2]]. I'm Not Givin' Up My Daughter!</ref>

Gunther is the son of a woodworker and dreamed of becoming a knight after listening to minstrel tales of knights. He didn't give up his dream and became a soldier who protected his city. He applied for apprenticeship at the gate, asking the commander, who was also Effa's father, and was accepted.

When he first met [[Effa]], he fell in love with her at first sight and would visit her every single day at her home and ask her father for her hand in marriage. Thanks to Gunther's passion, his marriage proposal was consented, if Effa wanted to marry him. Eventually, he won Effa over by proposing like a knight would. He knelt in front of Effa and offered a [[feystone
column2: magic stone]] he acquired after slaying a [[feybeast]]. He said: ""I became a soldier because I genuinely want to protect this city and my family. You didn't laugh at that, Effa, and I love you for it. I want you by my side.""<ref>''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 1 Volume 2]]. Gossiping by the Well</ref>

column1: During his work, he became well acquainted with the traveling merchant [[Otto]]. When Otto out of the blue bought his citizenship in Ehrenfest and needed a job to propose to his crush [[Corinna]], Gunther introduced him to the gate commander, and Otto was hired as a soldier, so they had someone competent to do all the paperwork.
By the time Myne reached five years old, his dedicated service has earned him the position of Captain, the second in command at his local post.

The teams guarding each gate get relocated in regular intervals. At the start of the story, Gunther is guarding the southern gate and thus often sees and interacts with the children going out to forage in the forest.
*'''Carving:''' While not quite on the level of a professional craftsman, Gunther is still quite talented in woodworking.
*'''Combat:''' As a soldier, Gunther is well-trained in hand-to-hand combat. He was able to take down multiple grey priests singlehandedly, and even fight weaker [[Devouring]] soldiers head on.

*When [[Justus]] is seeking information about Myne from the soldiers at the gate where Gunther works, he was warned off by the soldiers not to bring up Gunther's daughters with Gunther, as he would talk your ear off about them to you.

*Effa thinks Gunther is at fault for how Myne behaves. In fact, they are similar in the way that both of them will charge head on towards their goals while disregarding everything else, and will protect their loved ones without hesitation, even when faced against overwhelming odds.

column1: '''Gustav''' (グスタフ ''Gusutafu'') is the head of the [[Othmar Company]] and is the guildmaster of [[Ehrenfest]]'s [[Merchant's_Guild
column2: Merchant's Guild]]. Once he becomes aware of [[Myne]] and the products that she keeps coming up with, he keeps trying to poach her for his own store.

column1: He dotes on his granddaughter [[Freida]] and after learning that she has the [[Devouring]], he arranges a contract with the laynoble [[Henrik]] for her to save her life. He carefully selected Freida's partner.

The guildmaster is described as looking around his fifties, with broad shoulders. Though his normal appearance is that of a kind, albeit older man, his merchant mode is far scarier. He is described as usually wearing a smile.

Gustav is a conniving man with an instinct for profit. He is not above manipulation to get what he wants. He has a terrible aptitude for personal affairs though, and though he means well, tends to antagonize rather than support, especially in Benno's case.
Gustav has a mindset oriented towards the greater good of the [[City of Ehrenfest]], prioritizing the stability between nobles and the lower city and taking care of its economic prosperity.

He and [[Benno]] have a fairly long-lived rivalry and don't get along well, although they do understand each other quite well. When Benno's father died, he offered to marry Benno's mother directly after his death. As Benno's mother married the person she loved, Gustav earned the whole family's hatred and starting the feud between Benno's and his family. After Benno's mother died shortly following her husband, Benno became the sole adult and took over the Gilberta Company. Benno just came of age and was therefore an inexperienced young man. Gustav didn't want to see the Gilberta Company and new hard-working talents crumbling down and offered his daughters for marriage to Benno, after Benno's fiancée Liz died. Benno, who loved Liz, was furious, deepening his hatred for Gustav. Later, Gustav offered his sons to Benno's sisters for marriage later. They all declined leaving Gustav perplexed to why all his well-meant offers were declined. Reaching present day, Gustav still hasn't understood the hostility directed at him from Benno and his family.
*Gustav introduced his name during his debut in the anime. However in the light novel, [[Rozemyne]] never knew his name until the [[Italian Restaurant]] trip in [[Part 3 Volume 1]].

column1: '''Hannelore''' (ハンネローレ, ''Hanneroore'') is an archduke candidate from [[Dunkelfelger]] and [[Lestilaut]]'s younger sister.
She is the main character of the spinoff novel series ''[[Hannelore's Fifth Year at the Royal Academy]]'' that takes place after the events of [[Part 5 Volume 12]].

Hannelore is a rather quiet looking girl with light-pink, almost purple hair that she usually wears in two tails. Her eyes are a vibrant shade of red almost exactly like that of a [[Feystone#Proposal Feystone
column2: proposal feystone]] dyed by someone born in winter. She is small for her age, though still taller than Rozemyne.<ref name=""P4V3C11"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 3]]. Chapter 11: The Tea Party for All Duchies</ref>

column1: Due to being reprimanded often during her strict upbringing, Hannelore is shy, timid, and unconfident. When it comes to people relationships, she is constantly worrying about whether she has caused displeasure in other people, making her appear hesitant and apologetic. She is nervous around large gatherings of people, and often laments about her poor timing and her brother Lestilaut's tendency of dragging her into trouble.

She didn't cared much about books previously because books in Dunkelfelger are mostly written in ancient texts and are tough to read, but came to love reading after getting introduced to Ehrenfest books. As such, she can become quite animated when discussing books with [[Rozemyne]].
As relatives of [[Trauerqual]]'s third wife [[Magdalena]], Hannelore and her brother [[Lestilaut]] occasionally visited her and her son [[Hildebrand
column2: Prince Hildebrand]] at their royal villa in the [[Sovereignty]], but didn't form a particularly close relationship with the prince.<ref name=""P4V5E"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 5]]. Epilogue</ref>

column1: In the past, Hannelore didn't care too much for books. But this changed when [[Rozemyne
column3: Ehrenfest]] lent her a book. Unlike the stories popular in Dunkelfelger, which tend to be written in euphemism-heavy, old, and difficult to read dialects, the book Rozemyne lent her was written in modern vernacular and both easy and fun to read. It also fit the young girl's taste for romance much closer than the popular Dunkelfelger literature which is almost exclusively about fighting in some form or the other. This awakened Hannelore to the joy of reading and made her eager to read more Ehrenfest books.<ref name=""P4V7P"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 7]]. Prologue</ref>

She also has the protection of Angriff, the God of War, and Dregarnuhr, the Goddess of Time. *Due to her red eyes, twin-tail hairstyle, small stature and timid behavior, Rozemyne thought she looks like a rabbit. Interestingly, Rozemyne herself was said to resemble [[Shumil
column2: shumils]], a feybeast species that look very similar to rabbits.

column1: * A running gag with Hannelore is that she is always unfortunate with timing, so much that she's often praying or complaining to Dregarnuhr, the goddess of time. As a result, she obtained Dregarnuhr's divine protection.

*Among all characters introduced, Hannelore is one of the only two female nobles that tie their hair into two tails, the other being [[Philine]]. Coincidentally, both of them are shy book lovers that Rozemyne quickly became fond of.

**She is also similar to [[Freida]] in hairstyle and was someone with slightly higher status than Myne/Rozemyne when they first met, but she achieved something Freida couldn't -- becoming Rozemyne's best friend.

*Privately Rozemyne thinks of Hannelore as ""quiet and fluffy"", but also a capable archduke candidate.<ref name=""P4V6C18"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 6]]. Chapter 18: A Tea Party of Bookworms</ref>
*Hannelore is the third person that Rozemyne described as an angel internally, after [[Tuuli]] and [[Charlotte]].

column1: Hartmut has amber (sometimes called “orange”) eyes and noticeable red hair. He smiles frequently and has a bright, peaceful expression. Rozemyne remarks that his way of speaking makes him sound exactly like [[Justus]].<ref name=""P4V1C8"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 1]]. Chapter 8: The Better Grades Committee</ref> He is about 175 cm (5’9”) tall.<ref name=""FB2"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Fanbook 2]]. Character Design Sheets</ref>

Hartmut gives the impression of a friendly young man who loves talking to people and is quite good at gathering information.<ref name=""P4V1C7"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 1]]. Chapter 7: My Retainers and Entering the Dormitory</ref> Internally, he is more cynical and calculating than he appears.

Prior to becoming Rozemyne's retainer, his uncle described him as ""exceedingly uncaring"" and ""infinitely stubborn."" When he hears Rozemyne describing Hartmut as open-minded, he is surprised to the point of shock. Seeing the once uncaring boy being so devoted has become both a heartwarming sight, but also a point of worry for his family.<ref name=""P4V5C11"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 5]]. Chapter 11: Groschel and the Harvest Festival</ref> He is devoted to [[Rozemyne]] and praises her effusively to anyone who will listen, to the point where her other retainers are often exasperated by his rambling speeches.

Despite his eccentric attitude, Hartmut is exceedingly competent and has high standards for both himself and others. He judges other people primarily based on how useful they are (or aren’t) to Rozemyne, and is willing to do whatever he can to most effectively support her. He has shown a surprising willingness to treat commoners and [[Temple_Hierarchy#Gray_Priest
column2: grey priests]] respectfully and even allow them to teach him. This attitude is very much out of the ordinary among nobles in general, and archnobles in particular.<ref name=""P4V5C11"" />

column1: Hartmut was born the youngest<ref name=""P4V1C7""/> of [[Ottilie]] and [[Leberecht
column2: Leberecht’s]] three.<ref name=""FB2FamilyTree"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Fanbook 2]]. Noble Family Tree</ref> sons. His family is part of the [[Ehrenfest (Duchy)#Leisegang Faction
column3: Leisegang political faction]]. Due to his mother being a friend of [[Elvira]], he and [[Cornelius]] spent a lot of time together as children. Before becoming a retainer, he worked under his uncle, who is also an archnoble scholar.<ref name=""P4V5C10"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 5]]. Chapter 10: Post-Competition and the Harvest Festival</ref>

column1: When Hartmut entered the [[Royal Academy]], he quickly became aware of his duchy's unfavourable position in the country. The victorious faction of the civil war distrusted and looked down on Ehrenfest for staying neutral, rather than helping whom they view as the legitimate Zent, and the losing faction resented them for rising in the ranks solely due to circumstance with no merit of their own, resulting in Ehrenfest having virtually no influence at all. In light of this big picture, he became painfully aware how insignificant and stupid the faction squabbling within their backwater duchy truly was, killing off any motivation he might once have had and reducing all his efforts to merely doing what was expected of someone of his status. Likewise, he lacked even the slightest urge to serve any of the short-sighted and ignorant Ehrenfest nobles, so caught up in their own little power-struggles they failed to notice how insignificant their entire duchy was right now.<ref name=""SSC1C8"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Short Story Collection 1]]. Chapter 8: Hartmut — That Fateful Ceremony</ref>
Upon learning of Rozemyne's existence he quickly deduced that she couldn't be [[Elvira
column2: Lady Elvira]]'s daughter and thus must be the daughter of [[Karstedt
column3: Lord Karstedt]]'s second or third wife, meaning she was of mednoble stock. His mother being asked to serve a girl from such low status dismayed Hartmut, who perceived it as an insult to his family's status.<ref name=""SSC1C8""/> However, after seeing [[Rozemyne]] give a [[blessing]] to the crowd at her noble [[baptism]], Hartmut was deeply moved. He became convinced that she was a true saint and someone worthy of being the next [[Aub Ehrenfest]].<ref name=""P4V1C10"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 1]]. Chapter 10: Royalty and Nobles from Other Duchies</ref>

column1: When Hartmut heard that [[Wilfried]] committed the crime of entering the Ivory Tower, he told his mother that Rozemyne should have used the opportunity to cement her position as the next archduchess. Ottilie replied that Rozemyne thought “only of raising others up, not dragging them down” and advised him to support her in positive ways instead. Hartmut accordingly devoted himself to spreading the legends of her sainthood to as many people as possible.<ref name=""P4V1C10""/>

During the time Rozemyne spent unconscious in the [[jureve]], Hartmut sharply criticized Cornelius and her guard knights for letting her be harmed.<ref name=""P4V2S2"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 2]]. Life without One’s Lady</ref> He also gathered information at the [[Royal Academy]] in accordance with Rozemyne’s instructions, focusing on interduchy relations. [[Ferdinand]] was especially satisfied with his work.

*'''Mana Affinities:''' Hartmut has a natural affinity for Light,<ref name=""P4V2C7"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 2]]. Chapter 7: Measuring Schwartz and Weiss</ref> Fire, Wind and likely Earth from his birth season, though this is so far unconfirmed. He also gained an affinity for Life via divine protection of subordinate gods.<ref name=""P5V4C11""/> He lacks a natural affinity for Darkness.<ref name=""P4V2C7""/> When Rozemyne accepts his name, he becomes omni-elemental through the name-swearing.<ref name=""P5V6C4""/>

*'''Divine Protections:''' Hartmut has the divine protections of the [[Goddess of Light]], [[Leidenschaft]] and [[Schutzaria]], as well as the subordinate gods Gebordnung, Anwachs, Ordoschnelli, Dauerleben and Schlaftraum.<ref name=""P5V4C11""/>
*'''Magecraft:''' As an apprentice [[scholar]], Hartmut has studied [[Magic#Magic Circles
column2: magic circles]], magic tools, and potions. He earned very good grades in his class on magic circles.<ref name=""P4V2C7""/>

column1: *'''Intelligence Work:''' Hartmut is gifted at gathering information, to the extent that even [[Ferdinand]] offers him a position as his retainer.<ref name=""P4V3C15"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 3]]. Chapter 15: Buying Information and the Mana Compression Lecture</ref> He is also skilled at spreading rumors and misinformation to improve [[Ehrenfest (Duchy)

*'''Education:''' A good (albeit strict) teacher, Hartmut frequently delegates tasks to the younger apprentice scholars, corrects their errors, and coaches them on how to respond to queries from other duchies.
*'''Commoner Communication:''' Unlike many other nobles, Hartmut is well capable of communicating with commoners, even those that have not been taught how to talk to nobles.

*Hartmut is a distant blood relative of [[Rozemyne]] and several of her other retainers, including [[Leonore]], [[Brunhilde]], [[Cornelius]], and [[Traugott]]<ref name=""FB2FamilyTree""/>, all of whom are descendants of important [[Ehrenfest (Duchy)#Leisegang Faction
column2: Liesegang faction]] members. In fact, [[Previous Count Leisegang]] is their great-grandfather.

column3: central district]]. His name was never mentioned.

column1: Hasse's Mayor was a very arrogant man with little respect to anyone who didn't futher his own goals.

column2: former High Bishop]] being unable to use a [[highbeast]] he travelled by coach and thus often stopped in [[Hasse]] on his way to other places. During these many visits the mayor managed to ingratiate himself to the Bezewanst through gifts of ""flowers and fruits"" (i.e. women and alcohol) as well as other bribes.

column1: This connection with the High Bishop made the mayor think of himself as nearly untouchable, leading him to be arrogant not just to his citizens, but also to visiting merchants and even the occasional noble.
The orphans under his supervision were treated very poorly, were overworked, and still had to get the majority of their food by foraging in the forest. If they disobeyed he beat them.
The first [[Rozemyne]] hears about the mayor is when the [[Gilberta Company]] and [[Gil]], accompanied by tax officials including [[Kantna
column2: Lord Kantna]] are sent out to investigate potential places for new orphanages and workshops outside of [[City of Ehrenfest
column3: Ehrenfest City]]. Unaware of Bezewanst's demise, Hasse's mayor is very uncooperative and exceptionally rude to Benno, believing that his connection to the High Priest will shield him from any consequence for his actions. During this visit the mayor signs a contract with Kantna over the sale of the orphan girl [[Nora]].

column1: [[Rozemyne]] and [[Ferdinand]] go to visit the monastery and the mayor, and wish to see the orphans to inform them of the monastery. The Mayor has concealed a few, namely the ones he wanted to sell, but [[Rozemyne]] forces him to reveal them. Four orphans decide to go with her: [[Marthe]], [[Rick]], [[Thore]], and [[Nora]]. This leaves the mayor with no goods to sell, and once [[Rozemyne]] and [[Ferdinand]] are gone, he attacks the monastery to get the orphans back, inadvertently committing treason. [[Ferdinand]] tasks [[Rozemyne]] with punishing the city and securing a successor to the mayor.

[[Rozemyne]], after meeting with [[Benno]] decides to spread rumors through the merchants to spread unease and to turn the town against him. [[Rozemyne]] is able to lessen the punishment from complete destruction of the town to the execution of only the mayor and the people of his faction who failed to accept that what they did was wrong, to ten years of increased taxes and not receiving any mana for the next [[Spring Prayer]], which will significantly reduce the following harvest.

When confronted by the nobles the mayor tries to plead for mercy, but Rozemyne is able to maneuver him to in essence argue for his own punishment by asking him how he would tread orphans if they unknowingly attacked his family, to which the mayor passionately argues that such a crime would require harsh punishment and that not even ignorance would protect them, thus sealing his own fate with the added effect of turning even those villages who were convinced he didn't deserve the death penalty prior against him.

To make sure that the seed of rebellion was entirely quashed, [[Ferdinand]] uses a shield of [[Schutzaria]] and orders all the citizens of Hasse and the surrounding villages to attempt to pass through it, calling it the ""Door of Judgement"". While the vast majority of the citizens are able to pass through without resistance, the mayor and six others are knocked away by the winds of the shield due to harboring ill intent, at which point [[Eckhart]] restrains them with [[Schtappe#Bands of Light
column2: magical bands of light]].<ref name=""P3V3C15"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 3]]. Chapter 15: The Door of Judgement</ref>

column1: Following this clear display of his guilt, the mayor and his compatriots are executed with a [[Large-scale_Spells#Execution_Magic
column2: rare form of magic]] only taught to archduke candidates and reserved for only the worst of crimes. It turns them slowly to stone from the feet up and then makes the statues crumble to dust, denying them even a funeral.<ref name=""P3V3C16"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 3]]. Chapter 16: The Execution</ref>

column1: At first glance, Hassheit appears to be a genial young man with a bright smile. However, his eyes show no kindness.<ref name=""P3V4S2""/>

An ambitious and opportunistic nobleman, Hassheit has no compunctions about using his marriage to Brigitte for political gain. He also has a vindictive streak and took satisfaction in ruining her reputation after she broke off their engagement. In public, he appears poised and is a persuasive speaker, using elegant language to undermine and mock his adversaries.<ref name=""P3V4S2""/>
Hassheit and Brigitte were engaged to be married. During the engagement her father died and the post of Giebe Illgner passed to her [[Helfried
column2: older brother]]. Her brother was still quite young for such a responsibility and is a poor negotiator.

column1: Hassheit and his family thought to use the weakness and inexperience of the new giebe to their advantage to take over the province for themselves, even going so far as to plan to kill him once the marriage put them into the succession for the title. When Brigitte found this out, she immediately cancelled the engagement with no regards to the societal norms or consequences. This kind of behaviour is unbefitting of a noble of her station and resulted in grave consequences for her and her province, leading the majority of the local nobles to abondon Illgner and move to other provinces.

Brigitte had to endure mocking from higher and equal-ranking nobles and whispering behind her backs from laynobles ever since, on top of the harrassment by Hassheit and his family.<ref name=""P3V1C10"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 3 Volume 1]]. Chapter 10: Starbind Ceremony in the Noble's Quarter</ref>
After hearing about Brigitte's circumstances, [[Rozemyne]] creates a [[Inventions#Halter-Top Dress
column2: new dress]] that flatters her body type more than the current fashion, hoping it will help her win a new fiancé in spite of her damaged reputation.<ref name=""P3V3C13"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 3 Volume 3]]. Chapter 13: Upcoming Spring Prayer</ref> The dress proves a resounding success, and, combined with Brigitte's newfound political backing from Rozemyne and [[Elvira]], serves to draw the attention of many eligible young noblemen at the [[Starbind Ceremony#Noble Starbinding

column1: Hassheit takes the opportunity to ask Brigitte to once again accept his proposal. While painting himself as the victim of their broken engagement, he uses elegant [[Noble Euphemisms
column2: euphemisms]] to insult Brigitte and Illgner. He implies, among other things, that she is a fool for breaking their engagement and that if she turns him down again, she will never find another man willing to take her.

column1: However, [[Damuel]] and his friends intervene to cut off Hassheit's insults. Although Hassheit tells him to ""know his place,"" Damuel instead proposes to Brigitte, promising to raise his [[mana]] capacity to equal that of a [[Nobility/Hierarchy#Mednoble
column2: mednoble]] within a year.<ref name=""P3V4S2""/> Although Brigitte initially believes he only wants to help her save face, uses the opportunity to spurn Hassheit's proposal and express her intention never to see him again. With Elvira observing the proceedings, Hassheit has little choice but to accept his loss and move on.

[[Part 5 Volume 6]]. Chapter 7: Preparing Fey Paper</ref>

This put him in a state of mind, where he was fully willing to lay down his life to assassinate Veronica for what she did to his family and the torment she visited upon Ferdinand, but his lord managed to reign him in.

She was a Leisegang-aligned noble on very bad terms with [[Veronica]]. At the time her house was being taken over by a [[Veronica]]-loyal second wife, she just joined the [[Royal Academy]]. She socialized with Eckhart from a young age and felt comfortable confiding to him of her situation. Justus recommended Eckhart become a retainer, and Heidiemarie soon followed. At the beginning, Ferdinand only thought of her as an ""extra"" with Eckhart, but when she competed with the others over how useful they could be, Ferdinand starting taking her seriously. She never gave Ferdinand her name.<ref name=""FB6QA>''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]].'' [[Fanbook 6]]. Q&A with Miya Kazuki</ref>

column1: Heidi (ハイディ ''Haidi'') is a [[Honorary Titles#Gutenberg (Title)

Heidi appears young for her age, and when [[Myne]] met Heidi, she assumed Heidi had just come of age, even though she is over 20 years old<ref name=""P2V4C4"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 2 Volume 4]]. Chapter 4: The Ink Guild and Succession</ref>. She has reddish-brown hair that is tied into a single braid and twisted into a bun and grey eyes that are filled with curiosity.

Myne comments that she thinks Heidi is ""funny and hard working, but kind of weird""<ref name=""P2V4C4""/> to which [[Lutz]] replies ""... You are one to talk."" [[Benno]] also tells Lutz that he now has two Mynes to look after, showing that everyone who knows both of them think they are alike.
Heidi is focused on ink and is very curious to find out why the ink colour changes when making it, rather than finding out how to make more colours.

While she is focused on discovering new ink, she does think about the future and her husband. This is shown when she asks her husband, Josef, to get his [[beruf]] certification once the work with coloured ink was completed<ref name=""P2V4S7"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 2 Volume 4]]. Josef - Beruf Certification</ref>. She hurried the research and worried about the research to lessen his burden and support him.
Heidi is the daughter of an ink maker, [[Bierce]], and joined his ink workshop when she was [[Baptism
column2: baptised]]. During her apprenticeship, another apprentice was told to look after for her<ref name=""P2V4AW"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 2 Volume 4]]. Afterword</ref>. This apprentice was [[Josef]], who ended up marrying her.

column1: [[Josef]] is Heidi's husband. Heidi is well aware of her own limitations, and supports and listens to her husband, doing her best to help him get a beruf certification, so he can become a foreman in place of her.
[[Myne]] is Heidi's patron. She also gave her research money, asking for the development of colored ink, and then gave them a title: [[Honorary Titles#Gutenberg (Title)
Lady [[Rozemyne]] is Heidi's patron, picking up where Myne left off.

column1: Made a deal with [[Tollkuehnheit]] to send one high mana individual back to [[Lanzenave]]. Founder of [[Royal Academy#Adalgisa Villa
The country of Lanzenave came into being about 400 years ago. Shortly before it's founding, Yurgenschmidt was ruled by [[Aeussewahl
column2: Zent Aeussewahl]] and three of his sons managed to obtain a Grutrissheit. Ultimately [[Aeussewahl]] chose his son [[Heileind]] as his successor. Unable to accept being passed over, his brother [[Tollkuehnheit]] took his magic tool and went looking for a new land to settle. Accompanied by his wife and retainers, he sailed through the southern country gate and eventually happened across an inhabited land, with a comparatively poor population, unable to use any magic. While the area didn't appear to be rich in any valuable natural resources, it was able to sustain the local population, which was good enough for [[Tollkuehnheit]]. He used his [[Grutrissheit]] to create a duchy foundation and raise an entire ivory city before the eyes of the stunned locals. Having never seen any magic of this scale, or potentially any magic at all, this awed the locals so much that many of them took to worshipping Tollkühnheit as an emissary from the land of gods, making it easy for him to crown himself the king of this new land and crism it [[Lanzenave]].

column1: Due to the mana disparity of the newly arrived nobles and the indigenous people, interbreeding was essentially impossible. Furthermore, since his [[Grutrissheit]] was only a duplicate, which he created with his [[schtappe]], rather than a physical transcription, he couldn't hope to pass it down to any of his children and it would disappear along with him upon his death. To make matters even worse, without a schtappe, no one could fully maintain the city's foundation magic either, once he was gone, meaning that not just the Grutrissheit, but the entire city would be lost, if he couldn't find a solution.

He petitioned his brother, now the Zent of [[Yurgenschmidt]], to give one of his children a [[schtappe]], but due to it being impossible for people not registered as Yurgenschmidt nobles to receive one, the Zent had to decline. Instead the two monarchs hammered out an agreement to sent a princess of [[Lanzenave]] to Yurgenschmidt, where she would conceive children from the local nobility, who would then be raised as Yurgenschmidt nobles, including going to the [[Royal Academy]] and obtaining a schtappe. However, [[Heileind
column2: Zent Heileind]] was concerned that, if all the children were allowed to leave the country after their coming-of-age, their neighbor might become too powerful and threaten his own country one day, so he only agreed to send a single child - regardless of gender - each generation to Lanzenave. Due to practical reasons, primarily involving the effects of pregnancy, the first couple of children thus chosen, were all male, until it became tradition to always receive a male heir.<ref name=""P5V6S1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 6]]. The Lanzenave Envoys</ref>

column1: '''Heisshitze''' (ハイスヒッツェ, Haisuhittze) is a knight from [[Dunkelfelger]] who's [[Royal Academy]] education overlapped with [[Ferdinand]]'s.<ref name=""P4V7C12"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 4 Volume 7]]. Interduchy Tournament (Second Year)</ref>

Befitting his position as a Dunkelfelger knight, Heisshitze is hot-blooded and ditter-hungry. He is extremely persistent, insisting to challenge Ferdinand for years despite Ferdinand being very reluctant and turning him down repeatedly.

While not entirely rash, he tends to go with his emotions rather than pragmatism. He usually has good intentions, but appears to be rather naïve in his views, often acting on what he thinks is right even when lacking crucial information. As a result, he unintentionally make things worse for the person he wants to aid.

As long as his goals do not negatively affects his home, he puts his personal feelings above the benefit for his duchy.<ref name=""P4V8S1"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 4 Volume 8]]. Clearing Regrets from Ten Years Ago</ref>

At some point of their shared time at the royal academy, Heisshitze wagered his cape in a competition against Ferdinand and lost. During the remainder of their time at the academy he challenged Ferdinand at every opportunity to regain his cape, but was never able to beat his rival.<ref name=""P4V7C12""/>

While Ferdinand does not appear to reciprocate the feelings, many Dunkelfelgerians consider Heisshitze and Ferdinand to be ""frenemies"". With Heisshitze himself being convinced that playing ditter against each other can bring even the worst enemies together in friendship over time, it seems clear he shares this view. As such he holds Ferdinand in high regards in more ways than just as a rival to strive against.
During their time in the academy Heisshitze and several other Dunkelfelger knights made it their goal to rescure Ferdinand from the abuse he suffered from [[Veronica
column2: Lady Veronica]] and her faction. To this end they pressured their Aub to arrange a marriage between Ferdinand and [[Magdalena]], without getting her consent. This infuriated Magdalena who was already in love with [[Trauerqual]] the fifth prince. Aub Dunkelfelger eventually gave in to the pressure, but before any official arrangements between Dunkelfelger and [[Ehrenfest]] could be made, Magdalena managed to secure her betrothal to her beloved on her own, dashing the efforts of the knights.<ref name=""P4V8S1""/>

column1: At some point after his graduation Heisshitze married the younger sister of his uncle's wife, who have a considerable age-gap between them. Due to how close he is with the Commanders second son, their in-law relationship of uncle and nephew seems to take precedence over their biological connection as cousins.

At the [[Interduchy Tournament]] in [[Rozemyne]] and [[Hannelore]]'s second year at the royal academy, Aub Dunkelfelger challenges Ehrenfest to a [[Ditter]] match over the publishing rights for a manuscript that Lady Rozemyne - [[Sylvester
column2: Aub Ehrenfest]]'s adopted daughter - had made by translating a borrowed Dunkelfelger book into modern language. When Aub Ehrenfest and Rozemyne are unable to dissuade Aub Dunkelfelger from this and find other ways to handle the publishing rights, Aub Ehrenfest reluctantly agrees, but suggests to make it a very small scale affair between only one champion of each duchy.

column1: Aub Dunkelfelger accepts those turns and requests for Ehrenfest to declare Ferdinand as their champion. Ferdinand is very opposed to participating, but Heisshitze manages to convince him to join by wagering several valuable materials. Being able to convince Ferdinand also earns him the approval of Aub Dunkelfelger and thus the right to fight as Dunkelfelger's champion against Ferdinand and thus the chance to win back his old cape.
At Heisshitze's suggestion, Hannelore and Rozemyne are chosen as the treasures in their ditter match, much to the two girls' surprise, confusion and dismay.<ref name=""P4V7C12""/>

Meeting his old rival Ferdinand again at the interduchy tournament reinvigorates Heisshitzes passion for ""rescueing"" him from his duchy. Without bothering to gather information or talk to Ferdinand he assumes that him remaining in the temple can only mean that he is still mistreated. Together with many other Dunkelfelger knights he once again pleads with Aub Dunkelfelger to find a woman for Ferdinand so he can marry into another duchy and be free of the abuse they believe he has to suffer in his home. Initially their passioned please are argued down by [[Sieglinde
column2: Lady Sieglinde]] since she sees no benefit for Dunkelfelger in it.

column1: After discussing the matter further among themselves the knights come up with ways they can achieve their goal and benefit their duchy at the same time, securint the support of the Aub and his first wife who then go on to support [[Gieselfried

column1: Prince Hildebrand has mainly silver hair, with a slight tinge of blue and bright purple hair.<ref name=""P4V5C18"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 5]]. Chapter 18: The Second-Year Fellowship Gathering</ref>

Hildebrand appears to be rather lonely, on account of having spent the entirety of his life nearly entirely isolated in royal villas. The prospect of going to new places and meeting new people greatly excites him, though as a member of the royal family, he has been well trained to not openly show his emotions. Being just seven years old, he still lets this royal facade slip sometimes, but generally manages to contain his emotions when not in private with just family members and his own retainers present.

Due to the near complete lack of interactions with anyone who isn't either related to him or a servant, Prince Hildebrand has a very tenuous grasp of politics and his own powers. He often feels that his mother and even his own retainers have more power than he himself, despite being told otherwise.

As the child of the third wife of his father, Hildebrand grew up never leaving the royal villa of his mother even once prior to his [[baptism]]. The only people he ever met in the first seven years of his life were family members and servants. His baptism was the first time he ever left this estate and visited the royal palace. After his baptism, he was granted his own villa, where his isolated lifestyle continued for the most part, with him only getting very few chances to leave and visit other places.

Due to his duties, [[Sigiswald]] was unavailable to take up the position of overseer at the [[Royal Academy]]. Likewise, [[Anastasius]] had important duties connected to the land he had recently been put in charge of. After debating the issue for a long time, the [[King Yurgenschmidt
column2: king]] decided to appoint Hildebrand as the overseer. While it was unprecedented for a royal child that had not had their debut to take up official duties, Anastasius' and Sigiswald's respective duties were deemed too important to pull them away, and thus the king was left with no other viable choice.
