column1: Hirschur has violet eyes and black, slightly wavy hair, which she wears pulled back in a bun. She is about 170 cm (5’7”) tall.<ref name=""FB2CharacterSheets"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Fanbook 2]]. Character Design Sheets</ref> She usually wears a monocle on her left eye.

While she is perfectly capable of showing the usual noble etiquette expected of an archnoble, she apparently shares [[Ferdinand]]'s dislike for anything that delays her unnecessarily. As a result, she chooses to forgo the lengthy euphemisms and overly polite ways of her class whenever she can reasonably get away with it, preferring instead to be surprisingly direct and curt in her conversations.
She is practically obsessed with research, fitting the image of a ""mad scientist"" to a T in [[Rozemyne]]'s opinion, even more so than Ferdinand.
This attitude extends to her laboratory, where she barely ever bothers to clean up and - much like Ferdinand himself - often forgoing meals in the pursuit of her research.
To Rozemyne, it is rather clear that Ferdinand picked up many of his unusual personality quirks from Hirschur.

The monocle that Professor Hirschur wears is a magic tool that is helpful in seeing and understanding magic circles. It is unclear, at the moment, of the way this works or whether it has any functions beyond this.<ref name =""P4V2C7"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 2]]. Chapter 7: Measuring Schartz and Weiss</ref>

Since at his time in the Royal Academy, Ferdinand's ability to compress mana surpassed what the regular magic tools to show mana density can display, so she built a new one specifically to measure him. She later used the same tool to measure Rozemyne.<ref name=""P4V1C13"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 1]]. Chapter 13: Mana Compression and Creating a Highbeast</ref>
Hirschur is regarded as a genius at the Royal Academy, albeit a very eccentric one, in her field of specialization. [[Anastasius
column2: Prince Anastasius]] once remarked that not even [[Gundolf
column3: Professor Gundolf]] was able to follow some of her discoveries.<ref name=""P4V2S1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 2]]. Honest Courting</ref>

column1: As the overseer of the Ehrenfest Dormitory, it would usually be expected of Hirschur to live in the Dormitory that she is nominally in charge of. She, however, chose to live in the room in the scholar building of the central complex of the Royal Academy, where she had been living in during her schooldays, to have fewer potential distractions for her research. Her experiments also at times produce foul smells, making the residents of Ehrenfest's facilities somewhat glad Hirschur chose to deviate from the norm in this case.<ref name=""P4V2C6"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 2]]. Chapter 6: Tea Party with the Music Professors</ref>
Initially after her graduation, there was a period when she lived at the Ehrenfest Dormitory, but this came to an end once she chose to take on [[Ferdinand]] as her disciple. Due to [[Veronica
column2: Lady Veronica]]'s paranoia and spite, she did everything she could to mess with Ferdinand and anyone who would associate with him. This not only caused Hirschur to receive regular insulting messages from Veronica herself, but Veronica also had the students of her faction and their adult attendants mess with her in any way they could get away with, which caused her to often sleep in her laboratory and eventually to move entirely to the scholar's building.

column1: The people of the former Veronica faction also intercepted and either stole or redirected the funds meant for Hirschur. This state of affairs even continued well after Veronica's imprisonment, since [[Sylvester
column2: Aub Ehrenfest]] was never made aware of the issue until years later. This, however, was to Hirschur's own design. Due to this financial independence from her former home duchy giving her far more freedom in choosing her disciples, regardless of faction politics or inter-duchy relations, she asked Ferdinand - who was aware of the issue - to not tell Aub Ehrenfest and keep things as they are, telling him she neither wanted nor needed the funds. Only once [[Rozemyne
column3: Lady Rozemyne]] entered her second term at the academy, did Ferdinand end up explaining this to the archduke. In the meantime, Ferdinand took it upon himself to divert some of the money he earned from selling magic tools to Hirschur.<ref name=""P4V6E"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 6]]. Epilogue</ref>

column1: In previous years, Hirschur is said to only enter the Ehrenfest Dormitory twice a year and to prefer to stay entirely out of regular business, to be able to devote as much of her time as she can to her experiments into alchemy and magic tools.
This attitude also extends to her regular reports to Aub Ehrenfest, since they almost always just state that nothing out of the ordinary happened, even when there were issues well worth reporting.

Hortensia was originally born in [[Klassenberg]], but managed to be recruited into the Sovereignty, where she became a scholar retainer to the king's second son [[Waldifried
column2: Prince Waldifried]]. Her duties were mainly to care for the governmental documents and the bookshelves in the prince's villa, giving her a familiarity with several of the kind of magic tools employed by actual libraries. At the time, Hortensia was entirely devoted to her job and considered marriage inconsequential.

column1: Only days after the king's death, the villa of the second prince was visited by his older brother, but instead of a friendly visit, the first prince slaughtered Waldifried and his entire family, sparing only the retainers and servants and sparking off the [[Civil War
The loss of her master also saw Hortensia lose her sole purpose, and she didn't see a reason to live anymore. The at the time [[Previous Aub Klassenberg
column2: Aub Klassenberg]] introduced her to the third prince. She became his retainer and was charged with cleaning out the villa of her former master, but soon after, the third prince died too, only days after he defeated and killed the first prince, and Hortensia came to serve the fifth prince [[Trauerqual]].

column1: With the two leaders of the civil war faction dead, their followers congregated behind the two remaining princes. Those of the second and third prince rally behind the fifth prince. To strenghten the bonds between the newly assembled retainers, Aub Klassenberg suggested that Hortensia and [[Raublut]] marry, which they both accepted out of duty. Hortensia has no feelings toward her husband, but at the time was just glad to be given another duty to fill the void that the death of her former master left in her.

To her frustration, she was never able to give Raublut a child, and thus felt she failed her duty as a wife. When she was asked to become a librarian at the Royal Academy, she was greatly relieved and happy to finally have a duty she could fulfill to royal family and her husband. She arrived at the Royal Academy two days before the start of classes in Rozemyne's third year at the Royal Academy.<ref name=""P5V1S2"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 5 Volume 1]]. Finding Purpose and the Guardians of Knowledge</ref> Her duties, apart from being a librarian, are to unlock the closed-stack archive only accessible to archnoble librarians, so the royal family can look for clues to find the lost original transcription of the [[Grutrissheit]], to take ownership of the magic tools [[Schwartz and Weiss]] for the Sovereignty, and to keep a close eye on [[Rozemyne
column2: Lady Rozemyne,]] to see how loyal she is to the crown.

column1: On her initial tour of the library, she tells Solange about her tragic past, but reassures her that not all her memories are sad, which Solange returns in kind.
When she learns that only a [[Mestionora#Guardian of Knowledge
column2: guardian of knowledge]] can get the key to enter the room in which the previous archnoble librarians stored the keys to the closed-stack archive, she decides to become a guardian too.

column1: As instructed by Solagne, she inscribes the words of the ancient contract on the base of Mestionora's statue. When she completes this, the words float away from the base and are sucked into the part of the statue that resembles the Grutrissheit. A moment later, a key appears out of thin air and drops onto the socket of the statue. Solange urges her to pick it up, and when Hortensia does so, the key is absorbed into her body like a divine will.<ref name=""P5V1S2"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 5 Volume 1]]. Finding Purpose and the Guardians of Knowledge</ref>
She is able to meet with [[Rozemyne
column2: Lady Rozemyne]] on the first day of classes and gets registered with the pair of shumils, but is only a secondary master for the time being. Only when the amount of her mana inside the pair surpasses that of Rozemyne, will she become the primary master, but since Solange filled them up from a feystone with Rozemyne's mana the day before Hortensia arrived, this will take some time.

column1: When Solange suggests to once again hold a tea party for bookworms this year and explains what it is, she is happy to join.<ref name=""P5V1C4""/>

column2: Princess Eglantine,]] who hosts the bookworm tea party in her and [[Anastasius
column3: Prince Anastasius]]' royal villa. At the party, [[Hannelore]] tries to apologize for accidentally becoming the master of Schwartz and Weiss for a short time, but Anastasius tells her to not worry, since the fault lies with the library for not informing her. To this, Hortensia explains that she never expected the students to come to the library often enough for it to matter so early in the year, and thus was too slow to inform Hannelore on time. Rozemyne wonders how this could happen in the first place, and the new librarian explains that she had to prioritize other magic tools over the shumil, which Anastasius points out was at the request of the royal family. Since the matter involves the members of the library committee, she further explains to the students that she was tasked with taking ownership of the three archnoble librarian keys to enter the restricted archive they opened, but after dyeing the second key, she found that she had lost ownership of the first. To enable the royal family to enter the archive, they request that Rozemyne and Hannelore also take ownership of one key each, and to not overburden them, the mana supply for the shumil would be done only by Hortensia, Solange, and Hildebrand.

column1: Hildebrand is rather sullen about being left out, but Rozemyne is only too eager to accept this. She is disappointed to be forbidden from entering the archive itself, but is promised that she'll be allowed to read any document and book found inside that is deemed safe for her to read.<ref name=""P5V1C18"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 5 Volume 1]]. Chapter 18: Tea Party for Bookworms</ref>

In the next summer, she is summoned back home by her husband between and hasn't returned to the Royal Academy library since, not even when the new semester begins. At the time she sent word that she doubted she'd return to the library ""any time soon"" and has fallen completely out of contact since then. It is only from her husband that the academy is informed of her falling ill and being unable to perform her duties this year.<ref name=""P5V7C4"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 5 Volume 7]]. Chapter 4: The First Week of Classes</ref>

It is later revealed that Raublut killed Hortensia, when she became a risk to his plans. He uses her death as an excuse to gain entry to her room in the library under the excuse of retrieving her belongings and uses her feystone to open the door.<ref name=""P5V9E""/>

column3: blessing of the God of Darkness]] from the bible and of his expertise on both the [[Religious Ceremonies#Healing Ritual

column3: Staff of Flutrane]], much to Immanuel's amazement.

column1: After this proof that she had indeed been telling the truth and explaining that she was able to perform the entire ritual on her own due to having considerably more mana than most [[Temple Hierarchy#Blue Priest
column2: blue priests]] and using numerous high-grade [[Magic Potions#Rejuvenation Potions
column3: rejuvenation potions]], she is cleared of most of the suspicions. However, this still leaves the issue of being able to grant the God of Darkness blessing.

column1: Despite being very familiar with the bible, Immanuel has never seen this particular prayer in it, thus he initially doubts Rozemyne's honesty. When Rozemyne's words lead to the possibility of the Ehrenfest's and Sovereignty's bibles having differences, other members of the inquiry suggest to compare the two bibles with each other, which Immanuel eagerly supports, and so it is decided to adjourn the inquiry and continue in three days. Since much of what Rozemyne told about her past leads back to the local High Priest [[Ferdinand]], he is also summoned.<ref name=""P4V7C7"" />
Naturally, since only he can grant permission to read the Sovereignty's [[Bible#High Bishop's Bible
column3: Sovereign High Bishop]] is also invited. Together the gathered people find out that parts of the High Bishops' bibles are protected by enchantments that hide certain passages of text, even from those granted permission to read the bibles. While the precise triggers are not known, Ferdinand speculates that, in all due likelihood, it is tied to a combination of mana capacity and elemental affinities.

column1: While the Sovereign blue priests are unable to see any text in the passage pointed out by Rozemyne, both Prince Hildebrand and the Sovereign Knight's Order Commander are able to clearly read the words of the prayer in question, albeit due to the ancient dialect, both doubt they would be able to accurately understand said text. This clears Rozemyne from all accusations.

During the meeting, Immanuel questions why Rozemyne is just the High Bishop of Ehrenfest and suggests she should really become the Sovereign High Bishop, at which point he is curtly reminded by Ferdinand that, as an archduke candidate, this is not possible. The suggestion also earns Immanuel a rather displeased look from his superior the Sovereign High Bishop.<ref name=""P4V7C8"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 7]]. Chapter 8: The Bible Inspection Meeting</ref>

Since their meeting at the inquiry into the Ternisbefallen incident, Immanuel is very open in his attempts to win Lady Rozemyne for the Sovereign Temple. The next year the royal family arranges for Rozemyne to hold the Starbind Ceremony, in which [[Sigiswald
column3: Lady Adolphine]] are to be married. In the preparations for the ceremony, Immanuel gets a first-hand demonstration of Rozemyne's ability to morph her schtappe into multiple [[Divine Instruments]] simultaneously and effortlessly read ancient dialects, which makes him even more determined in his pursuit. After she leaves the chapel, he somehow manages to get ahead of her and intercept her. He tries to convince Rozemyne to visit the Sovereign Temple to read the ancient texts stores there and proof to the royal family that they have not been lying about the contents, but Rozemyne claims to be too fatigued by the ceremony and that any questions about such a visit would need to be decided by Aub Ehrenfest anyway. When Immanuel tries to move close to her, under the pretext of guiding her to a comfortable resting spot nearby, one of Rozemyne's guard knights draws her weapon and threatens to cut off his hand, if he doesn't back up. This gives Immanuel pause and while he and his subordinates hesitate, Rozemyne is whisked away by her knights.<ref name=""P5V5C3"" />

column1: Due to Relichion refusing to cooperate with [[Raublut]], the Sovereign Knight's Commander has him assassinated with poison, which results in Immanuel being promoted to Sovereign High Bishop. With the promise of forcing Lady Rozemyne to join the Sovereign Temple and getting a true, god-chosen Zent on the throne, Raublut is able to gain the support of Immanuel for his insurrection.<ref name=""P5V10S1"" />

After the fact, they recount how Rozemyne froze the ocean and closed the country gate. The fisherman were healed by Rozemyne directly through the Aub's Protection spell. Jiffy and co were shocked to see an aub heal commoners and valued them enough to receive protection.<ref name=""P5V11SS3"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]].'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 11]]. The New Aub’s Awesome Magic</ref>

Furt, another fisherman who works as a shipmate on a merchant vessel. He informs Jiffy and co about his experience with the new aub doing work in Kannawitz. He saw Rozemyne letting out her excess mana during Spring Prayer, describes it as rainbow light raining down from the sky from a chalice. Furt goes on to describe Lessy as a ""weird rainbow thing"" which grew as big as a house and it flew. After Rozemyne healed the land, the water in the ocean turned from foggy to clear, seaweed grew fast and the fish became huge. Hartmut came to Furt, informing him of the new aub's name and dedicating prayers to her.<ref name=""P5V11SS3"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]].'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 11]]. The New Aub’s Awesome Magic</ref>

After the announcement from the castle there's was going to be large-scale spell casted to heal the entire duchy at once, Jiffy and his wife Fina past through the central plaza where the city was full of buzz in anticipation of the events to come. They went to the port to wait for the large-scale spell to begin. Once it began, the women found joy in the magic circle's design as it resembled lace work and fans the rich girls use.<ref name=""P5V11SS3"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]].'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 11]]. The New Aub’s Awesome Magic</ref>

Hartmut made his announcement informing all Ahrensbach, soon-to-be Alexandrian citizens, to pray to he gods in order to help Rozemyne. By the third and fourth attempt, prayers could be heard all throughout the city and made it shake. Nobles and commoners alike were praying to the new aub.<ref name=""P5V11SS3"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]].'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 11]]. The New Aub’s Awesome Magic</ref>

Once the spell was complete, Jiffy and co went to get some sleep and decide to return the next morning. When they do, the ocean was bright blue-green. Even from far way, he could tell it was clear and no longer cloudy. Jiffy and co raced each other to the port and saw other fisherman already getting in their boats and setting sail. After that, a new race begins to deliver as much fish to Rozemyne as they can. The ocean had so many fish, Jiffy could see them just with his own eyes alone. He sets sail out to the ocean.<ref name=""P5V11SS3"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]].'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 11]]. The New Aub’s Awesome Magic</ref>

column1: '''Johann '''(ヨハン ''Yohan'') is an exceptionally skilled blacksmith in [[City of Ehrenfest
column2: Ehrenfest]]. [[Myne]] considers him to be the [[Honorary Titles#Gutenberg (Title)

column1: Johann is a ""younger guy"" with bright orange hair that he ties back in a low ponytail.<ref name=""P2V3C2"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 2 Volume 3]]. Chapter 2: Johann's Task</ref> His eyes are reddish-brown.

Compared to his fellow smith [[Zack]], Johann is quieter and more serious. He is not good at talking to clients,<ref name=""P3V4C16"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 3 Volume 4]]. Chapter 16: Hand Pumps</ref> and often frustrates non-craftsmen with his long and detailed lists of questions about each design. He enjoys challenging himself to create sophisticated and complex machinery, even when it means taking a bigger risk that the end product won't work.<ref name=""P3V1C17"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 3 Volume 1]]. Chapter 17: Johann and Zack</ref>
Johann is not good at dealing with other people. At Haldenzel when the local smiths fail to reach the necessary standards for [[Printing#Metal_Letter_Types
column2: metal letter types]], he only sorted the individual types of sufficient quality from those that failed, but didn't explain why they failed, leading to confusion and outright anger on part of the local craftsmen. Thankfully, Rozemyne was able to diffuse the situation by calming everyone and explaining in detail what exactly was wrong with the failed types and what consequences it would have if they had been used in a printing press, advising Johann to give similar explanations in the future.

column1: Heeding her advice, Johann was able to improve his communications skills and was able to avoid similar situations from cropping up when he visited [[Groschel]].<ref name=""P4V5C11"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 4 Volume 5]]. Chapter 11: Groschel and the Harvest Festival</ref>

*'''Smithing.''' Johann is a top-class smith who has a remarkable ability to precisely replicate almost any design, provided he is given detailed enough instructions.<ref name=""P3V1C19"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 3 Volume 1]]. Chapter 19: Finishing My Highbeast and the Wax Stencils</ref> Unfortunately, his tendency to ask lots of questions often frustrates his customers, who interpret it to mean that he can't do anything without tedious hand-holding.<ref name=""P2V3C2""/>

column3: laynoble]] who's the wife [[Kashick]]. She's the stepmother of [[Philine]] and [[Konrad]].

column1: Her abuse of her stepchildren was the primary reason for Konrad entering the [[Orphanage#Ehrenfest Temple Orphanage
column2: orphanage]] and Philine cutting ties with her family.
laynoble]] and graduated from the [[Royal Academy]].

column1: Due to an unspecified tragedy in her own family, Jonsara remained unmarried even in her early twenties, something that only happens very rarely among the Ehrenfest nobility. When Theresia, the wife of Kashick, a poor [[Nobility/Hierarchy#Laynoble
column2: lay]][[scholar]], died shortly after the birth of their son [[Konrad]], he had the choice between hiring a life-in-maid or marrying again. Due to both Kashick and Jonsara being in dire financial straights, they believed it economically better to marry and pool their meager resources together.

column1: When moving to Kashick's estate, Jonsara's aunt [[Eineira]] accompanied her niece and became the sole attendant of their family.<ref name=""SSC1C18"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Short Story Collection 1]]. Chapter 18: Philine — My Knight in Shining Armor</ref>

Initially Jonsara treated Theresia's children well, and she was also the one who taught Philine how to play the harspiel and praised her for her performance at her debut to noble society.<ref name=""SSC1C20"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Short Story Collection 1]]. Chapter 20: Charlotte — My Task</ref> But once her own son was born, she changed completely to the point that Philine feels like she turned into an entirely different person.<ref name=""SSC1C17"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Short Story Collection 1]]. Chapter 17: Philine — Coming Home from the Royal Academy</ref>

In her desperation to protect her own child and letting the power her husband put in her hands to go her head, she became outright cruel toward Philine and Konrad, often raising her hand against them under the excuse of discipline. Because her child had more [[mana]] than Konrad, she was determined to see him become the family's heir.

While her husband was working at the castle and Philine was studying at the [[Royal Academy]], she went as far as abusing Konrad with her [[schtappe]], leaving him battered and traumatized. She also confiscated the [[Magic Tools#Mana Draining Magic Tool
column2: mana draining magic tool]] given to him by his mother, drained it of mana, and re-registered it for her own son to use, effectively dooming Konrad to a slow death by [[Devouring
column3: mana exposure]].<ref name=""P4V3C16"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 4 Volume 3]]. Chapter 16: Philine's Family Circumstances</ref>

column1: When Philine returns from her first year at the [[Royal Academy]], she is horrified to discover how badly her brother has been abused in her absence. Jonsara confiscates the money Philine earned from Rozemyne and confines her in the family home, then sends an [[Schtappe#Ordonnanz
column2: ordonnanz]] to the castle claiming that her stepdaughter has fallen ill.

column1: However, Rozemyne's understanding of Philine's family situation and the muffled shouts in the background of the ordonnanz lead her to personally investigate, accompanied by [[Ferdinand]] and several of her retainers. Upon their arrival, Rozemyne's retainers go to collect the money and check on Philine in her place. They soon return, rushing out with the battered siblings in their arms.
[[Kashick]] and Jonsara explain the family simply does not have the money for a second magic tool or to support Konrad as a [[Temple Hierarchy#Blue%20Priest
column2: blue priest]]. Kashick is pained to admit that they have no choice but to place their family's hopes on the child with the larger mana capacity, while Jonsara is somewhat triumphant in her decision.

column1: Since both parents are willing to let Konrad die, Rozemyne insists on taking him into her custody as the orphanage director and giving him shelter at the temple, where he will eventually become a [[Temple Hierarchy#Grey%20Priest
column2: grey priest]]. Jonsara easily accepts, while Kashick seems to have mixed feelings.

column1: Before they go to the temple, Rozemyne attempts to heal Konrad. However, his memories of being abused by Jonsara send him into a fit of panic at the sight of her [[schtappe]]. Seeing his fear, she dispels her schtappe and proceeds to heal him with just her magic ring. After matters are settled, Rozemyne leaves with the two siblings. Philine vows never to return, leaving Jonsara happy and Kashick devastated.<ref name=""P4V3C16""/>
*'''[[Eineira]]''' - The sole attendant and permanent retainer of any kind in the house and Jonsara's aunt.<ref name=""SSC1C18""/>

''Due to their poor financial situation, they have no other noble retainers in their permanent employ and even the commoner chefs are only present from second to sixth bell to save on cost, meaning that sometimes the members of the family have to prepare their own meals despite being nobles.''<ref name=""SSC1C18""/>
*Her name ヨナサーラ (Yonasāra) is an anagram of さよなら (sayonara), which means ""farewell"". This reflects the incident where Philine left the house with Konrad and vow to never return again.

column2: Ehrenfest]] [[commoner]] clothing dyer who works at the Heuss Workshop as a [[lehange]]. [[Effa]] is one of his coworkers.

column1: Jorg is very confident in his own abilities and sometimes a bit forceful when it comes to pursuing his dream of opening his own workshop.<ref name=""P4V5S3"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 4 Volume 5]]. The Road to Exclusive Business</ref>
Jorg's dream is to open his own workshop, and he is putting his all into perfecting his craft and earning his [[Beruf
column2: beruf certification]]. He is rather jealous of [[Ingo]], who achieved this goal at an unusually young age, and the success his carpentry workshop saw after earning the title of [[Honorary Titles#Gutenberg

column1: When the dyeing competition is announced, he is very enthusiastic and confident in his ability to win it. Apart from his impressive skills at his craft, his over 60 year old father is one of the few people still alive who still remembers the old dyeing techniques and even retained some of his own tools. This gives Jorg an edge over most of his competitors. Despite this he still complains about how unfair it is that [[Effa]] has an even greater advantage due to having a daughter that had contact with Lady Rozemyne before and was regularly working on commissions for her. The needling of her co-workers eventually leads to Effa being the one who suggests that the samples should be labaled only with numbers, so the nobles would judge them on their qualities alone without even the chance for favouritism.
Jorg is utterly surprised by her bold suggestion and despite his constant complaints still asks her if that is truly what she wants, since once the issue has been passed to the [[Guilds#Dyeing Guild
column2: guild]] there would be no taking it back. But Effa is confident, and thus they make their suggestion to the guild, and it is consequently adopted.

column1: Within their own workshop Jorg's and Effa's pieces are chosen to participate in the competition and due to their good work they both manage to earn orders from nobles, albeit Lady Rozemyne does not award any titles and exclusive business to any of the competitors yet.
Despite not getting a title, Jorg getting a commission of a noble is still enough to earn him his Beruf.

When Effa voices her frustration of getting the High Bishop's exclusive business, Jorg cheers her up by admitting that he misjudged her and that her skills are indeed formidable. He further goes to encourage her to compete again at the next dyeing competition in the following spring, saying she hasn't lost her chance yet.<ref name=""P4V5S3""/>
Josef (ヨゼフ ''Yozefu'') is a commoner craftsman that specializes in Ink. He, along with his wife [[Heidi]], were given the title of [[Honorary Titles#Gutenberg (Title)
Josef is more calm and rational in terms of personality, acting similar to [[Lutz]] as he looks out for his ""weirdo"" wife and tries to keep her on track as much as possible.

When he was an apprentice, Josef was told to look after [[Heidi]].<ref name=""P2V3AW"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 2 Volume 4]]. Afterword</ref> He later married into her family and is continuing to look out for her.
*Miya Kazuki says that she wrote Heidi and Josef imagining what might have been between Myne and Lutz if Myne didn't have the [[Devouring]].<ref name=""P2V3AW""/>

Due to having grown up with several brothers, she is not used to being alone to the point of feeling lonely in the time between getting up and breakfast due to her roommate [[Philine]] having to sequester herself while absorbing her divine will.<ref name=""P4V1S1"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 4 Volume 1]]. A Productive Earthday</ref>
Judithe dislikes feeling “left behind” and works hard to keep up with the other retainers.

[[Part 5 Volume 4]]. Epilogue</ref>
At home Judithe often trained with the knights of her duchy, even when she hadn't yet reached her third year at the academy and thus wasn't even an apprentice knight yet.<ref name=""P4V1S1""/>

*'''Frederica''' - Judithe's attendant at least at the [[Royal Academy]].<ref name=""RAS1C9"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Royal Academy Stories - First Year]]. Chapter 9: Judithe - A Guard Knight Always Left Behind</ref>

*'''Marksmanship:''' Judithe is a skilled markswoman. column1: '''Justus''' (ユストクス, ''Yusutokusu'') is an [[Nobility#Tiers of Nobility
column2: archnoble]] [[attendant]] and [[scholar]] who serves [[Ferdinand]] as a name-sworn<ref name=""P4V5C15"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 5]]. Chapter 15: Leaving for the Royal Academy</ref> retainer alongside [[Eckhart]]. His mother is [[Rihyarda]], [[Rozemyne]]'s former head attendant in the castle.

column1: Justus has gray hair and brown eyes. Although he is slightly on the shorter side and has a slender build, he has an “ordinary” appearance that helps him to blend in with crowds when gathering information.<ref name=""P3V2C10"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 2]]. Chapter 10: Preparing for the Harvest Festival</ref>

When dressed as a woman, he looks “like a refined middle-aged lady” with brown hair. Because he has an androgynous face, Rozemyne comments that it doesn’t take much makeup to change his appearance.  He bears a strong resemblance to his mother, [[Rihyarda]], and his sister, [[Gudrun]].<ref name=""P4V3C9"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 3]]. Chapter 9: Justus and Preparing for the Interduchy Tournament</ref>

Justus’s prevailing trait is his insatiable curiosity. He loves to gather information, rumors, strange magical materials, rare spells, and anything that is new and unusual to him. Once he has collected something, however, he doesn’t have any particular interest in researching it further.<ref name=""P3V2C10"" />

He goes to great lengths in pursuit of his hobby and is willing to disguise himself as a woman or a commoner when needed. His single-minded enthusiasm can even override his survival instinct, putting himself and his companions in danger.<ref name=""P3V4C14"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 4]]. Chapter 14: Mount Lohenberg</ref>

In most situations, Justus has a friendly and easygoing personality. He tends to speak his mind and is not intimidated by status, occasionally even teasing [[Ferdinand]].<ref name=""P3V2C10"" /> Despite his familiar attitude, he has a strong sense of loyalty and feels contempt for those who shirk their duties, including his own nephew [[Traugott]].<ref name=""P4V3C8"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 3]]. Chapter 8: A Week of Socializing</ref>

Justus is more than willing to stand in as a guard, should Ferdinand require one in a position where regular guard knights aren't available or trustworthy enough.<ref name=""P4V5C3"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 5]]. Chapter 3: Going to the Italian Restaurant</ref>

When Justus was a child, he noticed that attendants and servants often spoke in an entirely different manner when away from their masters, saying things that they otherwise wouldn’t have. That led to him developing an interest in collecting information.<ref name=""P3V2C10""/>

Eventually, his mother [[Rihyarda]] scolded him that he should become a scholar if he loved gathering information so much, and use his enthusiasm to collect valuable intelligence for [[Sylvester]]. He did as Rihyarda suggested and decided to enroll in both the attendant and scholar courses at the [[Royal Academy]].<ref name=""P4V3C7"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 3]]. Chapter 7: Return to the Royal Academy</ref>
Due to both his mother and older sister serving [[Georgine
column2: Lady Georgine]] and the two being of the same age, she assumed he too would serve her upon enrolling at the Royal Academy. Since he was a male, he could not serve her as an attendant, so she tried to pressure him to enter as a scholar instead, but despite his intention to also take the scholar course, he still chose attendant as his first course, upsetting Veronica in the process. At the Royal Academy, Georgine called the information Justus collected and passed on unfiltered ""imprecise and entirely useless,"" causing him to lose any remnant of a desire to serve her he might still have had at the time.<ref name=""P4V9S2"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 9]]. The Beginning of a Winter Apart - Starting Life in Ahrensbach</ref>

column1: When [[Ferdinand]] later wanted to take multiple courses, Justus was the one who told him it was possible.<ref name=""P4V3C7""/>

However, Justus found that the information he brought to Sylvester usually ended up being put to good use by [[Ferdinand]], his right-hand man. He came to admire Ferdinand’s ability to connect seemingly irrelevant facts and use them to defeat the nobles who opposed him. Ultimately, Justus went against his mother’s wishes and chose to serve Ferdinand instead, alongside the guard knight [[Eckhart]].<ref name=""P3V2C10""/>
This loyalty and admiration went so far that Justus was even willing to [[Nobility#Name-Swearing
column2: name-swear]] himself to Ferdinand.<ref name=""P4V5C15"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 5]]. Chapter 15: Leaving for the Royal Academy</ref>

column1: His loyalty to Ferdinand was so strong that when he had to decide between his wife and child and Ferdinand, he picked the latter and divorced his wife, choosing to stay with his lord instead.<ref name=""P4V9S7"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 9]]. My Son’s Departure</ref>

When Ferdinand abandoned noble society and entered the [[temple]], Justus could no longer officially work as his attendant. However, he continued to assist Ferdinand in a reduced capacity, helping to gather intelligence and serving as a tax official when needed.

Not long after [[Myne]] joined the temple, Ferdinand assigned Justus and [[Eckhart]] to investigate her activities in the Lower City. After he was unable to gather information by disguising himself as a commoner, he and Eckhart broke into the [[Merchant's Guild]] building at night to investigate her official records.<ref name=""P3V2S3"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 2]]. Justus’s Grand Lower City Infiltration</ref>

column1: *'''Intelligence Work:''' Justus is very skilled at gathering difficult-to-find information. However, [[Rozemyne]] reflects no one but [[Ferdinand]] could make sense of the random details and gossip he collects.<ref name=""P3V2C10"" />

*'''Mimicry:''' As Justus explains, his line of work demands that he be able to “mimic men of all statures.” He is able to adapt his speech patterns, movement, lifestyle, and attitude as necessary to gather information.<ref name=""P3V2C10"" />

*'''Disguise:''' Justus can disguise himself effectively as a commoner, and more impressively, as a woman. Despite being familiar with him, Rozemyne mistakes him for a woman the first time she sees him cross-dressed.<ref name=""P4V3C9"" />
*'''Lip Reading:''' Justus is able to read lips.<ref name=""P4V3C10"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 3]]. Chapter 10: Meeting with the Prince</ref>

*'''Combat:''' Despite being an attendant and scholar by profession, Justus is strong enough to follow Ferdinand on his ingredient-hunting trips. He is able to overpower [[Traugott]], an archnoble apprentice knight.

*'''Sewing:''' To facilitate his crossdressing, Justus learned to be a surprising skilled seamstress. He was not only able to make his own dress - styled after an Ehrenfest attendant uniform closely enough that only a local would notice the difference on closer inspection - but also modified it to allow him to change into and out of it without the help of an attendant and added concealed pockets beneath the skirt to hide extra tools.<ref name=""RAS1C12"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Royal Academy Stories - First Year]]. Chapter 12: Traugott - A Worse Punishment than Expected</ref>

*Justus and his mother, [[Rihyarda]], are among the few characters in the series to use the terms “milady” (''hime-sama'', literally “princess”) and “my boy” (''bochama'', a “young master” or a young man from a rich family). They both often use “milady” to refer to Rozemyne.
*His name was previously translated as ""Eustachius."" It was revised to ""Justus"" in [[Part 3 Volume 2]]. The [[Anime
*Justus is banned from traveling in Rozemyne's [[Lessy
column2: Pandabus]], because he asks too many questions and makes it hard for her to concentrate.<ref name=""P3V5C1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 5]]. Chapter 1: The New Orphans and Operation Grimm</ref>

column1: *Justus and [[Eckhart]] both own a complete set of the forbidden illustrations of [[Ferdinand]] sold at Rozemyne’s harspiel charity concert. He presumably acquired them due to his love of collecting.<ref name=""P3V3E"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 3]]. Epilogue</ref>
*He once nearly caused Mount Lohenberg to erupt by stealing too many Riesefalke eggs.<ref name=""P3V4C14""/>
*Justus son was born when Justus himself was 18 years old. By the time Rozemyne entered the Royal Academy, this son had already graduated.<ref name=""FB6QA""/>
'''Kai''' (カイ, ''Kai'') is an orphan and apprentice grey priest in [[Orphanage#Ehrenfest_Temple_Orphanage
column2: Ehrenfest's temple]], roughly around the same age as [[Gil]].

column1: Kai grew up in the orphanage and was part of a group of boys that spent most of their time together which also included Gil. Despite this he didn't have a high opinion of Gil, remarking at one point that Gil was probably chosen as the commoner blue shrine maiden's attendant, because he was the most useless grey robe in the temple<ref name=""P2V1S2"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 2 Volume 1]]. An Attendant's Self-Awareness</ref>.
Kai was one of the orphans that made up the first group of grey robes to leave the temple and go to the forest to forage and learn to make [[Inventions#Plant Paper
He initially wondered out loud what [[Plant_Paper#Method
column2: paper-making]] was even good for. Since the orphans didn't know about money, [[Lutz]] eventually told them that it would help Myne get more food for them as an example.

column1: On the way through the [[City of Ehrenfest#Lower City
column2: Lower City]] he and others reminesce about their hopes and first impressions of Myne and how much Gil changed in the short time since becoming her attendant. They also marvel at how much Myne had already helped them despite or maybe exactly because of being just a commoner.

column1: '''Karstedt''' (カルステッド, ''Karusutetto'') is an archknight who serves as [[Ehrenfest (Duchy)

He is married to [[Elvira]], his First Wife, and father of [[Eckhart]], [[Lamprecht]] and [[Cornelius]]. Karstedt is [[Rozemyne]]'s noble baptismal father. He is also the grandfather to [[Siegrecht]].

Karstedt is a somewhat stocky older man with reddish-brown hair. Due to his many years of training, he moves with precision, and Myne thinks that he has the ""furiously intense air of a warrior.""<ref name=""P2V2C21"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 2 Volume 2]]. Chapter 21: Summons from the Knight's Order</ref>

A reliable and honorable man, Karstedt takes responsibility for his own actions and those of his subordinates. He stands firm on what he believes to be right and is not easily swayed. He also showed that he can be kind and affectionate, treating the commoner shrine maiden [[Myne]] like family as soon as her adoption was planned.<ref name=""P2V3C14"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 2 Volume 3]]. Chapter 14: Spring Prayer</ref>
Karstedt was born as the son of [[Bonifatius]], an archduke candidate of [[Ehrenfest (Duchy)
column3: Sixth Aub Ehrenfest]]'s first children were all girls, and he didn't plan on taking a second wife, Karstedt and his brothers were also raised as archduke candidates. As such, he received the training of an archduke candidate as a child and directly competed with [[Georgine
column4: Lady Georgine]] for the seat of successor to the Aub, and was quite evenly matched with her. column1: After his father [[Bonifatius]] retired as the commander of the [[Knight's Order]], Karstedt became the next Knight Commander. He was on good terms with [[Ferdinand]] during the time he served as a [[Knight
column2: knight]], recognizing him as his family and his cousin despite pressure from [[Veronica]] to ostracize him. Even after Ferdinand gave up his status and entered the temple, Karstedt continued to treat him with respect as a higher-ranking noble.<ref name=""P2V2C21""/>

column1: Karstedt married three times. His first marriage was a political match with [[Elvira]], an archnoble woman who created the Florencia faction and the younger sister of the Leisegang-aligned [[Claudio
column2: Giebe Haldenzel]]. They had three sons, [[Eckhart]], [[Lamprecht]], and [[Cornelius]]. His next marriage was to his second wife [[Trudeliede]], an archnoble and a member of the Veronica faction. They had a son named [[Nikolaus]].<ref name=""P4V1C5"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 1]]. Chapter 5: The Gifting Ceremony</ref>

column1: Finally, Karstedt married his third wife [[Rozemary]], a mednoble who had an abundance of mana. He loved her deeply and wanted to have a child with her. However, her family (including [[Viscount Joisontak]]) were troublemakers who began using her new status as an excuse to make demands on the family. When Trudeliede turned against Rozemary, Karstedt took his third wife's side. In turn, that forced Elvira to take Trudeliede's side to maintain balance in the household.

The entire family was strained by the conflict, which grew increasingly unpleasant as the years passed. In the end, Rozemary, who had a very poor constititution, died from the harassment and stress, deepening the gap between Karstedt and his other wives.<ref name=""P3V1P"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 1]]. Prologue</ref>
Karstedt was responsible to choose to knights to guard [[Myne]] during the [[trombe]] extermination. His subordinates failed, and [[Shikikoza
column2: one of them]] even hurt Myne, which lead to a failure on his part. As punishment, his pay got reduced, and he had to pay half the price of Myne's new ceremonial clothes.

column1: After Myne's memory searching, Ferdinand visits Karstedt's estate to return the magic tool. There he receives Ferdinand's report about his findings, while being amused and surprised by Ferdinand's attachment to Myne. Ferdinand wishes for Karstedt to adopt Myne and that as early as possible. Karstedt respects Ferdinand and deeply trust him, and so accepts his wish.

Karstedt visits the temple and speaks to Myne about the adoption. Due to Myne's emotional instability, the meeting ended abruptly. He remained involved with Myne and investigated [[Wolf]] with Ferdinand.

Afterwards, [[Sylvester]] investigates Myne in the temple as undercover blue priest, he follows Sylvester as his bodyguard. On one night during their [[Spring Prayer]] travel, they spend their night with music and sword dancing, where Karstedt displays his skillful sword dance. They were attacked during their travels once, leading Karstedt to unleash a strong magical attack with his sword turning rainbow-coloured. With the Spring Prayer completed successfully and finishing the investigation, Sylvester and Karstedt leave the temple.

Their roads cross not long after, at the time of the Archduke Conference. Sylvester and Karstedt returned to Ehrenfest using the Noble's Gate, and find themselves amidst a fight. In a matter of a few seconds, they reacted and followed Myne's instructions. The fight ended following Sylvester's job to judge the situation. Having determined the criminals and called in the Knight's Order, they could finally dedicate their time to discuss Myne's adoption. While they wait for Myne's family to arrive at the temple, they talk about Myne's situation, her adoption, her made-up story, and her new name. Karstedt would take in Myne as daughter between him and Rozemary, while baptizing her as [[Rozemyne]] with him and [[Elvira]] as her parents.

Originally, Lasfam was assigned to Ferdinand as an insult by [[Veronica
column2: Lady Veronica]]. With their low mana capacity, laynobles aren't able to use all the magic tools expected in an archduke candidate household, so by assigning him Lasfam, she made sure that his attendant would be seen as incompetent, which in turn meant that her followers had one more way to mock him for being ""unable"" to secure competent personnel.

Ironically, this made Ferdinand even more suspicious of him, since he suspected Lasfam might be a spy trying to play nice to gain more information from him. Only when Lasfam [[Nobility#Name-Swearing
column2: gave Ferdinand his name]] did he earn his masters trust.

He presides over summer, growth, and strength. His [[Divine Instruments
column2: divine instrument]] is a [[Divine Instruments#Leidenschaft's Spear
column4: divine color]] is blue, which symbolizes the vast sky.

column1: When the [[God of Darkness]] married the [[Goddess of Light]], they had four children. The oldest was [[Flutrane]], the Goddess of Water. Leidenschaft was the second of the siblings. [[Schutzaria]], Goddess of Wind, and [[Geduldh]], Goddess of Earth, were born after him.

The God of Life [[Ewigeliebe]] fell in love with Leidenschaft's youngest sister, Geduldh. The God of Darkness gave the two permission to marry, hoping they would fill the world with new life. But Ewigeliebe's jealous love consumed him, and he froze Geduldh in ice, so her child could never be born.

The world fell into winter, and Goddess of Light began to worry about her daughter. She found Geduldh trapped and melted the ice with her rays of sunlight, and Flutrane used the flooding water to fight off Ewigeliebe. The world was seeded with new life, and Leidenschaft used his power to nurture the growth of spring and create summer.

However, they could not fully defeat Ewigeliebe without preventing all new life from being born. Each year at the end of autumn, Ewigeliebe once again traps the Goddess of Earth in ice. Leidenschaft and the other gods rest and regain their power in winter, before fighting once again to rescue their sister in the spring.
Blue is considered a masculine color because of its association with Leidenschaft. People born in summer are also said to be passionate.

The Royal Academy contains a shrine dedicated to the God of Fire and his twelve subordinates, which grants a tablet, and a special word required to obtain the [[Grutrissheit]], after one has prayed and dedicated enough mana to him. The word Rozemyne was granted was Kraeftark.<ref name=""P5V5C5"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 5 Volume 5]]. Chapter 5: Zent Candidates</ref>

column1: Leise (イルゼ ''Iruze'') is the head chef of the [[Othmar Company]] and is the expert in cooking [[Inventions#Pound cake

Leise is a plump woman, who appears to [[Myne]] to be about the same age as [[Effa]] and to resemble [[Karla]].<ref name=""P1V3C2"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 1 Volume 3]]. Chapter 2: Making Cake with Freida</ref> She has green eyes.<ref name=""MP1V6"">[[Manga

column1: Leise is very competitive about food. If she is told about a new recipe or new variation, she must go and cook it immediately.<ref name=""P1V3C16"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 1 Volume 3]]. Chapter 16: Contract with Freida</ref> When the [[Italian Restaurant]] hosted [[Sylvester]], she personally delivered the desserts in order that she could test the food cooked by [[Hugo]].<ref name=""P3V1S2"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 3 Volume 1]]. One Stressed Out Chef</ref> Hugo had cooked the meal well to which she gave her grudging approval.

Leise grew up helping her parents in a restaurant near the east gate and learned to cook before her baptism, as well as having enough math skills to handle sales.<ref name=""P1V3S2"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 1 Volume 3]]. Leise - Confectionery Recipe</ref> After her baptism, she joined a restaurant run by a family friend and learned many more recipes. She continued to move from store to store, learning more recipes, until she was asked to cook for a noble. While she learned a large amount while working there, she was never able raise her status, as she did not have any other connections. When [[Gustav]] was looking for a noble-trained cook to help acclimatize [[Freida]], the head chef recommended Leise, as he knew she had the skills.

Myne met Leise when she was recovering from using a magic tool that was provided by Freida.<ref name=""P1V3C2""/> There, Myne talked with Leise about how to make pound cake. After the initial pound cake was over-baked on the outside, Leise immediately began baking a second cake to improve her skills. This improvement continued until Myne returned, and Leise traded a bag of sugar for more ideas.<ref name=""P3V1S2""/> When Myne visited a third time, Freida purchased the recipe for [[Culinary#Rumtopf
column2: rumtopf]] as well as trading another bag of sugar for more pound cake flavourings.<ref name=""P1V3S2""/>

column1: When Sylvester decides to visit the Italian Restaurant, [[Benno]] send Hugo and [[Todd]] to learn noble recipes from Leise to help improve the menu. Leise made the desserts for Sylvester's lunch, as Hugo and Todd were too busy making the main courses, and Leise had far more experience with sweets.
At Rozemyne's second visit to the Italian Restaurant for a discussion with the [[City of Ehrenfest#Lower City
column2: lower city]] merchants, they served several dishes that Leise had either improved or outright invented during Rozemyne's long sleep. One of those dishes is [[Culinary#Grilled Consommé Vegetables
column3: grilled consommé vegetables]], which she invented in response to losing a competition to Hugo.

column1: Both Rozemyne and the High Priest [[Ferdinand]] were pleased with all the dishes, and Rozemyne praised the assembled cooking staff, including Leise.<ref name=""P4V5C4"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 4 Volume 5]]. Chapter 4: Evolved Cooking</ref>
*When Leise got suspicious of Myne's knowledge and asked where it came from, Myne said it was from her dream world, and implied that it's better for Leise not to ask further questions.
'''Leon''' (レオン ''Reon'') is a [[leherl]] at the [[Gilberta Company]].
Leon seems down to earth and not immediately discouraged by hardships in his life. He seeks profit for him and his family's business in anything he does with his merchant soul.

Leon is from a linen merchant family, which wants to strengthen their connections with the Gilberta Company's clothing business. Resulting from this, he became an apprentice at the [[Gilberta Company]] after his baptism and later signed a [[leherl]] contract at the age of ten.

Since [[Myne]] associated with the [[Gilberta Company]], business changes happened, with one being the [[Italian Restaurant]]. The eatery needed qualified waiters, which is why [[Benno]] instructs Leon to train in the temple. He is thankful to be able to receive proper training, which might come in handy in the future, but more than just training, he is dispatched to the workshop or to bring orphans to the forest.

When [[Sylvester]] wanted to visit the lower city's forest, Leon, [[Gil]], and [[Lutz]] are asked to guide him to the forest with the orphans and show him around. After hearing Myne's request, he realizes that he is the only one who knows Sylvester's identity. In cold sweat, he decided to leave Sylvester to Lutz and look after the orphans. One shock after another arises for Leon, when he sees how the others are handling Sylvester.

When the topic of food comes up, he decides to report to Benno and organize the proper means to serve food to Sylvester. He splits up with the group and goes to the Gilberta Company. From there he takes food, a drink, and cutlery for Sylvester with him before he catches up with the group in the forest again. After arriving, he learns from Fritz that the orphans and Sylvester with Lutz split up in different groups. While thinking he found a companion in Fritz who has been making a table for Sylvester out of stones, the difference in common sense between the temple and commoners hit him over again. Leon somehow survives the trip with Sylvester's lunch and handling Sylvester spoils.
*Leon knows that Myne is not from noble origin.

column1: '''Leonzio''' is a grandson of [[Lanzenave]]'s previous king [[Chiaffredo]] and an envoy sent to [[Ahrensbach]] by his country.<ref name=""P5V6S1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 6]]. The Lanzenave Envoys</ref>
Leonzio is around 18 years old and 180cm tall. He has blonde to chestnut hair and amber eyes. He was born in Summer and has a Rainbow ring.<ref name=""FB6CDS""/>

In the year, after [[Rozemyne]]'s third academy term, Leonzio is part of the yearly delegation sent to [[Ahrensbach]] as part of their close trade relationship. This year a member of the royal family is dispatched, to directly plead with their neighbors for help in convincing [[Trauerqual
column2: Zent Trauerqual]] to allow a Lanzenave princess to be sent to the [[Sovereignty]], so a new crown prince can be conceived.
Lord Ferdinand]], he is quite shocked, due to how strongly the Ehrenfest noble resembles Leonzio's uncle, showing quite clearly that Ferdinand is a Seed of [[Adalgisa]].

column1: When he is informed that Zent Trauerqual turned down the request to allow a princess to be sent to [[Yurgenschmidt]], he pleads with [[Detlinde
column2: Lady Detlinde]], the acting Aub Ahrensbach, and Ferdinand for aid in changing the Zent's mind, which Ferdinand outright refuses. Detlinde clearly smitten with Leonzio and the sob story he tells, vows to do everything in her power to assist him and seems to assume that Ferdinand's refusal to help is due to him being jealous of Leonzio, over her.

column1: In a later private meeting, Leonzio uses Detlinde's obvious infatuation to woo her, complimenting her in ways more akin to how commoners talk, than the [[Noble Euphemisms
column2: euphemism]] laden language that is the norm among Yurgenschmidt nobles. Detlinde also becomes more pliable to his manipulations upon inhaling a sweet smell emanating from Leonzio.

column1: While under the influences of his charm, Detlinde informs Leonzio about Trauerqual not possessing a [[Grutrissheit]] and that she is a Zent candidate, albeit hasn't been able to obtain her own Grutrissheit yet. Leonzio claims he is aware of the location of the original Grutrissheit and promises to help Detlinde to ascend to the throne, if she promises to marry him. Detlinde is only too happy to oblige, against the alarmed protestations of her retainers.<ref name=""P5V6S1""/>

Once he managed to win Detlinde over completely, she distances her fiancé Ferdinand entirely, claiming that she abhors his jealousy toward Leonzio and dismisses anyone who criticizes her over her frequent visits to the Lanzenave estate and obvious adultery and frequently visits the Lanzenave estate to spend more time with Leonzio. She also often invites [[Letizia]] to come along with her. At such occasions Leonzio gifts the girl with sweets and toys from his homeland.<ref name=""P5V7P"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 7]]. Prologue</ref> When Ferdinand was poison by Letizia using Leonzio toys. It become clear Letiza was being used as a pawn.  Leonizo  justifying her punishment of being married off into Lanzenavian nobility as a form of mercy compared to the usual death penalty. Its unclear if Leonzio was being altruistic with this act of mercy or being pragmatic with Lanzenave shortage of fresh bloodline.<ref>''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 7]]. Epilogue</ref>

As we find out later, Leonzio is the leader of the Lanzenave faction that wishes to obtain more schtappes in Yurgenschmidt to be able to re-assert their dominance in their home country, where the rapid development of non-magical technologies has left mana-wielders to lose nearly all their influence and be viewed as little more than mana-sources by the general populace.

It was Leonzio, who came up with the idea to kill all the Ahrensbach nobles, not part of Detlinde and Georgine's faction and bring their feystones back to Lanzenave, with the permission and full cooperation of Detlinde and Georgine. While Gervasio seems to internally disapprove of this barbaric act, he does not stand in their way.<ref name=""P5V10C12""/>

*'''Mana Capacity:''' Detlinde is able to sense Leonzio's mana, meaning he has mana roughly equivalent to her's, which appears to be adequate for an archduke candidate of a greater duchy.<ref name=""P5V6S1""/>

column1: '''Lessy''' (レッサーバス, ''Ressaabasu'') is a [[highbeast]] crafted by [[Rozemyne]] utilizing a [[feystone]] presented by [[Ferdinand]]. Her inspiration for Lessy draws from the concept of a [[wikipedia:Red panda
column2: red panda]] (called lesser panda in Japan) and the [[w:c:ghibli:catbus

column1: First, Rozemyne created rides she knew from amusement parks and playground looking like a panda. After that, she used a lion as reference, as a lion-esque animal was the animal used by the archduke's family. As she thought about vehicles she could ride, she used a certain bus as reference. When she created the ''Lionbus,'' Ferdinand demands her to change the animal because it's ""not beautiful."" Rozemyne sets her mindset on making her highbeast even cuter, so Lessy the Pandabus was born. Lessy's tail was too big, and Ferdinand chastises it as a waste of mana. Rozemyne had to comply and shorten the tail about half of the length after a little argument with Ferdinand.<ref name=""P3V1C19>[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 3 Volume 1]]. Chapter 19: Finishing My Highbeast and the Wax Stencils</ref>

In Rozemyne's first year at the [[Royal Academy]], her unusual highbeast draws quite some attention from the other students. While most of the boys dismiss the design, many of the girl are intrigued by the advantages it brings. During one of the lessons, [[Hirschur
column2: Professor Hirschur]] is able to reshape her own highbeast into something inspired by Lessy, albeit with more traditional reigns instead of a steering wheel and pedals and modeled after a [[shumil]]. This starts a new trend among the female archduke candidates and archnobles, though due to the increased mana cost compared to traditional highbeats, few mednobles and no laynobles are able to follow suit.

column1: Coined by Professor Hirschur, the term drivable highbeasts becomes an established way to refer to these kind of car-like highbeasts, with the classical variant being called rideable highbeasts.

*Lessy is a highbeast that can transport any amount of passengers and luggage easily, as Rozemyne can increase Lessy's size to accommodate her needs. The biggest Rozemyne has made Lessy so far was big enough to hold luggage that would have taken three regular coaches to transport, as which point she thought that Lessy had become more of a Pandatruck than a Pandabus.<ref name=""P4V9C14"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 4 Volume 9]]. Chapter 14: Separation</ref>
*Lessy is a highbeast that does not have wings but still flies, which initially surprises people. This feature allows it to move easily in tight spaces like corridors and forests.
*Lessy is like a car on the inside. It has seats with seatbelts, pedals, luggage space, and a steering wheel.
*Lessy's internal is soft, comfortable, and feels pleasant to touch.

*Because the rider doesn't have to ride on a steed, s/he is able to sit on a chair. A few noble women take note that they will be able to wear their finest dresses while riding, instead of changing into their rider costumes.
*Since Lessy's insides are an enclosed space, the rider is unaffected by the weather outside. The windows are covered with transparent mana membranes.

*Lessy is created from Rozemyne's mana, therefore anyone with less mana than Rozemyne couldn't destroy Lessy or harm the passengers inside. Due to Rozemyne's exceptionally large mana capacity, it is nigh-impenetrable in terms of defense.

*The Pandabus, while recreating various components like steering wheels, pedals, and seat belts, does not replicate glass windows. Instead, the windows are composed of a mana membrane, providing transparency for the driver. Given the highbeast's stone-like structure, Rozemyne remains unconcerned about the specific material composition.<ref name=""FB2Q&A"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]: [[Fanbook 2]]. Q&A with Miya Kazuki.</ref>

While divine mana coursed through Rozemyne, she was unable to use her regular highbeast feystone. To retain her mobility and expant some of the divine mana, Ferdinand gathered a number of rainbow feystone, which Rozemyne combined into one big feystone, before turning it into a new highbeast stone. While the shape of this new Lessy is the same as the old one, it shimmered in all seven mana colours. Unlike the original, this Rainbow Lessy left anyone who looked upon it in awe, most likely because of the psychological effect that exposure to divine mana has on people.

Due to the need to stay away from the tiring meetings with the local nobility in this delicate phase, Ferdinand adviced Rozemyne to make Rainbow Lessy big enough to serve as a place in which all her retainers could rest for the night, so they didn't have to sleep outside or in commoner houses. Rozemyne originally envisioned this temporary form as resembling a mobile home from Earth, but after incorporating the changes Ferdinand suggested, it looked more like a house, than a vehicle, featuring among aother things two seperate storeys to accomodate both women and men and a room with sofas for relaxing to tea.<ref name=""P5V11C12"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 5 Volume 11]]. Chapter 12: Expending Mana through Spring Prayer</ref>
Lessy, the Pandabus, originates from Lesser Panda (レッサーパンダ, ''Ressaa Panda''). In the Japanese version, Rozemyne names her highbeast Lesser-kun (レッサーくん, ''Ressa kun'') which implies Lessy to be male.

column2: grun]], implying that a grun looks like a lesser panda. However, Rozemyne thought they're not similar at all when she encountered real gruns.

column1: *[[Miya Kazuki]] noted that most people abhorred Lessy because it's equivalent to making a cockroach-shaped car on earth. It's not going to be popular even when made to be cute, not to mention that [[Yurgenschmidt]] doesn't have the culture of making cute style drawings and figures.
*Rozemyne is allowed to use it around the Archduke's Castle, because she walks too slowly and the castle is very large.
*[[Justus]] is not allowed in it. This is because the first time he was driven in it, he talked too much and asked too many questions, which distracted Rozemyne.

*[[Brigitte]] is usually the guard who accompanies Rozemyne in Lessy when they're travelling, while [[Damuel]] is on his highbeast protecting them. She is also one of the very few people who find Lessy cute.
**After her retirement, [[Angelica]] and [[Judithe]] took her place in part 4.
*[[Hirschur]] is the first person to create a drivable highbeast based on Lessy. They become a trend in the [[Royal Academy]] since then, especially popular among females.
*When big enough to have side-by-side seats, Lessy has the steering wheel on the right side, as is common in Japan.

Lieseleta is exceptionally skilled in masking her true emotions. While working and in the presence of her mistress, Lieseleta always appears prim, proper and utterly calm. In private however she is quite bright, cheerful and talkative.
She even shows a playful side by lightly teasing [[Damuel]] on occasion.

column2: shumils]], in which her passion rivals Angelica's passion of getting stronger. Whenever topics about shumils are brought up, she gets very excited.

column1: Shumils are so far the only thing that ever managed to make Lieseleta's work façade slip and openly show her true emotions to Rozemyne, albeit briefly.<ref name=""P4V5C13"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 4 Volume 5]]. Chapter 13: The Library Plan and Completed Outfits</ref>

Due to Lady [[Rozemyne]] managing to get Angelica to successfully graduate from the [[Royal Academy]], Lieseleta is very thankful and loyal to Rozemyne. A noble failing to graduate the Royal Academy would be a great mark of shame upon the entire family that Angelica's master spared them from. It is also this act that made Lieseleta utterly convinced of Rozemyne's abilities. She once mused ""you guided my sister to graduation, so nothing is beyond your abilities.""<ref name=""P4V2C4"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 4 Volume 2]]. column2: Rozemyne's mana compression method]], their respective mana capacities diverge so much, they can not realistically expect to ever have children together. With Ferdinand departing from Ehrenfest to marry, any chance of Ulbrick learning the mana compression himself disappears, and their families have no choice, but to cancel their engagement.<ref name=""P5V6S2"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 5 Volume 6]]. My Hopes and Their Problems</ref>

column1: Upon witnessing how poor of health her lady truly is, she takes up the study of medicine at the Royal Academy. While she isn't able to finish enough of the courses to be officially recognized as a doctor, that was never her goal to begin with, since she only wishes to be better able to help her lady in any way she can, so the knowledge itself is the goal for her, not any title that comes with it.<ref name=""P5V6S2"" />

Lieseleta is very fond of [[Schwartz and Weiss]] and eagerly throws herself into her studies to make sure she finishes her courses for the year early so that nothing can get in the way of her participating in Lady Rozemyne measuring the two [[shumil]]s for their new clothing. Rozemyne suspects that this is at least partially due to her missing the pet shumils she has back home.<ref name=""P4V2C7"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 4 Volume 2]]. Thanks to the [[Rozemyne Mana Compression Method
column2: Rozemyne Mana Compression]], Lieseleta's mana has grown to a capacity of an archnoble, which also opened the gap between her and her fiancé - a fellow mednoble - beyond the point, where the two are able to sense each other's mana, forcing the families to cancel it. With her barely in range to still feel her father's mana, it becomes clear that she will only be able to marry an archnoble, but as the successor of her house, it is necessary her future husband marry into her family, and thus be reduced in status to a mednoble, which makes it quite difficult to find a suidatable husband for her.

column1: Ideally both the family and Lieseleta herself wish for a future husband who is an attendant, serves a member of the archducal family, or at least works in the castle and is willing to marry into their family, but her father is unable to find any such mednoble, with high enough mana capacity to be compatible with his daughter, or archnoble who both fits all the preferances and is willing to marry down. However he is able to find [[Thorsten
column3: Lord Wilfried]]. Due to being only the third son of his father, Thorsten has little in inheritence to expect and wasn't able to bring up the enormous sums necessary to create a new house of his own. Furthermore, Thorsten's family wishes to form connections with Lady Rozemyne, but as former members of the Veronica faction, they find it difficult to approach most of Rozemyne's retainers, due to the generation-lasting feud between the Leisegang, who most of them belong to, and the former Veronica factions. Lieseleta's family being faction neutral, despite the budding connections they have with both Rozemyne and Bonifatius, and her having archnoble levels of mana, makes her attractive enough of a match for Thorsten, the family is willing to marry their son down into the mednoble family, while such a match would grant Lieseleta's family a future husband who fulfills all their wishes, except being an attendant. Despite Lady Rozemyne's involvment in Veronica's fall, Thorsten and his family are not resentful of her, but on the contrary are thankful to her, due to Rozemyne's intervention preventing Wilfried from being disinherited, which would have brought their house down with him.

Liz (リーゼ, ''Riize'') was [[Benno]]'s childhood friend and fiancée, with their relationship initially rooted in a competitive rivalry as merchant apprentices that blossomed into a profound and genuine love.

In the bustling world of merchants, Benno and Liz initially stood as rivals, both undergoing the trials of apprenticeship. As they navigated the intricate world of commerce, a gradual shift occurred, and the rivalry evolved into a deep and genuine love. This love led to their engagement, a promising union that held dreams of a shared future.

However, fate took a cruel turn, as Liz succumbed to the relentless grip of the Devouring before their vows could be exchanged.<ref name=""MP1V7"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Manga]]. [[Manga Part 1 Volume 7
column2: Part 1 Volume 7]]. As the Gilberta Company's Successor</ref> The Devouring, a mysterious and often fatal ailment, struck Liz after she had passed through the threshold of puberty, revealing its harrowing symptoms. This unexpected tragedy left Benno devastated, haunted by the anguished screams of his beloved during the relentless onslaught of Devouring attacks.

column1: The impact of Liz's untimely death lingers in Benno's memories, an indelible mark on his heart that shapes his perspective and actions.<ref name=""P4V2E"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 4 Volume 2]]. Epilogue</ref>

In the short story ""Renewal Of Contracts and Relationships,"" written from Liz's perspective, their relationship is explored further. Amidst a disagreement banishing them to the storeroom, Liz contemplates the decision to renew her contract with the Gilberta Company. Surprisingly, Benno, initially seen as a rival, encourages her to stay, revealing a more profound connection.<ref name=""SS54"">[https://ncode.syosetu.com/n7835cj/54/ Renewal Of Contracts and Relationships]. ncode.syosetu.</ref>
*She was one of the few people who could fight [[Benno]] head-on on equal terms or even win the argument.
*She and Benno would often hide behind the store and act like adults while planning little plots.<ref name=""P1V3S4"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm ]]. [[Part 1 Volume 3]]. Mark - The Master and I</ref>
*Looking at her Japanese name リーゼ and how most names of citizens of Ehrenfest look German, her name could also have been ""Liese"", which may look a bit too close to [[Leise]].

*Benno's late fiancée, Liz, silently grappled with the Devouring, a rare ailment. Her symptoms, triggered by the condition, emerged after she had gone through puberty and become engaged to Benno due to her low mana levels. Liz's story is not extensively explored in Myne's narrative, but [[Miya Kazuki]] said she would hold a significant role in an account centered around Benno's experiences.<ref name=""FB2Q&A"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]: [[Fanbook 2]]. column1: Lueuradi has hair of such a light shade of orange that it's almost yellow and light green eyes.<ref name=""P5V1S1""/>

Lueuradi is completely enamored with the Royal Academy Love Stories book series from Ehrenfest. She appears to be rather shy for an archnoble when meeting new people, but that shyness quickly flies out the window and is replaced by passion once romance stories come up.<ref name=""P5V1S1""/>

Rather than having each Jossbrenner students who chose to take up Rozemyne's crest work contact Ehrenfest, Lueuradi is the organizer who gathers the stories and acts as the contact point to Philine on behalf of her duchy's dormitory. In her third year at the Royal Academy, Philine introduces her to a fellow retainer [[Muriella]], who just freshly entered Lady Rozemyne's service. The two quickly strike up a friendship over their shared passion for romance stories.<ref name=""P5V1S1""/>
Together with her elder sister [[Fairziere]] and the fellow archnoble [[Lustlaune]], Lueuradi participates in the [[Dedication Ritual]] held by [[Ehrenfest (Duchy)
column2: Ehrenfest]] and [[Dunkelfelger]] as part of their joint research into how divine protections are obtained. Before the ritual, Lueuradi had not given much credence to [[Hartmut]]'s endless praise for [[Rozemyne

column1: Despite being an archnoble, Lueuradi is very late in performing the ritual to acquire the divine protection of the gods. Thanks to this circumstance, Lueuradi creates a charm dedicated to Bluanfah, the Goddess of Sprouts, and sincerely prays to her every day that she will encounter more wondrous romance stories. column1: Lutz has short golden-blond hair and jade green eyes. When they first meet, [[Myne]] thinks that his colour scheme makes him look both reassuringly familiar and like a ""cool, handsome guy.""<ref name=""P1V1C6"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 1 Volume 1]]. Chapter 6: Neighborhood Boys</ref> Growing up in the lower city, he has a scruffy appearance and wears secondhand, heavily patched clothing. However, he begins to dress in nicer merchant clothing and pay closer attention to his appearance after joining the [[Gilberta Company]]. After Rozemyne wakes up from her [[jureve

Lutz has a patient and calm personality, due partly to growing up as the youngest of four brothers. Unlike most people, he isn’t put off by Myne’s outlandish ideas. Instead, he takes a practical approach and plans to make them a reality.

Despite his easygoing nature, he can be exceedingly stubborn and tenacious. He works tirelessly to achieve his dreams and even goes against his family’s wishes to become a merchant. When he becomes an apprentice merchant, he studies hard to catch up to the other apprentices, who come from merchant families.

Lutz is equally loyal as a friend. He remembers and upholds his promise with Myne, even years after making it. He also pays close attention to her health, gives her advice, fights on her behalf, and comforts her when she’s feeling down.

Lutz was born to a very poor family in the south of the [[city of Ehrenfest]]. His father [[Deid]] was a carpenter, and his mother [[Karla]] was a textile worker. His three older brothers, [[Zasha]], [[Sieg]], and [[Ralph]] often took away his food and belongings, and Lutz didn’t always get enough to eat.

column2: Urano’s]] memories awoke in [[Myne]], Lutz didn’t see her very often due to her illness. When they did meet, he looked out for her and tried to act like a ""tough older brother,"" helping her carry things and protecting her whenever she got exhausted.<ref name=""P1V1C6"" />  Like most [[Commoner
column3: commoner]] children, he spent the years before his baptism helping around the house and foraging for food in the woods with his brothers.

column1: *'''Business:''' Thanks to Benno’s strict tutelage, Lutz has a thorough understanding of business, pricing, negotiation, and other important skills for merchants.
*'''Education:''' Despite growing up in an illiterate household, Lutz developed reading, writing, and math skills equal to those of any child born to a merchant family.

*'''Etiquette:''' Lutz was able to quickly learn the formal language and mannerisms that merchants use with wealthy customers and nobility. On several occasions, he picked it up faster than [[Myne]], albeit is left behind quick and far, once Myne is adopted into the nobility and becomes [[Rozemyne]].
*'''Carpentry:''' Lutz is quite talented with woodworking, likely due to coming from a family of carpenters.
*'''Printing:''' After many years of helping with Myne’s [[Plant Paper
column3: printing]] efforts, Lutz has an in-depth understanding of both industries. His skill in producing and selling books led to Myne naming him among her [[Honorary Titles#Gutenberg (Title)

first wife]] is from a [[Gilessenmeyer]], currently ranked Fourth, while Magdalena is from the greater duchy [[Dunkelfelger]], Magdalena tries to keep out of the public eye as much as possible, to show her support for the first wife and counteract calls for her to be made the first wife instead.<ref name=""P5V5C4""/>

column1: As a member of the Dunkelfelger archducal family, Magdalena received far more extensive combat training than most nobles of her position of other duchies.
