column2: Lady Veronica]] and her faction by marrying him into their own duchy. Toward this purpose, they pressured their Aub to arrange an engagement between Ferdinand and Magdalena. This infuriated Magdalena, who had no intention of marrying the boy from a middle duchy, when she was already in love with the at-the-time fifth prince [[Trauerqual]]. Before any official arrangements could be made between Dunkelfelger and [[Ehrenfest]], Magdalena managed to secure engagement of herself and the prince, even though it would only be as his third wife.

column1: Not too long after the civil war happened, she ultimately saw her husband rise to the position of [[Nobility/Hierarchy#Zent

Marthe being the youngest is the quickest to adjust to the new environment.
Not long after Rozemyne left, the mayor organizes an attack on the monastery, but the barrier around the building prevents the attackers from getting near.

With the help of [[Ferdinand]], Rozemyne is able to approach Kantna and have the contract for the two orphan girls nullified. She then proceeds to pay the Mayor for the four orphans, making their status as grey priests official.

column2: capital]], but they return to their hometown's monastery in the next spring.

column1: Due to serving Detlinde, and participating in the [[Lanzenave]] invasion, her [[schtappe]] was permanently destroyed and will spend the rest of her life imprisoned, regularly having her mana drained.<ref name=""P5V12C11""/>
According to [[Lamprecht]], she is smart and cheerful, making her the favored child in the family.

Due to being the daughter of a woman from [[Frenbeltag]], Martina and her sister were exposed to much hostility and mistrust by many of Ahrensbach's citizens, which naturally hit her older sister first. Seeing how Aurelia's timid nature and intimidating appearance worsened her situation made Martina adopt overly cheery and bubbly behaviour, which succeeded in overcoming the stigma of her lineage and made her a very well-liked person, not just in her own family, but in the duchy as a whole and more importantly with Georgine and Detlinde.

After his demotion from archduke candidate to archnoble by Ahrensbach tradition after his brother's ascention to Aub, Martina's father made sure to spread his children among the different factions vying for dominance in the duchy. Due to her Frenbeltag mother, Martina would have had a very difficult time to join the faction of Aub Ahrensbach's first wife, who was from a duchy on the winning side of the [[Civil War
column2: civil war]], so she was told to join Georgine's faction instead, which had already absorbed the former second wife's faction after her execution in the purges and was steadily gaining power. Also the family believed that both Martina and Georgine having ties to Frenbeltag - the former through her mother and the latter through her [[Constanze
column3: sister]] who had married the new [[Aub Frenbeltag]] - would help the girl to get into the faction. Finally due to being of a fitting age, Martina's father had hopes that his daughter might be able to become Wolfram's second wife or Detlinde's retainer.

column1: Once she joined the faction upon her baptism, Martina's diligence and hard-working attitude quickly caught the eye of Georgine, who is quite fond of strong-willed and hard-working individuals. Despite originally planning to become a scholar and serve Lord Wolfram upon entering the Royal Academy, when Georgine offered to make Martina an attendant of her daughter Detlinde, Martina accepted and dedicated herself to this new role. In this position, her likable facade quickly gained her the favour of her new lady as well and made her one of Detlinde's favourites.

Her father initially was very pleased with how quickly his daughter had managed to put down such deep roots, but this quickly changed when he realized that this was a ploy by Georgine to control the flow of information and he barely received any intel from his daughter. In his irritation, her father bemoaned that his daughter was only serving the ""lowly"" Detlinde - at the time the mostly neglected youngest daughter of a third wife - and decried Georgine as “Ehrenfest’s chamavarein.”<ref name=""P5V3E"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 3]]. Epilogue</ref>

Rather than primarily being concerned with fulfilling her lady's wishes like most attendants, Martina and her fellow retainers appear mostly busy with damage control for Detlinde's constant social blunders and attempting to prevent even further blunders from taking place, which rarely succeeds. Due to the grading system for attendants at the Royal Academy, this unfortunate circumstances also have a noticeable negative impact on her grades in class. This makes Martina quite glad that with her being one year younger than her lady, she will have one year free of those antics before graduation, of which her older fellow attendant [[Fatiehe]] is rather envious. Martina in turn envies Fatiehe for being engaged to a noble from another duchy and about to marry in the coming spring, thus escaping both Ahrensbach and Detlinde's service. While being one of Detlinde's favourites does have some perks for Martina, it also means that her lady is that much less likely to ever let her marry outside of Ahrensbach, greatly limiting Martina's marriage prospects and future plans.

When Ferdinand first arrived in Ahrensbach, Martina was entirely fooled by his outward facade of loving affection for Detlinde and truly believed that she beheld an actual romance. However, when Detlinde brazenly demands Ferdinand [[Nobility#Name-Swearing
column2: give her his name]], she finally sees past his gentle and sweet smile and notices the utter coldness in his eyes.<ref name=""P5V3E""/>

column1: Due to serving Detlinde faithfully and even accompanying her to the Adalgisa Villa during the insurrection, Martina is branded a criminal of the highest order. While she escapes the death sentence, thanks to the Goddess of Wisdom, [[Mestionora]]'s decree that no further lives are to be lost, she is still severely punished. Her [[Magic Tools#Citizenship Medal
column3: Execution Magic]] while she was in another duchy, permanently destroying her schtappe and demoting her to the status of a commoner. Furthermore, she will spend the rest of her life imprisoned and regularly having her mana drained, to be used for whichever duchy she'll be sent to, which will be decided at the upcoming archduke conference.<ref name=""P5V12C11""/>

column1: '''Melchior''' (メルヒオール ''Meruhiooru'')  is the youngest son of [[Sylvester]] and [[Florencia]] and an [[Nobility/Hierarchy#Archduke Candidate

column1: In the midst of the [[Lanzenave]] Invasion and [[Rozemyne]]'s absence during Spring Prayer, Melchior was formally inaugurated as Ehrenfest's High Bishop.<ref name=""P5V12C13""/>

Despite sharing the hair colour of his father, his facial features and blue eyes make him more reminiscent of his mother.<ref name=""P4V8C1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 8]]. Chapter 1: The Return and Dinner Meeting</ref>

Melchior is very attached to his siblings and tries to spend as much time as he can with them, even trying to join them in their work and studies whenever he can and trying to find other ways to at least stay in the same room, even when they do things he can not help them with.<ref name=""P4V8C11"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 8]]. Chapter 11: Sitting Out the Archduke Conference</ref>
Like all Archduke Candidates of Ehrenfest, he lives and grows up in a building separate from the main castle to its north.

Since he would never have any opportunity to meet them before being baptized, Melchior was not told about any of his relatives in other duchies, except Constanze and her husband, who had came up in conversations previously.

During their visits to their younger brother, both [[Wilfried]] and [[Charlotte]] have often talked very positively about [[Rozemyne]], but due to not being a blood-related sibling, she was not able to personally visit Melchior<ref name=""P4V8E"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 8]]. Epilogue</ref>
He is eager to also join his siblings in performing [[Religious Ceremonies
column2: religious ceremonies]] and is studying geography very diligently for this purpose. He is also looking forward to borrow the boards from his siblings from which they learned the necessary prayers. His parents have decided that he will only join in the ceremonies the following year, so he can get more used to moving and using his mana. Unlike with Charlotte, who had to stand in for her comatose sister right after her [[Baptism
column3: baptism]], this year there is no pressing need to push such a difficult and exhausting task onto the boy right now.

column1: In the meeting with his parents right after their return from the Interduchy Tournament, Melchior first learned that he had a [[Rudiger
column2: cousin]] in [[Frenbeltag]], much to his surprise. His parents explained why they didn't tell him about his relatives from other duchies in the past and said they would soon teach him about them.<ref name=""P4V8E""/>

column1: Melchior's new room in the northern part of the [[City of Ehrenfest#Archduke's Castle
column2: Archduke Castle]] has been prepared while his siblings were at the [[Royal Academy]] and [[Interduchy Tournament]]. He is very excited to finally meet his adopted sister [[Rozemyne]].<ref name=""P4V8C1""/>

column1: A few days before his baptism, Charlotte hosts a tea party for all four children of the archducal couple, where Rozemyne and Melchior finally meet face to face for the first time. The two get along very well. Melchior admits that he felt rather lonely ever since Charlotte moved from the children's rooms to the northern building and couldn't wait to move there too. After he mentions his fondness of books and stories of the gods to Rozemyne, she immediately tells her head attendant [[Rihyarda]] to bring the [[Bible#High Bishop's Bible
column2: High Bishop's Bible]] from the [[temple]], but relents after being reminded that this is a bad idea. Instead, she opts to tell her younger brother some stories of the gods from memory.

column1: During the feast celebrating spring, Melchior manages to successfully hide his nervousness and finish his [[Baptism]] Ceremony with aplomb.<ref name=""P4V8C4"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 8]]. Chapter 4: Melchior's Baptism</ref>
His father has decided that upon Rozemyne's coming-of-age and subsequent abdication of her post as [[Temple Hierarchy#High Bishop
column2: High Bishop]], Melchior will take over the position. In part for this reason, the temple is currently in the process of changing the roles of both the High Bishop and [[Temple Hierarchy#High Priest
column3: High Priest]] away from daily administrative work and focus almost entirely on providing mana, performing ceremonies, and leading the [[Temple Hierarchy#Blue Priest
column4: blue priests]], with the grey priests taking over all the paper-work.<ref name=""P4V8C15"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 8]]. Chapter 15: Successors</ref>

column1: While his siblings are off to the Royal Academy for Rozemyne's and Wilfried's third terms and Charlotte's second term, Melchior is confined to the northern building almost immediately after their departure. He's not even permitted to go to the children's playroom. Despite their best efforts to make time, his parents are just too busy to visit him often, and thus solely in the company of his retainers and tutors, he soon grows lonely and depressed.

When his siblings finally return from the Royal Academy, he's overjoyed to be able to spend time with them. And since they too are told to not leave the northern building, they have plenty of time to catch up and spent time together.<ref name=""P5V4C1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 4]]. Chapter 1: Returning Home and Everyone’s Situation</ref>

Seeing how much work his siblings and parents have to do and feeling responsible for contributing as an archduke candidate of Ehrenfest, Melchior is eager also work for their duchy.<ref name=""P5V4C3"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 4]]. Chapter 3: Archducal Family Meeting</ref> In part to accommodate her younger brother's adorable request and in part to gain the help of his retainers for paper work in the temple, Rozemyne agrees to have him regularly visit the temple and work there from third to fifth bell. Melchior was already supposed to learn the necessary prayers to participate in this year's [[Religious Ceremonies#Harvest Festival
column2: Harvest Festival]], so Rozemyne intends to first have him learn the necessary prayers for that, while also dedicating some mana to the divine instruments to both alleviate the mana shortage and increase his chances of gaining a larger number of divine protections when he goes to the Royal Academy. His older retainers are rather reserved about the issue, but once they learn how praying, dedicating mana to the Divine Instruments, and doing temple work increases the chances of obtaining additional divine protections and that they will likely be able to re-do the ritual to obtain them, even the most opposed come around to being eager to visit the Temple. Rozemyne suggests that they work out a rotating schedule, so that each of them gets the chance to do so, rather than having the same people attend their lord for each visit.

column1: Apart from this immediate concern, this arrangement will also have the added benefit of getting Melchior used to the Temple early, so his transition to becoming the High Bishop once Rozemyne comes of age will go more smoothly.<ref name=""P5V4C4"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 4]]. Chapter 4: Melchior and Preparing for the Temple</ref>

In the course of his visits to the Temple, Melchior also begins to donate mana to the [[Divine Instruments]]. Under Rozemyne's supervision, his first session transfers two small feystones worth of mana. When the Spring Prayer comes up in conversation, Melchior is eager to watch. Sylvester gives his permission for Melchior to accompany Rozemyne on her first leg of the journey, so he can watch the ritual being performed and see the [[Hasse]] monastery and orphanage, but refuses to allow his son to sleep there, and instead insists he be back in time for supper.

At such short notice, it is impossible to make ceremonial robes for Melchior, but Wilfried suggests he simply borrow Rozemyne's old robes, since she'll be wearing her high bishop's robe anyway. He is a little reluctant to do so when he learns that it is covered in flower-pattern embroidery, but ultimately his eagerness to join the Spring Prayer wins out over his embarrassment of wearing such feminine clothes and he asks Rozemyne to lend him her old robes.

Once at the monastery, some his his retainers appear displeased with how nobles and commoners not only eat in the same room, but at the same time, but Melchior himself doesn't seem to mind at all, showing only an expression of curiosity at all the new things to experience.<ref name=""P5V4C14"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 4]]. Chapter 14: Melchior and Spring Prayer</ref>
Due to Rozemyne's absence during Spring Prayer, Melchior was officially inaugurated as Ehrenfest's High Bishop.<ref name=""P5V12C13""/>

column1: '''Mestionora''' (メスティオノーラ, ''mesutionōra'') is the Goddess of Wisdom and one of the subordinate gods of [[Schutzaria]], the Goddess of Wind.

Mestionora is almost always depicted as a child and thus the only goddess with her hair down in illustrations and statues.<ref name=""P5V10S4"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 10]]. Gervasio — Descent of a Goddess</ref>
Statues of her are erected in the [[Royal Academy/Library

column1: She is depicted holding the book [[Grutrissheit]], the original bible. According to legend, the first king of the country was permitted to transcribe a copy of the book when he was chosen by the gods.<ref name=""P4V1C18"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 1]]. Chapter 18: Schtappe Acquisition</ref>

According to old books in [[Klassenberg]] and [[Dunkelfelger]], Mestionora is the child of [[Ewigeliebe]], the God of Life, and [[Geduldh]], the Goddess of Earth. To hide and protect her from her jealous father, the God of Darkness blessed her with hair as black as the night sky, and the Goddess of Light blessed her with golden eyes. To protect her further, she became the subordinate of [[Schutzaria]], the Goddess of Wind, who boasts the strongest defense among all the gods.
According to this legend, Mestionora was also granted the use of all the other gods' [[Divine Instruments]].<ref name=""P5V2C7""/>

At birth Mestionora had white hair and red eyes, but the [[God of Darkness]] and [[Goddess of Light]] gave her midnight blue hair and golden eyes.<ref name=""FB6QA"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]].'' [[Fanbook 6]]. Q&A with Miya Kazuki</ref>

Guardians of Knowledge are people sworn to Mestionora, the Goddess of Wisdom, and no one else. Once the oath is made, it prevents any other oath or magic contract that would bind them to someone else from taking effect. Likewise, the oath is only going to work if the supplicant isn't bound by other oaths or contracts that would interfere with their supplication to Mestionora and is genuinely honest in their desire to serve the goddess.
To take the oath, the person needs to use [[Schtappe#Stylo
column2: stylo]] to inscribe the words onto the socket of a statue of Mestionora. The ancient text is recorded on an ivory tablet kept and cared for in the [[Royal Academy/Library
column3: Royal Academy Library]] and goes as follows:

column1: I am a guardian of knowledge.
I am one who swears loyalty to Mestionora, the Goddess of Wisdom.
I shall devote all knowledge born in Yurgenschmidt to Mestionora, the Goddess of Wisdom.
I shall spread throughout Yurgenschmidt the knowledge gifted to me by Mestionora, the Goddess of Wisdom.
I respect the wisdom of humanity and shall ensure its protection.
I swear not to falter before authority, to remain courageous in the face of might, and to continue seeking and gathering knowledge, which I shall offer to the goddess.

Muriella is the birth daughter of Giebe Bessel and his third wife. Since the giebe's younger sister was unable to have a child of her own, Muriella was given to her less than a full year after her birth.<ref name=""P5V1S1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 1]]. Fantasy versus Reality</ref>
Ever since first laying eyes upon one of [[Elvira
column2: Lady Elvira]]'s romance novels, Muriella wished she could serve her. However, this proved to be a problem, since her parents loathed the Leisegangs so much, that they won't even allow their daughter to own a book written by a Leisegang noble.<ref name=""P5V1C1""/>

column1: Shortly before the purge, her baptismal mother was finally able to give birth to a child of her own, a boy. With a true born heir present and the winds of politics shifting away from the former Veroncia faction ever more, Muriella's father tried to distance himself from the sinking ship by rejecting Muriella, making her parentage default back to her biological family.

When the students are informed about the impending purge of the nobles of the former Veronica faction, they are given the choice to either return to their families and share in the traditional punishment by association, or escape the punishment by [[Nobility#Name-Swearing
column2: giving their name]] to a member of the archducal family. Since giving her name to Lady Elvira does not appear to be an option, Muriella decides to serve [[Rozemyne
column3: Lady Rozemyne]] instead, hoping that serving Elvira's baptismal daughter might grant her earlier access to Elvira's newly released romance stories.<ref name=""P5V1C1""/>

column2: Aub Ehrenfest]] visits the Royal Academy to have a discussion with [[Hirschur
column3: Professor Hirschur,]] he also takes some time to inform the students about the outcome of the purge. Afterwards, he calls Muriella to a private meeting. There he reveals to her that her baptismal mother - the woman who raised her - was in fact innocent of any crimes since at the time the Veronica faction made their moves, she had completely withdrawn from noble society to care for her baby boy. But unfortunately, she was name-sworn to [[Georgine]], leaving the Aub no choice than to execute her. With both her mothers and her birthfather executed, Muriella is required to give her name to a member of the archducal family. The Aub deeply apologizes to Muriella for how the situation turned out, but thankfully she was already prepared for this outcome and didn't have much love for the majority of her family in the first place, which greatly helps her in accepting her new lot in life.<ref name=""P5V1S1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 1]]. Fantasy versus Reality</ref>

column1: Apart from Muriella, only four more students have to give their names. Matthias and Laurenz, who are in the same situation, immediately give their names to Lady Rozemyne, since they already had their name-swearing feystones completed. Muriella, however, is unable to do the same since she has not been able to acquire the necessary materials.<ref name=""P5V12"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 1]]. Chapter 12: Finishing the Archduke Candidate Lessons</ref>

To help Muriella and the other students in the same position, Rozemyne organizes a joint trip to the gathering spot. Matthias also shares a way to more efficiently obtain high-quality feystones that he derived from Rozemyne's ditter victory in her first Royal Academy year. Rather than hunting for the strongest feybeasts, they intentionally make lesser beasts evolve by feeding them charged up feystones and quickly slaying them before they can get used to their new bodies and mana qualities.<ref name=""P5V14"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 1]]. Chapter 14: Gretia's Circumstances and Gathering Ingredients</ref>

Soon after she finishes her feystone and gives her name to Lady Rozemyne, officially entering her employ as an apprentice scholar. To her surprise and frustration, no one among Rozemyne's retainers is willing to discuss Royal Academy Love Stories with her in depth, each one either appreciating the books in a very different manner than her, or not caring for them much at all. Seeing her plight, [[Philine]] takes her along to the library where she is due to meet the [[Jossbrenner]] noble [[Lueuradi]] to discuss the crestwork her duchy is doing for Lady Rozemyne. She introduces Lueuradi and Muriella to each other, and after some small initial problems getting a conversation going, the two quickly find each other to be kindred spirits and gush about their favourite aspects of the depicted romances at length, until to their surprise the bells announce sixth bell after what felt like only a short time to them. The two promise to meet each other again on their next free day to talk again.<ref name=""P5V1S1""/>

Lady Rozemyne plans to experiment in the Ehrenfest Temple to see if the ritual to obtain divine protections can also be performed there. To help her fiancé Wilfried, Rozemyne agrees to move up the schedule and start the experiment a few days after the Feast Celebrating Spring and offers all her retainers the chance to participate. For the sake of the research, Muriella is allowed to give her name to Lady Elvira early and thus is scheduled to do the ritual twice, once before and once after the switch.

While doing the ritual the first time, she is surprised to see the symbols of all seven elements produce pillars of light. At the private discussion with Rozemyne, under the privacy of sound-blocking magic tools, she learns that the other name-sworn of Rozemyne experienced the same phenomenon and that apparently the ones sworn to someone inherit their master's elemental affinities in addition to their own.

In Rozemyne's hidden room, she retrieves Muriella's name-swearing feystone and sucks her mana out of it, which makes the cocoon disappear slowly to reveal the original white box, with the stone inside. Once this is completed, Muriella swears herself to Elvira, who gratefully accepts her. To her considerable surprise, Muriella is not in any pain while Elvira dyes the feystone.

After the switch in masters is done, Muriella re-does the ritual for divine protections and reports that she is no longer omni-elemental, now only having her own natural elements and those of Elvira.<ref name=""P5V4C11""/>

After giving her name to Elvira, Muriella serves her new lady as a retainer, but is lent to Rozemyne, while they are at the Royal Academy<ref name=""P5V7C2"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 6]]. Chapter 2: The Winter Playroom and Another New Term</ref>.

*'''Mana Affinities:''' Muriella's natural affinities are currently not known. While being sworn to Rozemyne, she was omni-elemental, but lost the elements she gained this way after her name was returned and gained those of Elvira instead, but her own and Elvira's affinities apparently do not amount to the full set of seven. The only elemental affinity Muriella has for sure is Water, which she would have gained from the divine protection of Blufanah, if she didn't have it naturally or from Elvira already<ref name=""P5V4C11""/>.

*""[[Urano Motosu]] (本須麗乃),"" Myne's name in her previous life, is a Japanese word play that means ""books must be mine."" Her new name, ""Myne,"" is a play on both ""mine"" (belonging to me) and ""main"" (main character).<ref name=""FBQA"" />
**""本"" is the kanji for ""book"", ""須"" can be interpreted as ""must be"" in kanji, and ""Urano (うらの)"" means ""my possession"" or ""mine"".

*Myne's voice actress Yuka Iguchi also voices the titular main character Index from [https://toarumajutsunoindex.fandom.com/wiki/Toaru_Majutsu_no_Index_Wiki A Certain Magical Index], a teenage nun with 103,000 grimoires (spell books) crammed into her memory -- another young clergy with her head filled with books.

*Myne is often affectionately nicknamed ""landmine"" because she is called ""Mine girl"" in the character introduction posthttps://ncode.syosetu.com/n4099cd/1/ ''本がないなら作ればいいじゃないと奔走し、問題を起こす'''地雷娘'''。''
''Worked hard for ""If there is no book then why not make some."", '''Mine girl''' that kept causing trouble.'' and used among Japanese and Chinese fans, playing on the pronunciation of her name and her tendency to cause troubles wherever she goes.

*Myne was born in the summer, which is the season of [[Leidenschaft]], the God of Fire. The season symbolizes strength and growth, which is ironic because Myne suffers from poor health and stunted growth.
*Myne's final memories before being subsumed by Urano were ""...It's so hot. It hurts. I hate thiiis..."".<ref name=""P1V1C1"" />
*Myne had dreams of Urano's world, where she could run and play and eat all she wanted. She wanted to sleep forever so she could stay in the other world.<ref name=""P1V2S2"" />

*Judging from the fact that the original Myne survived for 5 years without magic tools despite throwing tantrums often, her original mana capacity is probably less than even [[Konrad]], a typical laynoble child.

Her lack of communication with him is solely due to her adoption into the archducal family and the responsibilities that come with it. She explains that, as an archduke candidate, she can not show favoritism and has to keep even communication with her full brothers far below the level she would wish for.

After touring the Temple, Nikolaus expresses a desire to live there, rather than in the castle. column1: '''Ortwin''' (オルトヴィーン, ''Orutoviin'') is an archduke candidate from [[Drewanchel]], who currently attends the [[Royal Academy]]. He is the younger brother of [[Adolphine]].

According to his classmate [[Wilfried]], Ortwin is “quite intelligent.”<ref name=""P4V3C11"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 3]]. Chapter 11: The Tea Party for All Duchies</ref>

Despite being heavily pushed to become the next Aub Drewanchel, Ortwin himself would much rather leave the title to his half-siblings and dedicate his life to research. He finds it very difficult to disobey his sister and thus works diligently on achieving the excellence expected of the next archduke.<ref name=""RAS1C15"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Royal Academy Stories - First Year]]. Chapter 15: Ortwin - The Drewanchel Siblings</ref>
Although Ortwin is in the same year as [[Rozemyne]], they rarely interact because of how quickly she passes her classes. He is better acquainted with [[Wilfried]].

column2: Ehrenfest]] sends out invitations to all duchies for a final tea party before the Interduchy Tournament. Due to a limit on the number of people they can accommodate, they ask that each duchy only send one person (and their retainers) to attend. Ortwin is eager to go to the tea party. However, his sister [[Adolphine]] claims the spot for herself.<ref name=""P4V3C11""/>

column1: After the tea party, Adolphine hands Ortwin a small jar which contains a sample of a substance called [[Inventions#Rinsham
column2: Rinsham]], which makes a person's hair smooth and lusterous when washed with it. She asks him to analyze it over the rest of the year and come up with their own version of it before the next winter. While Ortwin is not interested in the beauty aspect of it, he is intrigued for scientific reasons.<ref name=""RAS1C15""/> Over the course of the year, he is partially successful in creating a derivate of Rinsham, but isn't able to reach the same level of quality as the original. While his product does much the same as original Rinsham, it does not make the hair quite as glossy and silky as the original. It is also slightly unpleasant to the scalp when used, according to Adolphine.

column1: In the following term at the Royal Academy, Ortwin and [[Wilfried]] share a very enthusiastic greeting and promise each other to meet and play gewinnen again, hinting that they have formed a friendship while Rozemyne was absent from the Royal Academy the previous year.<ref name=""P4V5C18"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 5]]. Chapter 18: The Second-Year Fellowship Gathering</ref>

When Adolphine borrowed books from Rozemyne, Ortwin also read them. He quite enjoyed them, but is getting rather tired of only ever getting to read the romance stories his sister borrows. At a tea party with Rozemyne, however, the Ehrenfest archduke candidate promised she would lend Ortwin a book with knight's stories through Wilfried.<ref name=""P4V7C10"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. Oswald began as a very casual person.<ref name=""P3V2C9""/> However, when [[Rozemyne]] traded places with Wilfried for a day, he was quickly put under pressure to perform in order to keep his job. Since then, he had taken his position much more seriously and has begun planning with the other attendants to ensure Wilfried remains the heir.<ref name=""P3V3S1""/>

Two days after returning with his lord from his third year at the Royal Academy, Oswald resigns from his position as Wilfried's head-attendant and retainer, stating that he could not risk creating an opening for the Leisegangs to exploit against Wilfried.<ref name=""P5V4C8""/>
In truth however, he was secretly forced to resign by [[Sylvester

column1: '''Otto''' (オットー ''Ottoo'') is the current head of the [[Gilberta Company]]. He is married to [[Corinna]], the younger sister of [[Benno]], and they have a daughter named [[Renate]].
He previously served under [[Gunther]] as a soldier at the city gate, where he taught [[Myne]] how to read and write.

Otto is ""young looking soldier with dark brown hair, and gentle, calm brown eyes.""<ref name=""P1V1C4"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 1 Volume 1]] Chapter 4: Paper: Unobtainable </ref>
Retaining his merchant-like qualities, he often barters in his dealings with others.
He is very devoted to his wife and daughter and will praise them for great length of time with minimal prompting, much to the annoyance of most listeners.

He was in the traveling merchant trade before becoming a soldier, and he still has connections with merchants. Otto originally planned on buying citizenship in a city near Frenbeltag, where he would have to pay less due to his parents owning a store there. This discount would have left him enough to open a store of his own.
However, he fell in love with Corinna at first sight. To prove he was serious, he spent all of his savings to buy citizenship in [[Ehrenfest (City)
column2: Ehrenfest]] and used his connections to obtain a job as a soldier. Despite the possibility of drawing the [[Gustav
column3: guildmaster]]'s ire, since he was trying to arrange a marriage between Corinna and one of his sons, that would lead to him never being able to do official business as a merchant again, Otto believed marrying Corinna would be well worth it.<ref name=""P1V2S1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 1 Volume 2]] Corinna's Married Life</ref>

column1: After the wedding, he moved in with Corinna on the third floor of the building which houses the Gilberta Company's store.

Despite officially working as a soldier, his duties were primarily taking care of all kinds of paperwork, as well as trading for supplies, in which his connections and experiences from his previous career as a traveling merchant helped a great deal. At heart, he never stopped being a merchant first and foremost. His duties also include teaching the new apprentices the basics of reading, writing, and math.

Due to being one of only few soldiers in his team who is both good at writing and math, he ends up doing practically all the paperwork, leading to him regularly being overworked during the busier times of the year.

He was often asked to train helpers for his math work, but refused the vast majority of them on the argument that it would be a waste of time trying to teach idiots.<ref name=""FB2S2"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Fanbook 2]]. I'm Not Givin' Up My Daughter!</ref>

When Rozemyne replies that she has no new composition she is willing to debut in class, Pauline picks up on the sub-text and once again invites her to a tea party and urges her to bring along her personal musician, eager to hear some new songs.<ref name=""P4V6C2""/>

In Rozemyne's fourth year at the Royal Academy, the girl is once again able to pass her music class right away, in the first class. Despite the flawless performance of the two songs however, Pauline insists that Rozemyne repeat one of the songs and give a blessing while playing. She states that blessings appear, when someone plays in earnest. It is unclear whether she misunderstood that it requires earnest prayer, rather than earnest music playing to give a blessing, or whether she was tasked by the royal family to prop up Rozemyne for some, to her, unknown reason.<ref name=""P5V7C4"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. column1: Philine is a cute girl with honey-coloured hair and grass-green eyes, a bit on the smaller side for her age. In [[Part 4 Volume 1]], she is about 140 cm (4’7”) tall.<ref name=""FB2CharacterSheets"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Fanbook 2]]. Character Design Sheets</ref>

Philine has a shy and humble personality, but can get rather animated when books or sweets are involved. She is also a hard worker, managing her duties as a retainer, her studies under [[Hartmut]], and her side job transcribing stories, while also keeping up with the demanding pace of her classes.

Philine was born to a laynoble family as the daughter of [[Kashick]] and his previous wife, Theresia.<ref name=""FB2FamilyTree"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Fanbook 2]]. Noble Family Tree</ref> Shortly after her little brother [[Konrad]] was born, their mother passed away. However, Philine fondly remembered the stories her mother used to tell her.

Kashick later remarried a woman named [[Jonsara]], who became Philine's and Konrad's stepmother. When she first came into the family, she got along well with the children. It was also Jonsara who taught Philine to play the Harspiel and praised her after her performance at her noble debut.<ref name=""SSC1C20"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Short Story Collection 1]]. Chapter 20: Charlotte — My Task</ref> However after the birth of her son, Jonsara's behaviour changed drastically. The change in her step-mother after the birth was so drastic that to Philine it seemed like she became an entirely different person.<ref name=""SSC1C17"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Short Story Collection 1]]. Chapter 17: Philine — Coming Home from the Royal Academy</ref>

At one point, she tried to take away Philine's compiled stories, but her father returned them shortly after since they were written on paper that was gifted to Philine by Lady Rozemyne, and it would be unwise to disrespect a gift from the archduke's family.

[[Short Story Collection 1]]. Chapter 17: Philine — Coming Home from the Royal Academy</ref>

Due to distancing herself from her family, Philine currently has no attendants or retainers of any kind outside the Royal Academy, but is able to make due thanks to living with Rozemyne's other female retainers and them helping each other with dressing and such.<ref name=""P4V9C3"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 9]]. Chapter 3: The Farewell Supper</ref>

*'''Highbeast''': Philine is more skilled at handling her [[highbeast]] than most attendants and scholars her age and rank, among other things being able to summon it surprisingly fast for a second year student. Rozemyne thinks this is due to a combination of natural talent and practice from commuting between the temple and castle so often.<ref name=""P4V5C16"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 5]]. Chapter 16: Fealty and the Dormitory</ref>

*'''Divine Protection:''' Apart from the expected protection of [[Geduldh]], Philine also managed to gain the protection of [[Mestionora]] despite neither having an affinity for Wind, nor having [[Schutzaria]]'s protection. This is likely due to working exceptionally hard as an apprentice scholar, often earnestly praying to her, and helping with the paper work of the temple.<ref name=""P5V1C6""/>
*'''Language''': While working for Lady Rozemyne, Philine has learned to read old and obscure dialects that few people in Ehrenfest are able to read these days.

column2: Ehrenfest]] province of Leisegang, but the position has since passed to [[Count Leisegang
column3: his grandson]]. Despite his advanced age, he still remains a leading member of the [[Ehrenfest (Duchy)#Leisegang Faction
column4: Leisegang political faction]]. He is also [[Karstedt]]'s grandfather and [[Rozemyne]]'s great-grandfather.

column1: The previous Giebe Leisegang is a very old man and has grown infirm due to his advanced age. He barely ever leaves his mansion and needs a stick to walk when he does.<ref name=""P4V3C18"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 3]]. Chapter 18: The Book Fair and the Follow-Up Meeting</ref> According to his retainers, he collapses quite often, to the point where they seem to consider it normal.<ref name=""P4V3C16"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 3]]. Chapter 16: Philine's Family Circumstances</ref>

He used to have reddish-brown hair, but had gone completely bald by the time Rozemyne first met him. It is unclear whether his eyebrows still retained any colour or had gone white.<ref name=""FB6QA""/>

To Rozemyne, the previous Giebe Leisegang appeared like a good-natured, doting grandpa, but one should not underestimate him. He is a very cunning and politically savvy man and a master-manipulator, who is still a major factor in Ehrenfest's political landscape, despite his advanced age and poor health.<ref name=""P4V3E"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 3]]. Epilogue</ref>

He has a tendency to use his disabilities and age as a shield. When things he does not wish to hear are said, he often pretends not to have heard it due to his poor hearing. He even sometimes entirely ignores the presence of people he is not fond of. It is at times difficult what he is genuinely unaware of and what he pretends to not notice out of obstinacy.<ref name=""P4V8C10"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 8]]. Chapter 10: Visiting Great-Grandfather</ref>

The previous Count Leisegang's daughter was once married to the son of the Fourth Aub Ehrenfest, who was expected to become the next archduke. Despite having been wed as the first wife, the arrival of [[Gabriele]] of [[Ahrensbach]] led to her being demoted to the position of second wife. On top of that, her husband was eventually removed from his archduke candidacy for fear of causing political strife in the duchy, and became the first [[Groschel

At the same time, the then-archduke had instructed the previous Count Leisegang to wed his youngest daughter to [[Bonifatius]], hoping to appease the Leisegangs and bring order back to the duchy. However, Bonifatius renounced his claim to the seat of archduke and actively surrendered it to his younger brother, [[Adelbert]], who became the Sixth [[Aub Ehrenfest]].

Then, the Sixth Aub Ehrenfest married [[Veronica]], the daughter of Gabriele. Not only did she have Ahrensbach blood, but she ended up mistreating the descendants of the previous Count Leisegang and rallying her political faction against them. As a result, the previous Count Leisegang became vehemently opposed to those of Veronica's descent and determined to see an archduke of Leisegang descent in Ehrenfest.

During the reign of the Sixth Aub Ehrenfest and later under [[Sylvester]], Veronica mistreated basically anyone who wasn't a clear ally to her, with the Leisegangs in particular due to their influence and open opposition to anyone with Ahrensbach blood. This fall from grace and decades long abuse has fostered a deep hatred for all of Gabriele's descendants in the previous Count Leisegang, even when the individual in question never personally wronged him or his kin.<ref name=""P4V8C10""/>
When Rozemyne gathered an expanded circle of nobles to teach her [[Rozemyne Mana Compression Method
column2: mana compression method]] to, the previous Giebe Leisegang fought with his grandson, the current [[Count Leisegang]] to attend as well and was ultimately successful. But in truth learning the mana compression method was only an excuse, since he really wanted to meet his great-granddaughter at least once before his death. When he came face-to-face with Rozemyne and the two exchanged noble greetings, they both seemed very happy to meet each other, but only for a moment since he collapsed before Rozemyne could fully voice her response. His retainers assured Lady Rozemyne that she was not at fault and that it was quite common for him to collapse like this, before carrying him out of the room to care for him.<ref name=""P4V3C16""/>

column1: Later at the yearly book fair, he is first in line and buys one of every available book.<ref name=""P4V3C18""/>

Despite his failing health and retirement he is still involving himself in Ehrenfest's politics, very actively advocating for Rozemyne to become the next Aub. He already got [[Haldenzel]] and Groschel on his side and is current working to convince [[Illgner]] to join him as well, which due to how much Rozemyne helped that province has a good chance of success.<ref name=""P4V3E""/>

After the announcement of Rozemyne's and [[Wilfried]]'s engagement, most nobles abandoned the idea of Rozemyne becoming the next Aub, but despite this setback, the Leisegangs and the previous Giebe Leisegang in particular keep at it.

In the spring following her second year at the [[Royal Academy]], Rozemyne, Wilfried, and Charlotte visit Leisegang for [[Spring Prayer]] and to put the finishing touches on the establishment of the printing and paper-making industries. During this visit, the three archduke children also personally visit the previous Count Leisegang to attempt to convince him to stop trying to make Rozemyne the next Aub Ehrenfest.

During the meeting, he collapses multiple times, though Rozemyne is unsure whether he genuinely fell unconscious or was just pretending. Even just getting him to acknowledge Charlotte's and Wilfried's very presence in the room took some work. Once Rozemyne managed this, Wilfried assures him that he will do everything in his power to right the wrongs of the past and not repeat his predecessors' mistakes. To this end, he reveals that should there ever be another incident like with Gabriele, with a woman from a higher-ranked duchy forcing a marriage with Wilfried resulting in Rozemyne's demotion to second wife, any child of Rozemyne and him would be adopted by Sylvester to preserve their archduke candidate status, even though this would almost assuredly enrage the new bride and her duchy.<ref name=""P4V8C10""/>

Shortly after Ehrenfest's internal purge of the former Veronica faction and those aligned with Georgine, the previous Count Leisegang passes away peacefully, his thirst for revenge against Gabriele, Veronica, and their ilk finally sated by the reprisals meted out in the purge. Due to seeing his wish to have Rozemyne made the next Aub Ehrenfest as his dying wish, rather than calming down, several of the older members of the Leisegang faction are reinvigorated in their attempts to make this happen, either not knowing or not caring that this is the last thing Rozemyne herself wants.<ref name=""P5V4E""/>

column1: She considers him a rare genius, second only to [[Ferdinand]], though where Ferdinand's talents lie in coming up with new ideas and innovation, Raimund has shown immense talent in improving and optimizing other people's inventions and minimizing the mana-usage of existing magic tools.<ref name=""P4V6C12"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 6]]. Chapter 12: Professor Hirschur’s Laboratory</ref>

Rozemyne first lays eyes upon Raimund when she meets Professor Hirschur at her laboratory to discuss a magic circle she is in the process of developing, intended to make lent out books return to the library and sort themselves back into the shelves by themselves once the lending period has expired.

Upon seeing what a huge mess the room is, Rozemyne's attendant [[Lieseleta]] scolds Hirschur about how unacceptable it was to accept a visitor of her lady's status to such a place and shows off a [[Magic Tools#Cleaning Magic Tool
column2: cleaning magic tool]] she brought along due to expecting such a situation. Immediately getting the message, Hirschur and Raimund quickly start to pick anything of value up off the floor and evacuate it to the tables, after which Lieseleta uses the magic tool to clean the floor. While this is going on, Rozemyne's other attendants set up one of the tables for tea and snacks she had brought along. After some more scolding about how dirty they themselves and their clothes are, the professor uses [[Spells and Prayers#Waschen
column3: waschen]] to also clean herself and her disciple.

column1: Between her work obsession and hunger, Hirschur entirely forgets to introduce her disciple until Rozemyne herself asks for an introduction. At this point, Rozemyne and her retainers learn that Raimund is from [[Ahrensbach]], causing her guard knights to jump between them and [[Cornelius]] to question Hirschur's loyalty and mental state, wondering out loud whether she has any idea what has been going on between Ahrensbach and Ehrenfest the last couple of years. Hirschur calmly explains that while she was born in Ehrenfest, she is a citizen of the [[Sovereignty]] now, and as a professor of the Royal Academy, she has a responsibility to nurture talent she find for the good of [[Yurgenschmidt]] as a whole and can not afford to be limited by inter-duchy politics. She goes further to state that if she was that kind of person, she never would have taken Ferdinand under her wing, since doing so received considerable pushback from the Veronica faction and earned her many toxic messages from [[Veronica
column2: Lady Veronica]] herself back in the day. Hearing all this, Rozemyne manages to get her guard knights to back off, though they remain on guard against Raimund.

column1: With both Hirschur and Raimund appearing to have skipped at least one meal due to being immersed in their work, they both dig in once the obligatory exchanging of first sips and bites has been finished, eating as fast as they can without violating noble table manners.

Following the snack, Rozemyne asks Hirschur to evaluate a magic circle she developed for the purpose of books returning to the library on their own once the lending period has expired. Hearing Rozemyne mention books she received from Ferdinand during her explanation causes Raimund a minor emotional outburst, but when Rozemyne turns toward her scholar [[Hartmut]] about whether they could show the books to Raimund, he immediately shuts her down before she can even finish the sentence, stating that they can not show Lord Ferdinand's books to a noble from another duchy without his express permission.

Upon inspecting the magic circle Rozemyne had drawn up, Hirschur calls it outright useless, only going on to go into more details when prompted. There is nothing wrong with the circle itself, and it will fulfill the desired functions just fine, but due to its complexity, it will require far too much mana for anyone below archduke candidate levels of mana capacity to use them, which would include [[Solange
column2: Professor Solange]], the currently sole librarian of the [[Royal Academy/Library
column3: Royal Academy's library]], who is only a mednoble. She passes the paper on to her disciple and tells him to demonstrate his talents by turning Rozemyne's work into something even he as a mednoble could use.

column1: After commenting on how impressed he is how much functionality Rozemyne was able to cram into a single magic circle, Raimund begins breaking it down and splitting the functions into two separate circles, explaining that it is better to split the necessary from the quality-of-life features. Separating the circle also come with the added benefit of allowing the function to return the books to their places among the shelves to also be used for books that have not left the library.

Doing this allows Raimund to strip out many elements that Rozemyne had to add to make the two functions compatible with each other, like for example, a section of Life-mana that then needed to be balanced with Earth-mana, so it wouldn't clash with the other types associated with Fire, Water, and Wind. Apart from added functionality, this would also drastically reduce the amount of mana any magic tools made with these circles would require to function, and the lessened complexity would also help to make it less likely for errors to happen during the drawing of the circles.
During his work, he offhandedly mentions that in all likelihood using [[Plant Paper#Verification Paper
column2: verification paper]] will further cut down on mana use, which catches Rozemyne completely off guard, since she believes that only duchies with which they are trading and the Sovereignty would know of verification paper. But as it turns out, [[Gundolf
column3: Professor Gundolf]] from [[Drewanchel]] had been talking quite passionately about it and his eagerness to research it during one of his classes, spreading the knowledge to essentially every duchy of the country.<ref name=""P4V6C12""/>

column1: Surprisingly to Raimund, this meeting leads to [[Ferdinand
column2: Lord Ferdinand]] taking a personal interest in Raimund's case. As far as Raimund knows, Rozemyne was so impressed with his talent that she suggested Ferdinand take him on as his disciple. For this purpose, Ferdinand issues Raimund with a series of questions as a test, mostly about Ahrensbach's geography, followed by a series of magic tools and circles that the boy is to improve to demonstrate his abilities. If he manages to pass these tests, Ferdinand will take him on as a long-distance disciple, with even the chance to become Ferdinand's retainer once he comes of age, should he wish to do so and get permission from his home duchy.

column1: What Raimund does not know is that Ferdinand only in part does this out of an interest in his talents, but is more concerned with cultivating him as an information source to gather data on Ahrensbach, though his offer to take him as a retainer in the future is genuine.<ref name=""P4V6C13""/>

Raimund is overjoyed with this development and, upon seeing Rozemyne the next time, thanks her deeply for opening up this opportunity for him, before charging off toward Hirschur's lab to finish the second part of his assignment.<ref name=""P4V6C15"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 6]]. Chapter 15: Gathering Feystones</ref>
In the following summer, [[Georgine]] and [[Detlinde]] are scheduled to visit [[Ehrenfest (Duchy)
column2: Ehrenfest]]. Ferdinand states that he wishes to take Raimund on as a retainer upon his graduation and uses this to request that he be allowed to visit Ehrenfest alongside the two women.

column1: During the visit, he is able to present Ferdinand and Rozemyne the [[Magic_Tools#Teleportation_Circle
column2: teleportation circles]] he modified as a task for his mentor. This version of the magic circle is considerably smaller and requires far less mana than the regular one, but only allows for comparatively small objects to be transported. During tests conducted by [[Philine]] and [[Damuel]], they ascertain that the circles are well capable of teleporting books - which is what they were primarily designed to do - and that even an average laynoble should be able to use them about ten times before requiring a [[Magic Potions#Rejuvenation Potions
column3: rejuvenation potion]]. Rozemyne purchases the modified circles pretty much on the spot. Much to Raimund's surprise, Ferdinand allows this, despite the specifications coming from him, which many other professors would have likely used as a way to take the credit or at least take a cut of the money.

column1: Rozemyne further requests that Raimund modify a voice-recording magic tool, so it will not only be smaller and run off of only a single feystone, but also stay usable for a long time and without restrictions as to how often the recorded messages can be played. To accomplish this difficult task, Ferdinand gives Raimund access to his notes on the magic circles of [[Schwartz and Weiss]] which incorporate a circle for long-term preservation of effects.<ref name=""P4V8C20"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 8]]. Chapter 20: Ferdinand’s Estate</ref>

As the third wife, Ralfrieda won't have to interact with nobles from other duchies, thus sparing her the ridicule they would most likely heap on her, for her unwitting assistance to the Lanzenave invaders, instead giving her the chance to enjoy a quiet life, out of the public eye, while supporting her husband from behind the scenes in their new duchy.<ref name=""P5V12C18""/>

column1: '''Raublut''' (ラオブルート, ''Raoburūto'') is the former commander of the Sovereign Knight's Order (中央騎士団, Chūō kishi-dan).<ref name=""P4V7C7"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 7]]. Chapter 7: The Ternisbefallen Inquiry</ref>
After being subdued during the [[Lanzenave]] invasion, his [[Schtappe]] was destroyed and faces life in imprisonment for treason and rebellion against the Zent.<ref name=""P5V12C11"" />
According to Rozemyne, he gives off ""STRONG vibes"" much like [[Karstedt]] and [[Bonifatius]].<ref name=""P4V7C7""/>
He has a prominent scar above his left cheek.<ref name=""P5V1P"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 9]]. Prologue</ref>
Raublut has a tendency to speak in short and precise sentences and accordingly gives brief and easy to understand explanations.<ref name=""P5V1S2""/>

He is not at all fond of paperwork, and pushes it off to other people, whenever it is an option. Before her assignment to the Royal Academy Library, he left the applicable administrative tasks to his wife Hortensia, but now that she is busy with her own job, he makes his subordinate take up the slack.<ref name=""P5V5S2""/>

Raublut was born in [[Gilessenmeyer]], as part of an archducal branch family. He hated the infighting and jostling for positions so much, that he decided to give his all to become a sovereign knight to escape it and eventually succeeded in this. He became the retainer of the third prince.
His first assignment as a sovereign knight was to guard the members of House Loweleier of [[Lanzenave]], whenever they left the [[Royal Academy#Adalgisa Villa
column2: Adalgisa Villa]]. Raublut initially misunderstood this assignment as guarding solely [[Valamarlene
column3: Lady Valamarlene]] and was quite surprised, when he was later called upon to also guard her younger brother [[Gervasio]].

column1: During their time together, he developed a deep respect and loyalty to Gervasio and fell in love with Valamarlene. He also came to believe that Gervasio, due to his intellect and mana capacity surpassing that of any of the royal princes - including the chosen successor Second [[Waldifried
column2: Prince Waldifried]]- would be best suited to became the next Zent of Yurgenschmidt. Gervasio tried and eventually succeeded in arranging an engagement between Raublut and Valamarlene, but this eventually fell through, when the current flower of Loweleider, [[Seradina]] was turned into a feystone in place of her son [[Quinta
column3: Ferdinand]], with the latter somehow being released from the villa and adopted by [[Adelbert
column4: Aub Ehrenfest]], and Valamarlene was called upon to replace her deceased sister as Loweleier's flower. Raublut tried to find out what happened, but was only told that it was due to ""the guidance of the Goddess of Time."" Having been denied the marriage with her, Raublut swore to Gervasio before the latter's departure to Lanzenave, that he would protect her.

column2: civil war]] the third prince was assassinated and Raublut became the retainer of the fifth prince, [[Trauerqual]]. To forge a stronger bond between those of Trauerqual's retainers who were formerly in the second and third princes' employ and strengthen the relationship to [[Klassenberg]], Raublut agreed to marry [[Hortensia]], a former Klassenberg noble and scholar of Prince Waldifried. Both of them had no feelings for each other, but considered it their duty to go through with the wedding. Unfortunately, they were never able to have any children together, which layed heavily on Hortensia's spirit.<ref name=""P5V1S2""/>

column1: After the conclusion of the civil war, the Adalgisa Villa was closed and all the residents were executed, including Valamarlene, much to Raublut's horror. He couldn't fulfill his promise to his dear friend and true liege Gervasio. This fostered a deep hatred toward the Yurgenschmidt royal family in his heart.

Depsite the hatred, over time Raublut developed a grudging respect and sympathy for the struggling Trauerqual, for his hard work and all the sacrifices he made to keep the country running without a [[Grutrissheit]]. But at the same time, it made Raublut only more sure that the current royal family was unsuited to lead the country and thus began to secretly reach out to his old friend and true liege, while lying the groundwork for a coup, which was supposed to have Gervasio take the throne of Yurgenschmidt.<ref name=""P5V9E"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 9]]. Epilogue</ref>

He was able to contact Gervasio when he was visiting Ahrensbach to investigate the ternisbefallen incident. Georgine used trug on Raublut in an attempt to control him and his investigation. However, from his experience in the Adalgisa villa, Raublut recognized the smell and asked Georgine where she obtained it from. From there, Georgine acted as an intermediary between Gervasio and Raublut as her position allowed her to be and they started to plan the coup attempt that also included assassination of Ferdinand and the invasion of Ehrenfest by Georgine.
His position as the trusted knight commander who has served Zent Trauerqual faithfully for a long time helped him a great deal in his clandestine scheming on behalf of Gervasio.

Raublut is acquainted with Prince Hildebrand since the latter's birth. Over the course of the years, he occasionally gifted the prince toys.<ref name=""P5V1P""/> When he is not otherwise busy with his duties to the royal family, he personally trains Prince Hildebrand in sword fighting.<ref name=""P5V5E""/>
[[Myne]] first meets Raublut at an inquiry into the [[Feybeasts#Feybeasts_from_spoiler_content
column2: ternisbefallen]] attack on the Royal Academy grounds during her second term at the Royal Academy.
Prince Hildebrand]], Rozemyne has to answer questions as to how she was able to give the [[Spells_and_Prayers#God_of_Darkness.27s_Prayer
column3: blessing of the God of Darkness]] and regrow all the damage the beast did inside the Ehrenfest gathering spot.

column1: At the meeting, Rozemyne was able to allay most of the suspicions leveled against her, but this also threw up questions on potential differences between the [[Bible#High Bishop's Bible
column2: High Bishop's bibles]] in the Sovereignty and Ehrenfest. To look into this, the inquiry is adjourned for three days to allow Ehrenfest to send their High Bishop and Rozemyne's guardian [[Ferdinand]] to bring their bible to the Royal Academy.<ref name=""P4V7C7""/>

column1: Naturally, this also meant that the [[Relichion
column2: Sovereign High Bishop]], as the custodian of the Sovereignty's bible, also needed to be invited. When everyone was gathered together, they made some interesting discoveries about the bibles. First, the fact that the High Bishop's bibles are magic tools, with protective enchantments that made the pages appear blank to anyone without direct permission from the relevant High Bishop, was revealed to the gathered nobles, when prior this knowledge appears to only have been known to members of the clergy. In addition to this, there are also passages of text that are even blank to people with said permission, unless they fulfilled certain requirements. Of the people present and with permission, only Prince Hildebrand, Rozemyne, Ferdinand, and Raublut are able to read certain pages - including the one containing the prayer to the God of Darkness - but not the Sovereign High Bishop or High Priest, which also explains why Immanuel was unaware of the prayer being contained in the bible. While it is not known what exactly the requirements to being able to read those passages are, based on the people who can and can not read them Ferdinand speculates it to be either an issue of mana capacity or elemental affinities.

column1: With both the Sovereign Knight's Commander and a member of the royal family confirming that the prayer is indeed there, and that consequently Rozemyne had been telling the truth all along, she is cleared of all accusations, despite Professor Fraularm's constant attempts to have her charged with anything and everything she could twist into something resembling a crime or breaking of a rule.<ref name=""P4V7C8"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 7]]. Chapter 8: The Bible Inspection Meeting</ref>
Following Prince Hildebrand's royal debut and the announcement of his engagement with [[Letizia
column2: Lady Letizia]] of [[Ahrensbach]], Raublut visits the prince in his villa. While there, he hands the prince a new toy and a box containing a feystone with a secret message. He informs the prince that in the coming semester in the Royal Academy, he is to gather information on Lady Rozemyne and that his sister-in-law [[Eglantine]] will be sent to the Royal Academy to teach the Archduke Candidate Course and a new female archlibrarian would be appointed. He suspects that the latter assignment is due to Anastasius wishing to keep Eglantine away from other men as much as possible. It also serves as a useful test of Rozemyne to see if she is willing to turn over mastership of the library magic tools [[Schwartz and Weiss]] or if she will selfishly try to keep them to herself.

column1: In the secret message, which Hildebrand is to only listen to in his hidden room, he tells him that the only way to get out of his unwanted marriage is to become king himself. Raublut confides to Hildebrand that he believes that should he acquire the lost Grutrissheit, [[Trauerqual
column2: his father]] would step down without opposition..<ref name=""P5V1P""/>

column1: <!-- missing events, in particular Hortensia's investigation of Schlaftraum flowers and subsequent ""illness""-->

It is later revealed that Raublut killed Hortensia, but is able to pass it off as a natural death, as some point during or shortly after the conclusion of the regular study season in Rozemyne's fourth' year at the academy. He tells only [[Solange
column2: Professor Solange]] and asks her to keep her confidence, until the official announcement is made at the archduke conference.

column1: After Gervasio obtains the final tablet from the [[Royal Academy#Shrines
column2: Royal Academy Shrines]], Raublut takes him and his retainers to the Royal Academy Library, with some of the retainers disguised as Sovereign Knights and others being brought under the excuse of retrieving Hortensia's belongings from her room in the library.

column1: It is later revealed that Raublut killed his wife, though he is able to dress it up as a natural passing. He uses her death to sneak Lanzenave retainers into the Royal Academy under the pretense that they were there to retrieve Horentsia's belongings from her room in the library and looks for the keys to the underground archive there. He is able to use Hortensia's feystone to enter her room, but the keys aren't there, so he binds Solange up in bands of light and threatens to torture her attendant, if she doesn't give them the key, which Solange eventually does. Due to Gervasio liking Solange, Raublut does not harm her and promises that he will release her, once his master has obtained the Grutrissheit.

As planned three of Gervasio's retainers take possession of a key each and are thus able to unlock the underground archive. Despite Gervasio being registered as a member of a royal branch family, thanks to Raublut somehow getting someone within the Sovereign Temple on their side, Gervasio is still unable to pass the barrier before the room with the magic tool Grutrissheit.

Upon informing Raublut of how the barrier rejected him, he muses how he is certain that the Ehrenfest archduke candidate was on the right path to the Grutrissheit and inquires were it was, that she vanished. Learning from his subordinate that it was on the second floor of the library they head there and Gervasio is quickly convinced that the statue of [[Mestionora]] must be the key. Shortly after he touches it, he disappears from in front of Raublut.<ref name=""P5V9E""/>
Shortly after the Zent Candidates disappear from the altar, [[Werdekraf
column3: Lady Magdalena]] manage to defeat and subdue Raublut. Under normal circumstances he would have faces execution for his crimes, but due to the [[Mestionora
column4: Goddess of Wisdom]] decreeing that no more life shall be lost, the perpetrators of the rebellion are instead sentenced to have their schtappe destroyed and become prisoners, and have their mana regularly drained for the benefit of the duchy they are sent to, for the rest of their life.<ref name=""P5V12C11""/>

column1: *Raublut kept his scar intentionally, rather than having it healed, as a reminder to himself of his pain and regrets.<ref name=""FB5QA"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Fanbook 5]]. Q&A with [[Miya Kazuki]]</ref>

column2: Zent]] of [[Yurgenschmidt]] in the ancient past.<ref name=""P5V8C9"" />

column1: Founder of the [[Royal Family]] structure, creator of [[Schwartz and Weiss]]. She managed to gain all seventy-nine Divine Protections. Moved Royal Palace to the [[Sovereignty]] as a protection against assassination. Sealed the six villas connecting the Holy Land to the six original duchies.

column2: Zent Rauchelstra]], a true Zent, who obtained her Book of Mestionora from [[Erwaermen]], believed that the cause for the many violent fights of succession, to be that anyone could become Zent and thus created a magic barrier in the corridor leading to the room of the failsafe magic tool, that would only allow those through, who are registered with the royal family. Her reasoning was that since her house was vehemently opposed to warfare, only allowing members of her family and their descendants access to the means to become Zent, would end the fights over succession permanently.<ref name=""P5V8C9"" />

column1: To further ensure the safety of this new system, she created [[Schwartz and Weiss]] as guardians, but disguised them as library magic tools, so they could keep an eye on potential Zent Candidates. That they call their master milady, goes back to [[Rauchelstra
column2: Zent Rauchelstra]], in an age when the concept of a princess hadn't existed yet. She also moved the holy land to within the royal palace and made it, so it could only be accessed via teleportation doors, thus making it near impossible for rebels to gain access to the failsafe magic tool, without the permission of the ruling Zent. column1: Initially these actions were harshly criticized, but when the number of conflicts really did drop, those critics quieted down and many nobles even came to praise [[Rauchelstra]]'s actions. With access to the holy land so highly restricted, the royal family had to carry out large scale ceremonies completely on their own, leading them first to scale down the size of the ceremonies and over time abandon some of them entirely. Likewise without a chance to become a Zent candidate, the nobles from the duchies had less of a reason to participate in any religious ceremonies and thus the door opened for religious services to be looked down on. Not long after Rozemyne left, the mayor organizes an attack on the monastery, but the barrier around the building prevents the attackers from getting near.

With the help of [[Ferdinand]], Rozemyne is able to approach Kantna and have the contract for the two orphan girls nullified. She then proceeds to pay the mayor for the four orphans, making their status as grey priests official.

column1: Rico is one of the smallest and youngest children locked up in the temple orphanage's basement, at the time [[Myne]] becomes an [[Temple_Hierarchy#Apprentice_Blue_Priest
column2: Apprentice Shrine Maiden]]. His days consist of just languishing of his pile of hay, looking out window, too high up for the children to reach, tracking time by the passage of the sun and waiting for divine gifts to arrive in the cellar. Since the children are arranged by age, with the oldest staying the closest to the main entrance door, and the youngest the furthest away, Rico has a much harder time getting food, than the older ones. By the time the divine gifts make it all the way to him, barely a few scraps are left and even they are often stolen by the stronger children. One day before Myne first sneaks an extra basket of bread into the cellar, Rico is in such a weakened state, that he is barely able to raise himself up onto the chair. When his single piece of soup-soaked bread is knocked from his hand, when an older and taller boy tries to steal it, he dives after it and eats it off the filthy floor and swallowed it down, with all the grit, hay and whatever else clung to it.

column1: When Gil and Myne come to the cellar for the first time, due to being among the smallest, Rico is closest to the backdoor and eagerly devours a loaf of bread, which Gil had dropped, not even noticing or caring that the bump he heard was Sister Myne fainting and crashing to the floor.

The next day, when Gil comes again, the apprentice gray priest makes sure that the food is shared equally, that the older children do not steal from the younger and weaker ones and that everyone uses their spoons, rather than touching the food with their dirty hands. At the end of the day, Rico is sated fro the first time since he can remember and the usually deathly quiet cellar, has some quiet conversation between the children, equally for the first in a long time.<ref name=""SSC2C2""/>

column1: '''Rozemary''' (ローゼマリー, ''Roozemarii'') is the deceased third wife of [[Karstedt]].

Rozemary was born to a mednoble family. However, due to her unusually large [[mana]] capacity she was able to marry into the archnoble family of the [[Knight's Order]] Commander [[Karstedt]] as his third wife.<ref name=""P2V4C14"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 2 Volume 4]]. Chapter 14: The New Me</ref>

Having their daughter married to the Knight's Order Commander himself made the rest of Rozemary's family arrogant. They made demands far above their station, leading to a serious feud between them and Karstedt's second wife [[Trudeliede]], who in turn went on to bully Rozemary severely, which only made her already poor health deteriorate further.
Due to his deep love for Rozemary, Karstedt took her side in this family struggle, forcing his first wife [[Elvira]] to take Trudeliede's side to keep the balance.
Eventually, Rozemary died from her health issues roughly one year after [[Myne]] was born into this world.<ref name=""P3V1P"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 3 Volume 1]]. Prologue</ref>

Sylvester later uses these facts to construct Rozemyne's cover story, spinning a tale of Rozemary dying in or shortly after childbirth and Karstedt sending Rozemyne to the temple to keep her save from Trudeliede and her family.

Due to the practices of the nobility, [[Elvira]] accepted Rozemyne as her own child at her [[baptism]], rendering Rozemyne's biological mother irrelevant. As Elvira makes clear during Viscount Joisontak's interrogation, accepting the girl as her own daughter during the baptism overrides any and all previous conditions, rendering any existing biological relation to Rozemary's family null and void for all intents and purposes.<ref name=""P3V5S1""/>
*Viscount Joisontak, Rozemary's older brother, tried to abduct Rozemyne at the end of Part 3.

*Miya Kazuki in [[Fanbook 3]] describes her as a mischievous imp who changed her attitude depending on the person she was talking to. She was skilled at acting sweet and was exactly the kind of woman, men like but women hate.
