column1: Rozemyne cares deeply about her friends and loved ones, and she will act without hesitation to protect them from danger. However, she draws a clear distinction between those she feels responsible for and those she is indifferent to.<ref name=""P4V1P1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 1]]. Prologue</ref> Because she's strongly averse towards suffering and shows concern to others regardless of social status, she has a reputation for being compassionate and is often scolded for being “too soft.”<ref name=""P4V1C1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 2]]. Chapter 1: Meeting for the Tea Party.</ref>

In addition, Rozemyne has a soft spot for younger siblings, like [[Kamil]] and [[Charlotte]]. She tries her hardest to look good in front of them, enjoys their praise and admiration, and is extremely protective towards them. She is also caring and compassionate towards younger children in general, including temple orphans and even those from opposing factions, like [[Letizia]] and [[Ehrenfest (Duchy)#Veronica Faction

column2: Myne’s]] carefree and lively personality. Although she learns how to conceal her emotions and act gracefully in the manner expected of a [[Nobility
column3: noble]] of her status, her candid nature occasionally still shines through. She has been reprimanded on several occasions for speaking too openly to high-status nobles,<ref name=""P4V2C14"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 2]]. Chapter 14: Reporting to the Prince.</ref> and she is aware that she is not very socially adept.

column1: Deeply influenced by her experience as an apprentice merchant, Rozemyne prefers to be independent and self-sufficient. She believes that even nobles should not be above earning their own money,<ref name=""P4V1C13"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 1]]. Chapter 13: Mana Compression and Creating a Highbeast.</ref> and she insists on personally covering all her expenses. She also believes in providing fair compensation for anything of value, including products, services, and knowledge. Karstedt reflects that while she looks like a child, she has “the rational mind of an adult.”<ref name=""P3V1P1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 1]]. Prologue.</ref> She has proven to be exceedingly competent when required and capable of learning quickly.

Despite her mature outlook, she often rushes headlong into new situations without thinking, which can cause a wide range of unpredictable outcomes. She tends to lose her temper and her sense of perspective when her books or her loved ones are at stake.

Rozemyne is a false persona devised by [[Sylvester]], [[Ferdinand]], and [[Karstedt]] to allow her to become a noble for her own protection. Using a magic contract, Sylvester changed Myne’s name and forced her lower city family to swear to treat her as a stranger. Her old identity, [[Myne]], is legally dead.

Originally, Sylvester suggested that Rozemyne be baptized as the daughter of Karstedt's late third wife, [[Rozemary]], who like Rozemyne had an unusually high amount of [[mana]]. According to this story, Rozemyne was hidden in the Ehrenfest [[Temple]] in secret to protect her from the power struggle between Karstedt's first two wives and his third wife after Rozemary’s death.

However, Elvira immediately saw through this story. She pointed out that introducing Rozemyne as Rozemary’s daughter would reignite the familial conflict. Instead, she agreed to baptize Rozemyne as her own true daughter as a favor to Ferdinand.<ref name=""P1V3P1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 1 Volume 1]]. Prologue.</ref> In private, [[Cornelius]] is told the original cover story, that Rozemyne is Rozemary’s daughter.<ref name=""P3V1S1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 1]]. Being My Little Sister’s Knight.</ref>

Rozemyne’s prior absence from the nobility was excused by the fact that nobles don't typically announce their children until their [[baptism]]. She was re-baptized the next summer and formally announced to the nobility, then immediately adopted by Sylvester as the daughter of the archduke.

To justify the baptism, Rozemyne’s official age is one year younger than Myne’s. This also helped to explain her small size, since the slow growth caused by the [[Devouring]] makes her look at least two years younger than girls her age.

Rozemyne continues to employ her existing attendants from her time as an apprentice shrine maiden, as well as her guard knight [[Damuel]]. She also gains additional guards and retainers to her service, as expected for a noble of her status.
*'''Blessings:''' Rozemyne has shown great proficiency with a variety of [[Blessing
column2: blessings]], and can invoke multiple gods at once. She occasionally gives blessings unintentionally by praying and by singing religious songs. She successfully improvised a blessing that did not follow the exact wording of an established prayer.

column1: *'''Enhancement Magic:''' In order to compensate for her muscle atrophy resulted from prolonged hibernation in [[Jureve]], Rozemyne learned enhancement magic with the help of Ferdinand's magic tools. By practicing with [[Bonifatius]], she eventually became proficient enough to selectively enhance part of her body.

*'''Highbeast:''' Rozemyne's [[highbeast]] [[Lessy]] is designed to be drivable. She can increase or decrease its size at will, allowing her to carry several passengers and their luggage together when necessary. She's also protected from most external harm when she is inside. It is modeled after a Red Panda, but also bears a resemblance to the foul-smelling and vicious [[Feybeasts#Grun
*'''Mana Affinities:''' Rozemyne possesses all seven elemental affinities, a rare occurrence normally found only in royalty and in archduke candidates of greater duchies.

*'''Divine Protections:''' Rozemyne obtained divine protections from 43 deities, including all 7 primary gods, which lowers her mana consumption for spells and brewing to about 40% of what it was before the ritual. To avoid standing out too much, however, she keeps this a secret. Two of the subordinate gods she has protections from are Chaosfliehe and Verbergen.<ref name=""P5V4C11"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 4]]. Chapter 11: Reobtaining Divine Protections</ref>

The Saint's Ritual</ref> While her family and a few trusted individuals are aware that this number is a lie and that she has considerably more divine protections than this, only the princes [[Sigiswald]] and [[Anastasius]] are privy to the exact number.<ref name=""P5V2C1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 2]]. Chapter 1: The Royal Family and the Library</ref>
*'''Divine Instrument Manifestation:''' Rozemyne is able to morph her schtappe into all the [[Divine Instruments]] of the primary seven gods and [[Divine Instruments#Verfuhremeer's Staff

**'''Grutrissheit:''' Rozemyne obtained the remaining content of Ferdinand's Book of Mestionora during her fourth year in the Royal Academy. It has enough content to operate country gates, but not enough to carry out duties as a Zent.

*'''Mana Capacity:''' Rozemyne has an extremely high mana capacity, even by archduke candidate standards. At the young age of 7, she has already surpassed every other noble in Ehrenfest - including the [[Sylvester
column2: Aub]] - except for [[Ferdinand]]. None of her peers came close when she enrolled in the [[Royal Academy]].

column1: *'''Magecraft:''' Due to her own extensive reading and brewing practices under Ferdinand's strict guidance, Rozemyne's knowledge and skills in mana manipulation, magic circles, and potion brewing far exceed her peers. Her cooking experiences as a commoner also gives her a significant advantage in ingredients preparation, especially when compared against fellow nobles that never did any manual labor in their life thus far.<ref name=""P4V6C7"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 6]]. Chapter 7: Brewing and Recovery Potions</ref>

*'''Multiple Schtappe Manifestation:''' Rozemyne is able to manifest two copies of her schtappe at once and even sustain two schtappe morphed into [[Divine Instruments]] at the same time.<ref name=""P5V2C7"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 2]]. Chapter 7: The Royal Academy’s Dedication Ritual</ref>

*'''Embroidery:''' Despite her dislike of it, Rozemyne is actually decently skilled in embroidery for someone her age.<ref name=""P4V4C14"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 4]]. Chapter 14: Left at Home</ref>

*'''Language:''' Rozemyne is very skilled in anything to do with language. She is able to easily read several ancient dialects that even other high-ranking nobles can barely decipher. She's also very good at taking complicated texts and abridging them into simpler language suited for a specific target audience. An example of this is her series of [[Inventions#Children's Bible

*'''Math:''' Thanks to her studies as Urano, Rozemyne is very good at math. Her method of doing written arithmetic makes her unique in Ehrenfest, where most people use an abacus. She can also calculate large numbers in her head well enough to put even some merchants to shame.

*'''Music:''' Due to Ferdinand's and [[Rosina]]'s extensive training, Rozemyne's skill in playing [[harspiel]] is way above her peers. She has a good ear for music and near-perfect pitch, allowing her to recreate many of the songs she heard as Urano.

*'''Negotiation:''' Thanks to her experience as an apprentice merchant, Rozemyne is a very skilled negotiator, capable of getting terms in her favor even when negotiating against people with higher authority. She's also good in motivating people to act in her bidding.

*'''Social Perception:''' Rozemyne is very perceptive in people's moods and true desires during social interactions, allowing her to win people over. However, she often acts on impulse without proper consideration of the surroundings and the consequences of her action, which frequently ends up causing troubles on an unprecedented scale.<ref name=""P4V7C1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 7]]. Chapter 1: Post-Return Discussion</ref>

*'''Tactics:''' While not being a combatant herself, Rozemyne is capable of coming up with unconventional battle tactics on the fly to win against overwhelming odds, as shown during the treasure-stealing ditter match with [[Dunkelfelger]].<ref>''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. column1: '''Schutzaria''' (シュツェーリア, ''Shutseeria''), the '''Goddess of Wind''' (風の女神, ''Kaze no Megami''), is one of the [[Gods and Subordinate Gods#Eternal Five
She presides over autumn, protection, and the harvest. Her [[Divine Instruments
column2: divine instrument]] is a [[Divine Instruments#Schutzaria's Shield
column4: divine color]] is yellow, symbolizing bountiful wheat.

column1: When the [[God of Darkness]] met the [[Goddess of Light]], they had four children. The oldest were [[Flutrane]], the Goddess of Water, and [[Leidenschaft]], the God of Fire. Schutzaria was the third, and [[Geduldh]], Goddess of Earth, was the youngest.

The God of Life [[Ewigeliebe]] fell in love with Schutzaria's younger sister, Geduldh. The God of Darkness gave the two permission to marry, hoping they would fill the world with new life. But Ewigeliebe's jealous love consumed him, and he froze Geduldh in ice, so her child could never be born.

The world fell into winter, and the Goddess of Light began to worry about her daughter. She found Geduldh trapped and melted the ice with her rays of sunlight, and Flutrane caused the water to flood away, bringing spring to the world, while Leidenschaft used his power to nurture the growth of summer. However, they could not defeat Ewigeliebe, because it would prevent all new life from being born into the world.

Schutzaria devoted all her strength to fighting off Ewigeliebe and protecting her sister, but she could not stop him forever. At the end of autumn, her powers waned, and Ewigeliebe once again trapped the Goddess of Earth in ice.
Each winter, the gods rest and recover their strength before fighting to free their sister once again.

Schutzaria is also called by the epitaph ""Protector of All,"" and is considered a goddess who specializes in defense and protection.<ref name=""P2V4C12"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 2 Volume 4]]. Chapter 12: The Black Charm</ref>

column2: Night of Schutzaria]] is the last full moon in autumn, when the God of Life is believed to finally defeat Schutzaria and take back Geduldh. On this night, autumn mana is at its strongest and the moon is purple.<ref name=""P3V2C15"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 3 Volume 2]]. Chapter 15: The Night of Schutzaria</ref>

Schutzaria is invoked in several [[Religious Ceremonies

*'''Shield of Wind:''' Praying to Schutzaria can conjure a shield of wind which protects those inside from physical and magical attacks. It also prevents anyone from entering if they mean harm to those already inside.<ref name=""P2V4C12""/>

Schutzaria has twelve subordinate goddesses, including Dregarnuhr the Goddess of Time, Jungereise the Goddess of Separation, [[Mestionora]] the Goddess of Wisdom, Ordoschnelli the Goddess of Couriers, and Steifebrise the Goddess of the Gale.
*Her name is most likely derived from the German word ""schutz"" which translates to ""protection"", and the Italian word ""aria"" which translates to ""air"".

'''Schwartz''' (シュバルツ, ''Shubarutsu'') and '''Weiss''' (ヴァイス, ''Waisu'') are a pair of [[Magic Tools#Automated Magic Tool Assistants
column2: magic tools]] modeled to look like [[Shumil]]. Their purpose is to assist the librarians of the [[Royal Academy/Library

column1: Schwartz and Weiss were made to appear like larger versions of [[Feybeasts#Shumil
column2: shumils]]. They have golden eyes, like most natural shumils do, and also have a golden [[feystone]] embedded in their foreheads. Schwartz has black fur, while Weiss has white fur.<ref name=""P4V1C15"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 1]]. Chapter 15: Registering at the Library</ref>

column1: While they are clothed, they look almost like real shumil, except for the feystones in their foreheads and their size. Once their clothes are removed, the places where their limbs join their torso look like those of a stuffed animal rather than the real feybeasts. They have extensive magic circles embroidered around their entire torsos, made from golden [[Magic Tools#Mana-dyed thread
column2: mana-dyed thread]].<ref name=""P4V2C7"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 2]]. Chapter 7: Measuring Schartz and Weiss</ref>

column1: They wear clothes provided to them by their master until a new master takes over and provides them with a new set. During their debut, they were still wearing dresses made by the master prior to [[Rozemyne]], which are one-piece dresses mostly in the opposite color of their furs with highlights in their fur colors and fitted with many expensive feystones.

After changing into new clothes prepared by Ehrenfest, Schwartz is dressed as a male while Weiss is dressed as a female. Schwartz wears a white short sleeve shirt with a black vest lined with magic circles, completed with a pair black slacks and a bowtie made from dyed cloth. On the other hand, Weiss wears a black maid dress with a white apron lined with magic circles, completed with a dyed scarf. Since all functional magic circles are embroidered on the vest and apron, the clothes underneath are interchangeable. Both of them also wear the ""Library Committee"" armband made by [[Tuuli]] at Rozemyne's request.

While the pair might appear like living beings, they are in fact magic tools. They have no true personalities to speak of and act in a robotic manner. They have the ability to speak, but despite made by a noble for the use of nobles, their dialogues are short and direct, likely as a limitation due to them being only automata, rather than actual living beings.

They are capable of lending out and retrieving books and carrel keys, as well as bringing returned books back to their respective place among the shelves.<ref name=""P4V1C16"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 1]]. Chapter 16: Schwartz and Weiss</ref>

When Rozemyne inquired how many books the Royal Library holds, Schwartz was able to give an estimate of the number of books and documents stored on the library's first floor.<ref name=""P4V2C2"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 2]]. Chapter 2: Onward to the Library</ref>

They appear to be capable of learning to at least some degree, since they came to understand the meaning of being measured for clothing apparently on their own due to going through the process so often.<ref name=""P4V2C7""/>
They are incapable of leaving the library on their own. Only their current master can take them outside, which requires direct physical contact, like holding hands for example.<ref name=""P4V2C7""/>

As long as both the magic tools and the person in question are within the library, Schwartz and Weiss can sense the presence and the exact location of all their masters.<ref name=""P4V6C19"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 6]]. Chapter 19: Going Home</ref>

After the central magic tool of the library was filled with mana from a ritual, that also contained considerable amounts of Rozemyne's mana, the girl once again becomes the master of Schwartz and Weiss, making it very likely that the shumils are in some way connected with this magic tool, even though the connection is clearly not strong enough to power the pair without magic being poured directly into their feystones as well.<ref name=""P5V2C11"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 2]]. Chapter 11: Preparing for Ditter</ref>

The pair of magic tools are instantly aware of any person who enters the library and can recognize whether this person is their master, a secondary master, someone authorized to enter or a trespasser, even when they have no line of sight to them. If they feel trespassers, they will hunt them down and kill them.<ref name=""P5V10C5"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 10]]. Chapter 5: Rescuing Solange</ref>

Apart from the enchantments that allow them to act almost like sentient beings, the pair has also been fitted with sophisticated protection mechanisms to prevent theft and damage. Only their current master and those explicitly authorized by them are able to freely touch them. To give permission, their current master merely needs to say so out loud within ear-shot of Schwartz and Weiss.

Once someone is given permission to touch them, that person will be exempt from any of the wards and is thus able to steal or damage them at will. Thus a master is well advised to only give this permission to people they trust deeply.<ref name=""P4V2C5"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 2]]. Chapter 5: My First Tea Party at the Royal Acadaemy</ref>

When someone unauthorized touches them, they will immediately feel a tingling sensation that grows in intensity by the moment and quickly reaches painful levels, eventually becoming too strong for anyone to bear. There have also been reports of people being repelled before even making skin-contact with the magic tools or even being ""blown away"" by mana, making it likely that the defensive spells contain a component that reacts to the intentions of the offender, mildly deterring those that act out of good intentions or mere curiosity, while warding off those with ill intentions with a level of violence proportional to the malice sensed.<ref name=""P4V2C7"" />

They are also fitted with enchantments specifically designed to ward off outright attacks, capable of absorbing the energy of incoming magical attacks and reflecting it back at the attacker. It is unclear how exactly this mechanism works, but when the defensive spell is active, both the eyes and the feystones set into the buttons of their clothing light up.<ref name=""P4V2C8"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 2]]. Chapter 8: The Battle for Schwartz and Weiss</ref>

Schwartz and Weiss are so old that the exact details of their origin is shrouded in mystery. The legend holds that they were created by a past princess a long time ago. The knowledge of how to create such sophisticated magic tools able to walk, talk, and work like them has either been kept private by their creator until their death, or has since been lost to time.<ref name=""P4V1C15""/>

At one point in [[Solange]]'s youth, the most recent master of the pair gave them outfits made purely for cuteness without considering how they might interfere with work. Their large hats kept falling off and their billowing sleeves made them knock over the stacks of gold paid as deposit. Despite these hindrances, the two magic tools attempted to continue their work unperturbed, neither trying to take off the cumbersome accessories, nor complaining even a single time. This forced the librarians to assign a person to keep an eye on them all the time, and their outfits were replaced with more practical ones within a couple of days. Since then it has become the norm to keep make their sleeves only reach their elbows.<ref name=""P4V2C5"" />

Following the civil war and the resulting purge among the [[nobility]], the three archnoble librarians that served as the previous masters for Schwarz and Weiss were sentenced to execution for being affiliated with the defeated princes. Knowing their days were numbered, they poured as much mana as they could into the two shumils to the point of putting their lives on the line, in a final act of dedication. Despite the enormous amount of mana their final act provided, it was only enough to keep the two magic tools running for one year.<ref name=""P4V2C10"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 2]]. Chapter 10: The Prince's Summons</ref>

The library was then left with only the mednoble [[Solange]] as the sole librarian. Due to their sophistication, Schwartz and Weiss unfortunately consume a lot of mana to operate. Even if Solange had been able to dedicate her entire mana to keeping them active, it is doubtful that it would have been enough. However, as the sole overseer of the library, Solange had to keep many vital magic tools active, and the two shumils eventually ceased to function. Despite this, Solange kept pouring as much mana as she could spare into the two to make sure the wards could keep them safe from theft or meddling.<ref name=""P4V2Pr"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 2]]. Prologue</ref>

Due to the pair being dormant for longer than any student will need from enrolling to graduation, hardly any current students knew about Schwartz and Weiss being animated magic tools and those who saw them in the shelf mostly assumed they were inanimate dolls belonging to Professor Solange, prior to them being reawakened by Rozemyne.

It is tradition for a new master to provide Schwartz and Weiss with a new set of clothes, to mark the passing of the torch.<ref name=""P4V1C15"" /> The normal way of passing ownership of the magic tools is for the current master to give permission to touch them to a successor and allow them to register their mana like with any other magic tool. In this way, it is also possible to have multiple mana providers at the same time, to share the burden of mana around.<ref name=""P4V2C10"" />

The two magic tools can only have one primary master at a time, whom they will call ""milady"" regardless of their gender. In addition to the primary master, they can also have multiple secondary masters at the same time. While the magic tools will follow the commands of all their current masters, they will prioritize those of their primary master.

Ehrenfest]] accidentally turned a prayer to [[Mestionora]] into a true blessing, which ended up recharging the two magic tools, who recognize her as their new master.

[[Part 4 Volume 6]]. Chapter 14: Changing Schwartz and Weiss</ref>

Due to their shared love in books and Hannelore's admiration for the library magic tools, Rozemyne offers to make her a secondary master of Schwartz and Weiss early in their second year at the Royal Academy. At a tea party in the library, Rozemyne makes good on her promise and registers Hannelore to became a secondary master, a few days after Prince Hildebrand has been registered<.ref name=""P4V6C18"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. column1: Shuu lived in the house next door to [[Urano Motosu

column1: One day, both families went on a trip. When they check into their hotel, both mothers were tired and wanted to take a nap. However, Shuu wanted an adventure, so his mother gaves him a map and marked the path to the planetarium with a red pen, telling him to explore and find it. Urano went with him, only to become an obstacle in his way because she was only interested in bookstores. He then came up with the idea to leave her at the library while he went alone to the planetarium. On his way back from the planetarium, he noticed that the library where Urano was had the lights off and its interior was pitch black, so he thought that she returned to the hotel. However, she wasn't there, which caused Shuu and her mother to panic and thoroughly search the nearby bookstore for her. After having no success, they call city hall to check if she was in the library, and even call the police, but are still unable to find her. They are worried that she has been kidnapped, but convince the police to request the library be opened so they can check for her there. Urano is found sitting on the windowsill in the darkened library, still unworriedly reading books. 10 years later, Shuu goes to explore the same planetarium again leaving Urano in the same library. This time, he makes sure to return to the library before closing time to avoid his past mistake. They reminisce, and Shuu thinks about how since then, Urano has spoken up if the library has started to close around her, rather than reading on, uncaring. This makes him think she has grown up some, but he then notices she is continuing to read instead of cleaning up, and quickly changes his mind. Reflecting on how little she has grown, he hopes she one day gets stuck in a world without books and suffers.<ref name=""P1V1S2"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 1 Volume 1]]. column1: He has some freckles on his face over his nose.
As lower city boy, his manners and behavior are rough. He is easily discouraged but can be determined when he sets his mind on something.

After his baptism, he begins his apprenticeship at the Dostal carpentry workshop.<ref name=""P3V3S2"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 3]]. The High Bishop's Exclusive Business</ref>

Sieg works at the carpentry workshop that is contracted with the [[Gilberta Company]]. He is an apprentice in his second year when [[Lutz]] and [[Myne]] are six years old. With only one year left to prove himself, he desperately tries to accomplish a task that shows his value. Due to his skilled senior apprentice Ast, he feels that he lacks the skills to complete such a task. During the last winter, the foreman found an elaborate-patterned basket woven by an amateur. Now it is Sieg's task to imitate the pattern.

While he struggles to stay positive in the beginning, he finds his motivation to make a better basket, than the one modeled after. On one day when he weaves the basket in the back of the workshop while Ast is working on his project, a rich looking customer comes to the workshop. He has two children with him in raggedy clothes like the ones Sieg wears. The foreman leaves the store with them, without Sieg being able to see the customers. As he is still an inexperienced apprentice, he is not allowed to deal with customers, other than some regulars. In fact, those people were [[Mark]], [[Lutz]] and [[Myne]], who ordered the screen for the suketa.

Sieg has finished his basket and proudly shows it to the foreman. He takes it with little reaction and sends him on an errand, which leaves Sieg disappointed. His errand would lead him to the thread store's owner which he knows by now from running errands. They chitchatted a bit when Sieg arrives to get the spin thread. Sieg tells him about his fear about his contract. The thread store owner points out his impolite language and motivates him to keep on. With new found motivation, he walks back and decides to ask the foreman for a new task. He assigns Sieg to make the suketa screen order he recently received. The prepared material looks carved by an amateur.

Motivated he begins his work and eagerly adjusts the brought material with his foreman approving any step. After the foreman finishes his own work, he joins in with Sieg. Sieg is impressed by the foreman's skill, seeing worlds between them. His foreman gives him some hints and advises, while they work together. At the end, Sieg matched the foreman's rhythm, unlike at the beginning, when he needed more time to finish one part. While Sieg talks about his ambitions to become a real craftsman, the foreman complimented Sieg's basket and voiced his acknowledgement that Sieg is already a pretty good craftsman.<ref name=""M1V4"">[[Manga
column2: Ascendance of a Bookworm Manga]]. [[Manga Part 1 Volume 4
column3: Part 1 Volume 4]]. Sieg the Apprentice Craftsman</ref>

column2: Prince Waldifried]] at the hands of his older brother, the Aub Dunkelfelger at the time banned all interduchy marriage to avoid the potential problems such marriages could cause with the factional divide following the event. He only intended to keep the rule in place until a new zent was crowned, but due to the uncertainty of having a king without a [[Grutrissheit]], he kept it in place even after [[Trauerqual]] had been won the throne. By the time the rule was finally abolished again, his son and Sieglinde had already married, leading to the unusual situation of the current Aub's wife not coming from another duchy as is common among greater duchies.<ref name=""P5V3S2"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. Shortly after the end of Hannelore's fourth year at the Royal Academy, Dunkelfelger is informed by Ehrenfest, that Ahrensbach has commited treason and is trying to kill Ferdinand. As such they seek an alliance with Dunkelfelger, which Werdekraf eagerly agrees to, in no small part because Rozemyne painted her planned assault as ""true ditter."" Despite their eagerness to join the fray, Sieglinde is able to reign her husband and son's passions in. She and the Aub will remain at the ready, to respond at a moment's notice, should the Zent call for their aid in this crisis, while Lestilaut's duty as the Aub's successor will be to guard the duchy's foundation. Of the archduke's family, only Hannelore is permitted to join the assault, so she can cleanse the shame of having thrown her previous ditter match.
When Rozemyne arrives via teleportation into their country gate, Sieglinde is greatly relieved to be shown a pendant emblazoned with the royal family's crest Rozemyne received from [[Sigiswald

column1: '''Siegrecht''' is the child of [[Lamprecht]] and [[Aurelia]]. He is [[Rozemyne]]'s nephew.<ref name=""P5V12C11""/>
Siegrecht inherited his mother's golden hair, but most of his other features, in particular the eyes, look like his father's. He is quite tall for someone his age.<ref name=""P5V12C11""/>

In Rozemyne's opinion, Siegrecht is far less shy than most children his age and his parents are a little worried about how impulsive he is. Rozemyne believes these traits were inherited from Bonifatius.<ref name=""P5V12C11""/>

Despite being expected in autumn, Siegrecht's birth only happens in winter. Due to the delicate political and familial circumstances of his mother, Siegrecht's existence is kept as a tightly guarded secret, known only to his direct family and a few trusted servants. At Aurelia's insistence, Rozemyne is also told about the birth, but any attempts by the new aunt to see her nephew fail due to tight schedules and the need for secrecy.

Only more than a year after Siegrecht's birth is Rozemyne finally able to meet him, shortly before her move to [[Alexandria]]. Unlike any other babies Rozemyne met in this new life, Siegrecht doesn't cry from being close to her and even charged straight toward her of his own accord, making ""Auntie Rozemyne"" quite happy.<ref name=""P5V12C11""/>

He asked for [[Eglantine]]'s hand in marriage, but unlike his younger brother, he did so solely for political reasons, since the one to marry her is almost assured to become the next king.<ref name=""P4V2S1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 2]]. Honest Courting</ref>

When his younger brother Anastasius offers to relinquish his claim on the crown, if Sigiswald retracts his marriage proposal to Eglantine, Sigiswald accepts, securing his own guaranteed succession to the throne in exchange for enabling his brother and his lover to marry. After some hard work on his part, Anastasius also manages to convince King Trauerqual, [[Aub Klassenberg]], and Eglantine's biological grandfather and adoptive father, the [[Previous Aub Klassenberg]] to agree to this arrangement, making it official.
With Eglantine now removed from his consideration for a first wife, Sigiswald gets engaged with [[Adolphine]] of [[Drewanchel]].

So that his new fiancée could wear the new kind of Ehrenfest hairpin at her graduation, despite Drewanchel not yet trading with Ehrenfest, Sigiswald personally ordered such an ornament for Adolphine directly from Rozemyne.<ref name=""P4V7C3"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 7]]. Chapter 3: Sylvester's Order</ref>

Sigiswald and Rozemyne meet for the first time face to face in her third year at the [[Royal Academy]]. The three princes invite her to Anastasius' villa to talk about an archive that only royalty and archduke candidates can enter, which she relayed to them upon learning of its existence from Ferdinand. Ultimately Rozemyne is unable to give any more answers than beyond what she sent in the letter already, and so Sigiswald decides to gather the three holders of the keys in the library and check the archive themselves.
Once the three holders of the keys - Rozemyne, the [[Dunkelfelger]] archduke candidate [[Hannelore]], and the archnoble librarian [[Hortensia]] - open the [[Royal Academy/Library#Underground Archive
column2: archive]], Rozemyne reluctantly refuses to go inside, since her guardians forbade her to. Hildebrand is also unable to enter the archive, since its protective barrier won't admit him due to having a too small mana capacity, and as Hortensia is not a royal or an archduke candidate, she can't enter either, so Sigiswald and Anastasius begin their search with only Hannelore to help them.

column1: Inside they find many ivory tablets inscribed with accounts in ancient dialects, which neither of the princes is able to read, and while Hannelore is able to understand them, she takes a lot of time to translate them, so the princes go back to the waiting area. Sigiswald does not want to make Rozemyne break her promise with her guardians, but due to the great need still reluctantly asks her for help, making the girl waver. Seeing this, Anastasius orders her to help them. Sigiswald is quit to chastise his younger brother to not abuse his powers, but Anastasius explains that this is the best way. Rozemyne clearly wants to go inside the archive too, but is held back by her promise. A royal decree would supersede any authority her guardians have and thus her entering would not break her promise, since she has no choice but to obey, giving both the princes and Rozemyne herself what they want. Seeing how gleeful Rozemyne is about the prospect of entering the place, Sigiswald relents.

Inside, the princes keep reading through the few bound books, since they are written in modern vernacular, while Hannelore and Rozemyne check over the ivory tablets. Since Rozemyne is far more used to reading ancient dialects, her joining speeds the work up considerably. With her help, they are able to find several useful pieces of information, including the mana compression method of a previous sovereign, information on how that person prepared for the ritual to receive divine protections, and details on a no longer used inauguration ceremony of old.

In a short break, the princes also question Rozemyne about her divine protections and extract the information that she was able to obtain the protection of a total of 43 gods. She also explains that her brother [[Wilfried]], who obtained 12 divine protections - only uses about 70 % as much mana and she only 40 % compared to before the ritual and that it is very likely that even adults can re-do the ceremony for the chance to obtain additional protections and how they can incorporate prayers into their everyday life to increase the chances for getting them.

When the library closes, they have trouble prying Rozemyne away from the books and documents, resulting in Anastasius literally carrying her out of the archive by the scruff of her neck. To make sure she can't go into this place, where her retainers can not enter on their own, Sigiswald forbids Rozemyne from going into the archive without a member of the royal family present<ref name=""P5V2C2"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 2]]. Chapter 1: The Royal Family and the Library</ref>

A short time before the date of his Starbinding with Adolphine, Nahelache gives birth to Sigiswald's first child. To avoid negatively influencing the child with another woman's mana, Sigiswald informs his fiancée that they will delay marital intimacy, but due to the dire mana situation of the royal family, is unwilling to delay the marriage itself until next year, as common decency and tradition would usually demand, much to Adolphine's open dismay.<ref name=""P5V5S1""/>
To quell the voices that call for Anastasius or Detlinde to become the next Zent, the royal family pressures Lady Rozemyne into performing the [[Starbind_Ceremony#Royalty_and_Archduke_Candidates
column2: Starbind Ceremony]] at his and Adolphne's wedding, to provide them with a true blessing. The Sovereign Temple uses this opportunity to promote themselves, by providing Rozemyne with instructions on how to perform the ancient form of the ceremony with the [[Divine Instruments]] of the [[God of Darkness]] and [[Goddess of Light]], resulting in a rather spectacular ceremony, stunning all the onlookers. In addition to the blessings for the couples, during the ceremony, magic circles appear similar in appearance to the one that was seen in Detlinde's Dedication Whirl, on the stage beneath Sigiswald and Adolphine and rise into the air briefly, before dissipating again.

column1: This is seen as a great boon to the royal family, since it proofs that Sigiswald is at the very least equally qualified in the eyes of the god as Detlinde.<ref name=""P5V5C4"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 5]]. Chapter 4: Work in the Underground Archive</ref>

In the following few days, Rozemyne ends up inadvertedly becoming a Zent candidate, which Anastasius notices and tells the rest of the royal family. This makes them determined to win her for the Sovereignty, so she can help them obtain the Grutrissheit. For this end, Sigiswald has a private conversation with Rozemyne in the underground archive, between just the two without any retainers present and even goes so far as to disperse of all noble euphemisms, speaking completely candidly and allowing Rozemyne to do the same.<ref name=""P5V5C11"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 5]]. Chapter 11: The Merchant Saint</ref>

Due to some of the country's magic tools starting to break from the lack of mana, with one already having been destroyed, the royal family feels they can not wait for Rozemyne to come of age and thus pressure Ehrenfest to allow them to adopt her as soon as possible, and have her marry Sigiswald as his third wife at a later date. Sigiswald negotiates some preliminary conditions with Rozemyne and hears her suggestions for the rest of the negotiation, but ultimately the final decisions will be made between Zent Trauerqual and Aub Ehrenfest. Rozemyne's relentless mechant insticts quickly leave the prince exhaused and out of his depth.<ref name=""P5V5C12"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 5]]. Chapter 12: Conditions for Being Adopted</ref>

After receiving the last testament of Ferdinand, Rozemyne decided to invade Ahrensbach with the help of Dunkelger knights to rescue him. However, she still needed Royal permission as it's an interduchy matter and [[Lanzenave]] is also helping Ahrensbach. While she was preparing for the invasion, Sylvester went to the Royal Academy to explain the situation and obtain permission for Rozemyne to invade Ahrensbach. There, Sigiswald gave a necklace style pendant to Sylvester. The pendant was was made out of a six-element feystone and engraved with the crest of the Royal Family and a protective magic circle<ref name="":0"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 8]]. Chapter 3: Teleporting</ref>. Rozemyne noted that the protective circle didn't seem particularly strong<ref name="":0"" />. When Rozemyne showed it to the Dunkelfelger Archducal Family as proof of the Royal Family's permission, [[Sieglinde
column2: Lady Sieglinde]] agreed to send the volunteers to Ahrensbach<ref>''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 8]]. Chapter 4: To Battle</ref>.

column1: After Ferdinand is rescued and Rozemye was discussing ways to take over the Lanzenave ships, Hannelore pointed out that the chain of the necklace seemed to be degrading<ref>''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 8]]. Chapter 10: The New Aub</ref>. Rozemyne touched the chain and noticed that it has now become unusually rough compared to very smooth when she was gifted it first. Rozemyne could even see gold dust on her fingers after touching the chain. When Rozemyne removed the necklace, she observed that only the part that were in contact with her skin was degraded. When Rozemyne wondering if she was given a low quality chain, Hannelore explained that the chains of courtship tools are made of the creators mana and it will experience great strain if it's worn by someone who possesses more mana than the creator. Since putting on the necklace, Rozemyne supplyied two country gates, teleported several times and dyed the foundation of a greater duchy. She used too much mana that far exceeded the capacity of the tool and perhaps the capacity of the creator too. Additionally, Hannelore's comment made it clear to Rozemyne that the pendant is not only a permission but a courtship magic tool that also leaks mana. This indicates that Prince Sigiswald was romantically interested in Rozemyne, even though Rozemyne herself views the arrangement as purely political. If the pendant is damaged further, Rozemyne might not be able to use it as proof of her Royal permission, so as per Hartmut's suggestion, she wraps the pendant with a piece of cloth and put it in the pouch in her hip.

Following the abdication of his father and the crowing of the new Zent Eglantine, Sigiswald becomes the Aub of a new duchy, made out of the parts of duchies that were dissolved after the civil war, but could not be removed entirely under Trauerqual's rule, due to the lack of a [[Grutrissheit]]. His new duchy has the name of [[Korinthsdaum]].

Sigiswald has a hard time adjusting to his diminished status, still expecting people to wait for him at the inauguration ceremony, until Lady Rozemyne points out to him and his retainers, that the door will open on Zent Eglantine's command, whether he's ready or not and dawdling will only result in him making a fool of himself in front of the entirety of Yurgenschmidt's rulers.<ref name=""P5V12C18""/>

*'''Divine Protection:''' Sigiswald has the divine protection of all primary gods he has an affinity for, but none by subordinate gods.<ref name=""P5V2C1""/> It is currently unknown how many and which ones they are.

column1: Solange diligently kept pouring mana into the dormant [[Schwartz and Weiss]]. Because she did not have both the attributes of Darkness and Light, she was not able to activate them. However, her mana sustained the wards on the the two magic tools that prevented theft and meddling.

column1: Stenluke outwardly looks like a regular sword with a large [[feystone]] embedded into its pommel. It is the size of a dagger when sheathed, and grows to its full size when drawn.

column2: Ferdinand’s]]. It is formal, intelligent, and disciplined. While it is strict with Angelica, it is very respectful to Rozemyne, calling her “master of my master.” Generally, it does not talk to anyone other than Angelica or Rozemyne.

column1: Stenluke was initially a regular [[manablade]]. To compensate for the elemental affinities she lacked, [[Angelica]] fed it [[Feystone
column2: feystones]] and materials of different attributes. She also gave it mana whenever she could to grow the blade.

column1: As a reward for studying hard and successfully passing her courses at the [[Royal Academy]], Rozemyne promises to donate mana to Angelica's manablade. Her mana is only expected to grow the blade and potentially instill it with some of her elemental affinities.

While pouring mana into the blade, Rozemyne reflects that what Angelica really needs is more brainpower and more motivation to study, and she remembers her own experience with Ferdinand’s strict teaching style. While Rozemyne is pouring mana into the blade, she is interrupted by [[Eckhart]] who promptly calls [[Ferdinand]]. Worrying that Rozemyne's lack of education on mana might have caused issues to the blade, he pours a small amount of mana into it to check it, but can't initially find anything wrong with it, much to Angelica and Rozemyne's relief. Following this Ferdinand goes to lecture the gathered people at length.

When he inquires whether they all now understood the dangers, Angelica's reply is less than convincing, causing Ferdinand to shout at her. To everyone surprise though, the manablade itself also shouts. It is then the blade that explains that Lady Rozemyne's - whom it called ""master of my master"" - wish has caused it to become sentient and because she was thinking of Ferdinand at the time, combined with Ferdinand pouring some of his mana into the blade influenced its voice and attitude. This resulted in the blade being nearly identical to Ferdinand in both voice and mannerism.<ref name=""P3V4C6""/>
Instead of being weirded out by this, Angelica is very happy about his happenstance and later christens the blade Stenluke.

Stenluke becomes a useful tool for Angelica, since it can remember important information for her, scold her when she slacks off on her studying, and caution her when she acts recklessly. However, it can only listen and talk while Angelica's mana is coursing through it, meaning that she can’t entrust the blade to someone else so they can teach it in her place. As Stenluke points out, her mana inside of it just isn't enough to last through the necessary lessons.<ref name=""P3C4C7"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 3 Volume 4]]. Chapter 7: Let's Print More Stuff</ref>

When Angelica begins to rely too heavily on Stenluke to remember information for her, Rozemyne forbids her from using it in classes at the [[Royal Academy]]. Stenluke agrees with the decision and abstains from providing help.<ref name=""P4V1C8"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 4 Volume 1]]. Chapter 8: The Better Grades Committee</ref> However, thanks to [[Cornelius
column2: Cornelius’s]] dedicated tutoring, Angelica just barely manages to graduate on her own.<ref name=""P4V2C15"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 4 Volume 2]]. Chapter 15: An Order to Return to Ehrenfest</ref>

column1: '''Sylvester''' (ジルヴェスター, ''Jiruvesutaa'') is the seventh [[Aub Ehrenfest]] and the current archduke of [[Ehrenfest]].

He is married to [[Florencia]], the First Wife, and they are the parents of [[Wilfried]], [[Charlotte]], [[Melchior]], [[Henriette]], and adoptive parents of [[Rozemyne]]. He is also the half-brother of [[Ferdinand]] and engaged to [[Brunhilde]], the future second wife.

Sylvester has long, Indigo blue hair, which he wears tied back with a silver cord. His eyes are Green (teal-tinted), and he has strong eyebrows. He is slightly shorter than [[Ferdinand]], but has a more muscular build. [[Rozemyne]] thinks he looks around the same age as [[Benno]] or Ferdinand.<ref name=""P2V3C13"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 2 Volume 3]]. Chapter 13: Preparing for the Spring Prayer</ref>

In contrast to his younger brother, Sylvester often acts impulsively, leading most people to think that he is younger than he actually is. He is a relentless teaser, but he can get serious in a heartbeat when needed. He is described to have a good heart deep down, although he acts like a spoiled child.

As an archduke, Sylvester is decently competent with his duty, although he has the tendency to run away from paperwork. He is open-minded and quick to accept new ideas. In fact, he is fascinated with new things and experiences, so much that he would go out of his way to try them out. Unlike typical nobles, he doesn't care much about formalities, such that he would even allow orphans to abbreviate his name.
Sylvester deeply cares about his family, but this also resulted in him often being too forgiving towards them, which led to dire consequences during multiple instances.
Sylvester is the son of [[Adelbert]], the sixth Aub Ehrenfest and [[Veronica]].

Before Sylvester's birth, his oldest sister [[Georgine]] was well on the way to become Archduchess. When Sylvester was born and grew up far enough, he and his siblings were thrown into a fierce competition for succession. Ultimately, Sylvester came out on top and was chosen to become the seventh [[Aub Ehrenfest]], in no small part due to his bigger mana capacity and gender, which caused no end of problems between him and Georgine, who had been practically raised to be the archduchess, but had the title ""snatched away"" by her younger brother, as she sees it.

As a result, she relentlessly tormented Sylvester at any opportunity, to the point where their parents started to fear for Sylvester's safety to a degree that they married Georgine off to [[Ahrensbach]], even though it meant she would only be the third wife, a position hardly worthy of an archduke candidate. This resentment between the two siblings continues to this very day.

Sylvester first met [[Florencia]] when [[Constanze]] was acquainted with Florencia's elder brother (now [[Aub Frenbeltag]]). Constanze brought Sylvester to tea parties with Frenbeltag.<ref name=""FB6QA""/>

Sylvester had developed mana-sensing in his second year of the [[Royal Academy]] and fallen madly in love with Lady Florencia of Frenbeltag, two years older then him.<ref name=""P5V8E"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 8]]. Epilogue</ref>

His second oldest sister [[Constanze]] married into the closely allied duchy of [[Frenbeltag]] and became the Archduke's first wife, while Sylvester himself married the younger sister of Aub Frenbeltag, [[Florencia]].

Due to both Sylvester and his wife being the younger siblings of their Frenbeltag counterparts, they have a weak position in negotiations with their siblings and often end up giving more than they are entirely comfortable with.

After the marriage, Sylvester's mother insisted he take a second wife, but he stoutly refused, choosing to devote himself completely to the woman he loved. This was the first act of open defiance he showed to his mother, and even led to some nobles temporarily believing that Veronica's influence had finally started its decline, though only for a short time.<ref name=""FB2S5"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Fanbook 2]]. Story 5: A Tea Party with My Older Sister</ref>

[[Ferdinand]] and Sylvester first met after Ferdinand's baptism. They have the same father but different mothers. Sylvester is six years older than Ferdinand and looked out for and cared for his younger half-brother.

Due to Ferdinand's harassment by Sylvester's mother, Sylvester told Ferdinand to join the temple to escape Veronica's harassment, which would remove him from the family's succession and keep him away from noble politics. When Ferdinand complained to Sylvester about being bored, he sent his younger brother some of his own work, figuring that since Ferdinand wanted something to do and since he himself wanted less to work, it would be a win-win.
Even after Ferdinand became the [[Temple Hierarchy#High Priest
column2: High Priest]], Sylvester kept sending him work. Since his brother never complained, Sylvester never considered the possibility that between the work of his new position and the work sent over by his brother, the freshly minted High Priest would be overworked to the point of requiring recovery potions to keep up with the load.

Theodore's family stems from Kirnberger. His father is one of the knights protecting the gate to the neighboring country.<ref name=""FB2S7"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Fanbook 2]] Story 7: Starting Life as a Retainer</ref>

His father appears to be regarded quite highly by Giebe Kirnberger. When the Giebe's son [[Alexis]] was chosen to be a guard knight for a member of the archducal family, he picked Theodore's father to give the boy extra lessons and training to be up to the task.<ref name=""P5V4E"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 4]]. Epilogue</ref>

After their return from the [[Royal Academy]] following [[Rozemyne]]'s second term, [[Brunhilde]] introduces her lady to her younger sister [[Bertilde]], who is planned to become Rozemyne's retainer upon entering the Royal Academy. Not fully understanding the implications of her actions, Judithe also introduces her younger brother to Lady Rozemyne. Both [[Cornelius]] and [[Angelica]] approve of the boy, with Angelica remarking that she had seen him train before and that he is surprisingly strong for his age.

Hearing this Rozemyne agrees to consider him as a retainer once he starts attending the Royal Academy, which puts Theodore in an awkward situation. He wishes to follow his father's footsteps and serve Giebe Kirnberger. Thankfully Rozemyne neither takes offense at his rejection nor uses her higher status to force him to serve her anyway despite many other high-ranking nobles likely having done so in her position. Instead she commends his commitment and encourages him to follow his dream. As a potential compromise, she suggests that he serve her only part-time. With her having sufficient adult guard knights, she only requires more knights at the Royal Academy and thus wishes to have Theodore serve her only there, without any obligations past his graduation. For her this would address the lack of guards at the Royal Academy, and Theodore would not only get more chances to practice being a guard knight, but also receive the better training usually reserved for guards of the archduke's family. Theodore is interested, but chooses to take some time for considerations before agreeing or rejecting this offer.
A little later, Giebe Kirnberger negotiates with [[Sylvester
column2: Aub Ehrenfest]], and this arrangement is put into place in exchange for Kirnberger being the next province visited by the Gutenbergs.<ref name=""P4V8C2""/>

column1: As was decided the year prior, upon his entry into the Royal Academy, Theodore entered Lady Rozemyne's service as a temporary guard knight until the time when he graduates from the Royal Academy, at which point he will be allowed to retire to serve Giebe Kirnberger. He is very surprised to learn how well regarded his sister actually is among her fellow retainers and that her seeming slow pace of learning was due to how thorough she is and how this paid off with grades considerably better than one would expect from someone of her station. He appears fine with calling [[Leonore]] without an honorific as is common among Rozemyne's retainers, but calling his sister by her name, rather than just 'sister' seems to come hard to him. A sentiment shared by Judithe as well.<ref name=""P5V1C1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 9]]. Chapter 1: The Children of the Former Veronica Faction</ref>

The next day, the classes start. After returning from the day's exams, Theodore proudly proclaims that all Ehrenfest first-years managed to pass their tests on the first try. A moment later, Lady Rozemyne receives an ordonnanz from [[Solange
column2: Professor Solange]], informing her that a new archnoble librarian has been appointed to the Royal Academy and asks her visit the library at her earliest convenience so that mastership of [[Schwartz and Weiss]] can be handed over. Theodore is excited for his first visit to the library for a moment before learning that on account of not having been registered yet he isn't able to accompany his lady and her other retainers. As the only one of Rozemyne's current guard knights unable to accompany her, he feels left out and pouts. Judithe scolds him that it is unbecoming of a guard knight to an archduke candidate to pout like that, prompting her fellow retainers to bust out laughing and pointing out that she used to pout in exactly the same way when she was in similar circumstances. Theodore and Judithe shout that they are not the same in complete synchronicity, leading the others to laugh even harder.<ref name=""P5V1C4"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 1]]. Chapter 4: The New Librarian</ref>

'''Tollkuehnheit''' was the first King of [[Lanzenave]]. He was a [[Royal Family]] member of the ancient past, being the son of [[Aeussewahl]] and the brother of [[Heileind]].<ref name=""P5V6S1""/>

Upon his brother becoming the next Zent, he's uses his [[Grutrissheit]] to find the new land of [[Lanzenave]] and became its first King. He makes a deal with his brother [[Heileind]] to send one high mana individual back to [[Lanzenave]]. Therefore, Tollkuehnheit is the reason the [[Royal Academy#Adalgisa Villa
The country of Lanzenave came into being about 400 years ago. Shortly before it's founding, Yurgenschmidt was ruled by [[Aeussewahl
column2: Zent Aeussewahl]] and three of his sons managed to obtain a Grutrissheit. Ultimately [[Aeussewahl]] chose his son [[Heileind]] as his successor. Unable to accept being passed over, his brother [[Tollkuehnheit]] took his magic tool and went looking for a new land to settle. Accompanied by his wife and retainers, he sailed through the southern country gate and eventually happened across an inhabited land, with a comparatively poor population, unable to use any magic. While the area didn't appear to be rich in any valuable natural resources, it was able to sustain the local population, which was good enough for [[Tollkuehnheit]]. He used his [[Grutrissheit]] to create a duchy foundation and raise an entire ivory city before the eyes of the stunned locals. Having never seen any magic of this scale, or potentially any magic at all, this awed the locals so much that many of them took to worshipping Tollkuehnheit as an emissary from the land of gods, making it easy for him to crown himself the king of this new land and crism it [[Lanzenave]].

column1: Due to the mana disparity of the newly arrived nobles and the indigenous people, interbreeding was essentially impossible. Furthermore, since his [[Grutrissheit]] was only a duplicate, which he created with his [[schtappe]], rather than a physical transcription, he couldn't hope to pass it down to any of his children and it would disappear along with him upon his death. To make matters even worse, without a schtappe, no one could fully maintain the city's foundation magic either, once he was gone, meaning that not just the Grutrissheit, but the entire city would be lost, if he couldn't find a solution.

He petitioned his brother, now the Zent of [[Yurgenschmidt]], to give one of his children a [[schtappe]], but due to it being impossible for people not registered as Yurgenschmidt nobles to receive one, the Zent had to decline. Instead the two monarchs hammered out an agreement to sent a princess of [[Lanzenave]] to Yurgenschmidt, where she would conceive children from the local nobility, who would then be raised as Yurgenschmidt nobles, including going to the [[Royal Academy]] and obtaining a schtappe. However, [[Heileind
column2: Zent Heileind]] was concerned that, if all the children were allowed to leave the country after their coming-of-age, their neighbor might become too powerful and threaten his own country one day, so he only agreed to send a single child - regardless of gender - each generation to Lanzenave. Due to practical reasons, primarily involving the effects of pregnancy, the first couple of children thus chosen, were all male, until it became tradition to always receive a male heir.<ref name=""P5V6S1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. column1: Shortly after the [[Lanzenave]] invasion was defeated, [[Eglantine]] is crowned the new Zent. Following his abdication, he becomes [[Blumenfeld#People and Leadership

Zent Trauerqual has silver hair with tinges of blue, closely resembling his youngest son, while his facial features are closer to his middle son Anastasius. When Rozemyne met him, he looked exhausted and sleep-deprived, as if he was constantly overworked and substituted lack of sleep with copious use of rejuvenation potions.<ref name=""P5V2C7""/>

Zent Trauerqual has a considerably higher tolerance for lacking etiquette in his conversation partners than his son Anastasius and the majority of his retainers, as was demonstrated by him allowing [[Rozemyne]] of [[Ehrenfest (Duchy)
column2: Ehrenfest]] to speak far more directly than usual in royal circles without rebuking her, even when his own son and his retainers spoke out against the perceived disrespect.<ref name=""P5V2C7""/>

column1: Born as the fifth prince, in his youth Trauerqual was raised to become a vassal to whichever of his brothers would eventually succeed the king, rather than participate in the competition for succession himself.<ref name=""P4V7C4"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 7]]. Chapter 4: Investigating the Bible</ref>
During the rule of his father, Trauerqual married his first wife [[Ralfrieda]] and taught the Archduke Candidate Course at the [[Royal Academy]]<ref name=""FB6QA""/>
The prince that was chosen as the successor was the second prince. By the time their father died the magic tool Grutrissheit passed down from parent to child since [[Albsenti
column2: Zent Albsenti]]'s times had already been passed to him. Shortly after their father's death, but before the coronation could take place the first prince visited his younger brother Waldifried's villa and slaughtered him and his entire family to usurp the crown, sparing only the retainers and servants.<ref name=""P5V1S2"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 1]]. Finding Purpose and the Guardians of Knowledge</ref> Not willing to let this injustice stand the third prince went to war against his older brother beginning the [[Civil War
column3: civil war]].<ref name=""RAS1C17"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Royal Academy Stories - First Year]]. Chapter 17: [[Solange]] - Closed-Stack Archives and the Old Diaries</ref>

column1: The third prince managed to defeat and kill his elder brother, but was soon after killed by an assassin sent by the first prince shortly before their final battle. With the two contenders for the throne gone, a new conflict broke out between the fourth and fifth princes, with most of the former first prince's allies siding with the fourth and the former faction of the third going over to the fifth prince.

In this second part of the civil war, Trauerqual's faction came out on top, in no small part thanks to the alliance with [[Klassenberg]]. Following his victory, Trauerqual was crowned to be the new Zent.

Despite his complete victory, his ascension to the throne was still not unopposed. Due to him failing to fulfill the qualification set down in the bible and thus failing to gain the god's divine mandate, many in the Sovereignty temple initially opposed his coronation, but ultimately relented due to there simply being no other suitable candidate to hold the position.

Due to the civil war, the transcription of the Grutrissheit owned by Trauerqual's father, which was supposed to be passed to the next king was lost, alongside the second prince's bible. Usually in such a case, it is the new Zent's duty to make a new transcription from the one made by the first king, but since its location is currently unknown, King Trauerqual has so far been unable to fulfill this duty.
Furthermore, with the candidates raised to potentially become king and the previous king all being dead, it is likely that many secrets passed down from the king orally have been lost.

This, alongside the bitterness over an unqualified royal becoming king, is what gave rise to the movement of the biblical fanaticism.<ref name=""P4V7C4"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 7]]. Chapter 4: Investigating the Bible</ref>

Following his victory and coronation, the new king imprisoned his older brother and initially only enacted small-scale punishments on his enemies, despite massive pressure from his allies for harsh and wide-reaching measures against their enemies.

Emboldened by the belief that Trauerqual would be unwilling to commit to mass-executions, the duchy of [[Werkestock]] conspired to have the new king assassinated and install the fourth prince on the throne. At some point, a group of rebels also kidnapped Trauerqual's daughter in an attempt to blackmail him into abdicating in favor of his brother.

Faced with these actions, the king eventually gave in to the pressure of his allies and thus a far-reaching and brutal purge was enacted throughout the entire country, leading to the dissolution of several of the defeated duchies and the mass execution of a large number of nobles. Among those sentenced to death was anyone who had supported the first or fourth princes or had a claim to the throne, as well as others seen as disloyal. Without a Grutrissheit, the duchy borders could not be redrawn, so the affected territory was only put under the management of the Sovereignty or neighboring duchies loyal to the king.<ref name=""RAS1C17"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Royal Academy Stories - First Year]]. Chapter 17: [[Solange]] - Closed-Stack Archives and the Old Diaries</ref>

This purge was not limited to just members of the losing faction, but also affected the winning duchies and those that remained neutral throughout the conflict.<ref name=""P4V2C13"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 2]]. Chapter 13: A Tea Party with Eglantine</ref>

This purge even claimed the lives of people who were not implicated in any act of disloyalty, but just had the misfortune to have a family relation with one of the nobles labelled as a traitor, even if they were part of a duchy that had supported the king during the war. One such example was the second wife of [[Gieselfried
column2: Aub Ahrensbach]], who was executed due to being the little sister of Aub Werkestock, despite being innocent herself and her husband fighting alongside the prince in the civil war.<ref name=""P4V4E"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 4]]. Epilogue</ref>

column1: To make matters worse for many duchies, the Sovereignty tried to fill the gaps in their noble ranks by calling nobles from the duchies to the Sovereignty, leaving many duchies drained of even more manpower and mana than the purge itself already did. This can be felt particularly strongly in the various temples, since they lost personnel three times: Once from the purge, once from the sovereign temple calling the best and mana-richest priests to the heart of the country, and finally from the duchies recalling those they sent to the temple to noble society.

Originally, the king planned to have Anastasius fill the role of overseer at the [[Royal Academy]] in the terms following his graduation, but due to being given lordship over Sovereignty lands, Anastasius became very occupied with filling the land and its magic tools with mana. After much debate, the king decides that this was too important to interrupt and thus reluctantly chose his third son, the just recently baptized [[Hildebrand]], to oversee the next term at the Royal Academy. While it is unprecedented for a child to take up official duties before their debut at Archduke's Conference following their baptism, the current situation left the king with no other viable choice than to rely on the young boy.<ref name=""P4V5E"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 5]]. Epilogue</ref>

At the [[Interduchy Tournament]] following [[Rozemyne]]'s second Royal Academy term, a group of rebels led by former Werkestock nobles launched an attack on the royal family utilizing several [[Feybeasts#Ternisbefallen
column2: ternisbefallen]]. They unleashed the mana-absorbing feybeasts in the arena with the students and in the ensuing chaos launched themselves at the king and his family. The attackers were so fanatical that some of them even launched suicide attacks, either by blowing themselves up, or by willingly feeding themselves to the rampaging feybeasts to power them up.

column1: Despite their efforts, no member of the royal family sustained serious injury. However, there were many injured and even several dead among the students.<ref name=""P4V7C16"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 7]]. Chapter 16: Unforseen Consequences</ref>

When he speaks with his son Hildebrand about his situation, he sounds as if he never wanted to be king - a position for which he was never educated - and would be entirely willing to hand over the position to one of his sons, should they come into possession of the lost Grutrissheit and prove themselves to be a proper king candidate.<ref name=""P5V1P"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. column3: Sovereign High Bishop]] announces that the circle in question is part of the selection process for the position of zent and that his conclusion is that Detlinde is a viable candidate. Despite the misgivings of pretty much every noble not of Ahrensbach, Trauerqual states that, should she obtain the [[Grutrissheit]], he would readily cede the throne to her. Privately, he has no confidence in her abilities or temperament, but believes very strongly that the Grutrissheit is a necessity for the ruler. He also seems to have quite some faith in [[Ferdinand]], apparently believing that even with Detlinde's shortcomings, with him at her side it will still work out somehow.<ref name=""P5V3C15"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 3]]. Chapter 15: A Discussion with Eglantine</ref>

column1: When fighting breaks out in the royal palace and Magdalena deduces, that the only person capable of pulling something like this off and hiding for such a long time, can only be Raublut, Trauerqual is shattered by the betrayal and barely able to act for a few seconds. In his stupor, Magdalena begins issuing orders. While under normal circumstances this would be presumptuous, he had just ordered her to take charge of the fighting. A moment later they receive an ordonnanz from [[Ferdinand]] of [[Ehrenfest (Duchy)

'''Urano Motosu''' (本須麗乃, ''Motosu Urano'') was a young college graduate who loved books. She lived with her widowed [[Urano Motosu’s Mother
column2: mother]] prior to her untimely death in an earthquake. She was reincarnated as [[Myne]].

column1: Urano was single-mindedly obsessed with books, even to the moment of her death. She enjoyed not only reading books, but also touching them, smelling them, and being surrounded by them. Although her peers considered her a ""weird bookworm,"" she was content to disregard them if it meant she could keep reading.

This single-mindedness even caused her to occasionally forget to zip up her pants or remove a price-tag before putting on new clothes, as those are issues she contemplates later when thinking on which mistakes she had made in her old life.<ref name=""P4V6C2"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 6]]. Chapter 2: Library Committee Member Get!</ref>

Urano was somewhat lazy and disliked having to do chores, since it meant less time spent reading.<ref name=""P1V1C1"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 1 Volume 1]]. [[Part 1 Volume 1 Chapter 1: A New Life
column2: Chapter 1: A New Life]]</ref> As she told her friend [[Shuu]], she hoped she would one day die in an avalanche of books than slowly pass away in a hospital bed.<ref name=""P1V1P"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 1 Volume 1]]. Prologue</ref>

column1: Urano's father died when she was still very young, leaving behind his collection of books. Urano was subsequently raised only by her [[Urano Motosu’s Mother
column2: mother]].<ref name=""P1V1C1""/> Urano had few memories of her father, but recalled that he once carried her on his shoulders when she was young.

column1: As a child, Urano went to the same daycare as her next-door neighbor [[Shuu]]. They became close friends and spent a lot of time together, although Shuu was often exasperated by Urano's eccentric behavior. Even in kindergarten, Urano was considered a strange, book-obsessed child, because she rarely went out and sometimes went days without eating so she could read.

Urano's mother was an enthusiastic fan of DIY and arts and crafts. She often dragged her daughter into new projects, which meant Urano gained a lot of experience making things by hand. Her mother also bribed her with books to try new hobbies like playing piano and Japanese dance in hopes that she would find something other than reading to occupy her time. Unfortunately, none of the activities stuck.

At the age of 22, just before her college graduation, Urano landed  her dream job as a librarian at the college library.<ref name=""P1V1C1""/> She returned home one day with her friend [[Shuu]] and went to read in her father's book room. However, a minor earthquake hit and Urano was crushed under an avalanche of her own books. Her last memory was praying desperately that she would still read books even in the next life.
*It had been Urano's dream to travel around the world to visit libraries with long a history.
*Urano wore glasses and had her driver's license.
*Urano would write everything she could remember on a notepad so that she could remember them. Because of this, she called herself the ""notepad monster"".

*Urano once wore a frilly mini-skirt maid outfit during her high school culture festival.<ref>''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 1 Volume 3]]. Chapter 6: Completion of my Outfit and Hairpin</ref>

*""Urano Motosu"" (本須麗乃) is a Japanese word play that means ""books must be mine."" Her name after reincarnation, ""Myne,"" is a play on both ""mine"" (belonging to me) and ""main"" (main character).<ref name=""FBQA"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Fanbook]]. Q&A with Miya Kazuki</ref>
**""本"" is the kanji for ""book"", ""須"" can be interpreted as ""must be"" in kanji, and ""Urano (うらの)"" means ""my possession"" or ""mine"".

*When Shuu's girlfriend mistook the friendship between him and Urano as her having a crush on her friend, Urano made up a fictional boy she was in love with to convince her that there was no romantic interest between the two childhood friends.<ref name=""P5V3C16"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 3]]. Chapter 16: Lending Books and a Place for One’s Heart</ref>
'''Urano Motosu's Mother''' was the mother of [[Urano Motosu]], who later became [[Myne]].
Urano's mother was loving and kind, although she often worried about her daughter's single-minded obsession with books. She was overjoyed when her daughter landed her dream job as a librarian.

She also had an impulsive side and often launched into new DIY projects, insisting that her daughter join her in learning how to do them. However, she had a short attention span and often gave up halfway through.

Urano's father died when she was still very young and she was subsequently raised only by her mother.<ref name=""P1V1C1"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 1 Volume 1]]. [[Part 1 Volume 1 Chapter 1: A New Life

*She made Urano practise all sorts of hobbies like playing piano, dancing etc. in hope that she'd find something besides books in her life. Urano went along with anything because her mother bribed her with books. So after the agreed period Urano had quit anything as they took away her reading time.
*She cried tears of joy when Urano got a respectable job.
'''Valamarlene''' was a [[Lanzenave]] princess, born and raised in the [[Royal Academy#Adalgisa Villa
column2: Adalgisa Villa]] in [[Yurgenschmidt]].<ref name=""P5V9E"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 9]]. Epilogue</ref>

column1: Little is known about Valamarlene's appearance, beyond the colours of her eyes and hair - gold and blond repsectively and that she shared a very strong resemblance with her brother Gervasio.<ref name=""P5V9E""/>

Despite technically being a Lanzenave princess, Valamarlene spent her entire life in the Adalgisa Villa in Yurgenschmidt. She was born there as the child of the at the time flower of Loweleier. Since her sister [[Seradina]] was chosen as the next flower, Valamarlene was designated as a bud, meaning if nothing happened to require her to replace the current flower and she didn't find a marriage partner, she would be turned into a feystone.

While living in the side building, she became close with her brother [[Gervasio]], the child chosen as the next king of Lanzenave. So close, that he worked hard to secure her an engagement with the Yurgenschmidt Soverein Knight [[Raublut]]. Since Raublut was only a member of a branch family of an archduke, before becoming a sovereign knight, this was no easy feat, but ultimately Gervasio persevered and managed to secure the engagement.
However, before his sister came of age, [[Adelbert]] - the at the time [[Aub Ehrenfest]] - somehow managed to get his son [[Ferdinand
column2: Quinta]] released from the Adalgisa villa. When Raublut tried to find out how and why, he was unable to, beyond being told that it was because of the ""guidance of the Goddess of Time."" In place of the boy, his mother Seradina was turned into a feystone and Valamarlene was called upon to become the next flower of Loweleier, automatically cancelling her engagement.
