column1: '''Veronica''' (ヴェローニカ, ''Veroonika'') was formerly the first wife of [[Adelbert]], the sixth Aub Ehrenfest. She is the mother of  [[Georgine]], [[Constanze]] and [[Sylvester]].

Perhaps due to witnessing various misfortunes befalling her mother and brothers, Veronica is awfully neurotic, self-centered and paranoid. She takes great pride in her [[Ahrensbach]] lineage<ref name="":0"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 9]]. [[Florencia]] — At the [[Ivory Tower]]</ref> due to her mother's influence. She is also extremely possessive, not allowing [[Adelbert]] to marry second and third wives despite the political necessity.

Veronica is the living embodiment of favouritism and nepotism -- spoiling people in her favour rotten while being outright cruel towards those that aren't. She would pamper people she likes so much, such that she turned a blind eye towards [[Sylvester]] and [[Wilfried]]'s bratty behavior, and even connived at [[Bezewanst]]'s various crimes over the years. On the other hand, she would relentlessly bully and oppress those that she viewed as a threat, regardless of whether they are actually antagonistic or not.

To make matters worse, Veronica is outrageously delusional in a self-serving manner. She truly believed that [[Florencia]] seduced Sylvester for ulterior motives, and that [[Ferdinand]] was plotting to take Sylvester's position. Even after being imprisoned, she never repented for any of her countless crimes. Instead, she victimized herself and blamed it as Ferdinand and [[Rozemyne]]'s conspiracy.<ref name=""P3V5C8"" /> She is also delusional enough to believe that [[Georgine]] would save her, despite the fact that Georgine clearly viewed her in contempt during her visit.<ref name="":0"" />

column2: political faction]] was the most powerful and influential in Ehrenfest. It was in a power struggle with both the older [[Ehrenfest (Duchy)#Leisegang Faction
column4: Florencia faction]]. She was powerful enough to manipulate things behind the scenes, which caused a lot of friction within Ehrenfest nobles. She was very protective of her little brother, the former High Bishop [[Bezewanst]], and used her power to protect him from any issues caused by his corruption and criminal activities.

column1: When her first child [[Georgine]] was born, Veronica began a brutal training regime to prepare her for the position of archduchess from an early age and regularly beat her as part of the education, so she wouldn't lose to her cousin [[Karstedt]]. Upon the birth of her second child, Veronica openly showed her disappointment at having just ""another girl"" and neglected [[Constanze]] almost completely. However, when her third child [[Sylvester]] was a born a boy, she endlessly doted on the boy. Whenever Georgine scolded her younger brother for not working as hard as she had been forced to at his age, Veronica would scold Georgine and make her apologize to Sylvester. Likewise she would reprimand anyone else, except [[Rihyarda]], if they voiced any criticism of Sylvester, causing the boy to became a spoiled brat and fostering envy and hostility in Georgine for her brother.

When her parents made it clear to Georgine, that she would never become the Aub and they expected her only to support her brother, Georgine once again tried to educate the boy and turn him into a worthy successor, but since she considered the brutal methods that Veronica used on her as normal, this was perceived as bullying by Sylvester and many of the duchy's nobles.

At Sylvester's [[baptism]], Veronica loudly declared before the entire nobility of Ehrenfest, that he would be the next archduke, despite the current Aub not having made any such decision. But to keep up the impression of a united front within the archduke's family, Adelbert refrained from contradicting her right there and then. Rumors of Georgine dropping out of the competition for the Aub's seat soon reached her fiancé's family and they canceled the engagement. When Georgine went to complain and beg her parent to do something about it, Veronica immediately shot her down, stating that there was no need for a foreign archduke candidate to marry into Ehrenfest to Georgine, since she'll never be Aub anyway and instead she should put her efforts into marrying into a higher ranked duchy's archduke family to better support Sylvester.

Not long after, Veronica and her husband discover, that Georgine had began to build a power base and make noble give their names to her in the shadows, while carefully spreading rumours about Sylvester to undermine him. Disappointed that their she would work against her brother, rather than supporting him, they prepared to marry her off into another duchy. Veronica reached out to her relatives in Ahrensbach and eventually managed to arrange for Georgine to become [[Gieselfried
column2: Aub Ahrensbach]]'s third wife. The girl was very unhappy with the prospect of having to marry a man as old as her own father and being forced to leave her home, but Veronica wouldn't hear any of it and just scolded her about how lucky she was to marry in the archducal family of a greater duchy and that she should be thankful to her mother for arranging such a beneficial match.

column1: At a dinner soon after, Sylvester falls victim to an assassination attempt, utilizing the very same kind of poison, that Veronica herself often used in the past to rid herself of perceived enemies and obstacles. While Veronica herself is frozen in terror, one of her retainers immediately springs into action and administers an antidote, barely saving the boy's life.<ref name=""P5V8E"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 5 Volume 8]]. Epilogue</ref>

When [[Ferdinand]] was brought into the family, Veronica immediately showed a great antipathy toward him, which over the years grew to outright abuse and paranoia. Despite how helpful and supportive he was to his half-brother Sylvester, Veronica still became convinced that he was plotting the downfall of everyone she held dear and plotting to take over the duchy for himself. While her husband was still in relatively good health, he prevented things from going too far, resulting in Veronica only antagonizing and bullying Ferdinand, but as Adelbert's health declined, Veronica's abuse grew ever worse, eventually escalating to outright assassination attempts, as Adelbert was lying on his deathbed. To escape her mistreatment, Ferdinand renounced his position in noble society and joined the [[Temple]]. While this stopped Veronica from directly interfering with him, it did little to disabuse her of her misconceptions, and she remained very hostile to him.

However, Ferdinand was not the only target for Veronica's cruelty. Anyone related or affiliated with any of her own half-siblings found themselves constant targets of ridicule and harassment, whenever she could get away with it. She displayed a particular hostility toward [[Elvira]] and her brother, almost bringing their entire home province of [[Haldenzel]] to ruin, by using her brother's position as [[Temple Hierarchy#High Bishop
column2: High Bishop]] to deny them [[Divine Instruments#Small Chalices
column3: Small Chalices]] for the [[Spring Prayer]] and by imposing harsh taxes on them, leading Elvira to gather all the people wronged by Veronica to form a counter-faction for their self protection.<ref name=""P4V3C2"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 3]]. Chapter 2: Mother and Printing in Haldenzel</ref>

column1: She was also rather hostile to Sylvester's wife [[Florencia]], practically forcing her to join Elvira's faction for protection and support, instead of trying to get her to join Veronica's own faction. When Sylvester and Florencia had their first child, Veronica personally took charge of the child's rearing, practically stealing the boy away from his mother, claiming that Florencia was not skilled or dedicated enough to properly prepare Wilfried for his future position of archduke. His grandmother's coddling of the boy, as well as Sylvester designating him as his successor without the need to compete for the position, caused Wilfried to become lazy and arrogant, running away from most of his lessons.

After he married Florencia, Veronica was very insistent that Sylvester take a second wife, but he stoutly refused. This was the first open sign of defiance that he ever showed to his mother, even leading to some nobles thinking that Veronica's influence might wane, though that did not happen.<ref name=""FB2S5"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Fanbook 2]]. Story 5: A Tea Party with My Older Sister</ref>

Likely due to the girl's close resemblance to her mother Florencia, Veronica was very harsh to [[Charlotte]], though thankfully she didn't go so far as to outright bully her granddaughter, like she did with so many other people, including her own half-siblings, their descendants, and Florencia herself.<ref name=""P4V3C4"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 3]]. Chapter 4: The End of Winter and the Summoned Merchants</ref>
When Bezewanst had problems getting a [[Count Bindewald
column2: foreign noble]] into the city in his plan to get rid of [[Myne]] due to heightened security measures, Veronica helps her brother by forging a permit with the archduke's personal seal.

Like all of Geduldh's subordinates, she was driven away by [[Ewigeliebe]] shortly after his wedding with the Goddes of Earth. Upon learning that they had been chased away, Geduldh had wept and protested that she would refuse all clothes not made with cloth woven by Wentuchte. Such a master of her craft was the Goddess of Weaving that cloth of the highest quality was praised as being ""excellent enough to have come from her hands."" new Zent]], with access to the country's foundation chosen, albeit not a true one, Wentuchte and Dregarnuhr discover that a single thread in the tapestry of history has been severed and if left alone, this would eventually result in the history of the last two decades being erased. The thread belongs to [[Ferdinand]]. Thankfully [[Rozemyne]]'s thread is close enough in colour, that, given he obtains the consent of the two mortals, [[Sterrat]] is able to weave the two threads together, which will repair Ferdinand's, albeit with Rozemyne losing a number of years off her life expectancy. column1: While the goddesses ponder how to overcome this obstacle, [[Hannelore]] accidentally puts mana into a prayer to Dregarnuhr, due to being so upset, she isn't in full control of her mana, which allows the Goddess of Time to summon the girl to her. Hannelore agrees to briefly lend the goddess her body, to contact Rozemyne and shortly after, Hannelore's friend arrives in the void, into which Hannelore was called.

There the goddesses explain the problem and Rozemyne quickly agrees to the deities' proposal. Despite expressing that she does not understand why Wentuchte and Dregarnuhr would bother over a mere 20 years and saying she'd only do anything if it was at least two centuries, Liebeskhilfe still goes along with the other deities and plucks the threads of Ferdinand and Rozemyne from history, for Sterrat to weave together.

That by itself however is not enough to repair Ferdinand's thread, so Dregarnuhr and Wentuchte send Rozemyne back into the past, to the moment, when Ferdinand's thread was severed. As a reward for lending Dregarnuhr her body, Hannelore is granted a wish and she uses it to have her consciousness sent back one year into the past, to get another chance to convey her feelings to [[Wilfried]]. Dregarnuhr appears to have some reservations, but Liebeskhilfe pushes Hannelore into Wentuchte's tapestry, before the other goddess can react.<ref name=""HP1V1C13"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]].'' Due to Ehrenfest being much shorter on manpower in general compared to the greater duchy of Dunkelfelger and also currently being low on supplies on account of the hunt for the [[Lord of Winter]], Aub Ehrenfest suggests a very small-scale competition between just one knight of each duchy, which Aub Dunkelfelger accepts and immediately asks for Ferdinand to be Ehrenfest's champion.

Ferdinand turns out to be very reluctant to participate, seeing no personal gain for himself in the endeavour, but is eventually convinced to join when his old student-days rival [[Heisshitze]] wagers several valuable materials for the chance to win back his old cape from Ferdinand, which he lost to him during their shared time at the Royal Academy. Apart from the personal bets of the two champions, the duchy of the winner will receive the rights to produce and sell books from Rozemyne's manuscript.

For reasons beyond their understanding and very much to their dismay, Rozemyne and Hannelore are pulled into the match, with both knights declaring they wouldn't let anything happen to their respective ladies. Since Ferdinand is eager to get this matter over with as soon as possible, the match will be held immediately, so they can be back in time to watch the second part of the ditter tournament, in which the apprentice knights of both duchies are participating.<ref name=""P4V7C12"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 4 Volume 7]]. Interduchy Tournament (Second Year)</ref>

Shortly after the end of Hannelore's fourth year at the Royal Academy, Ehrenfest contacts Dunkelfelger to inform them of Ahrensbach committing treason and trying to kill Ferdinand, as well as their intentions to ally with Dunkelfelger to launch an assault, or as Rozemyne words it ""true ditter,"" to steal the enemy's foundation and rescue Ferdinand. Despite his eagerness to join the fray, his wife is able to reign in his passion and convince the Aub to remain in Dunkelfelger, so she and him can come to the Zent's aid at a moment's notice, should he call for them. Likewise Sieglinde convinces Lestilaut to guard their foundation. Only Hannelore is permitted to join the assault force, so she can cleanse the shame of throwing her previous ditter match.

column1: '''Wilfried''' (ヴィルフリート ''Virufuriito'') is the first-born child of [[Sylvester]] and [[Florencia]] and an archduke candidate of [[Ehrenfest]]. He is the older brother of [[Charlotte]] and [[Melchior]], and the adoptive older brother of [[Rozemyne]].
Initially designated as the next aub, his reputation has diminished throughout the series. After the cancellation of his engagement with [[Rozemyne]], he is no longer considered the next aub.

Wilfried has dark green eyes and light gold hair that tends to stick up in the front. Other than the colour of his hair, he bears a strong resemblance to his father, [[Sylvester]].<ref name=""P3V1C4"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 1]]. Chapter 4: Adoption</ref>

As a child, Wilfried has a kind heart, but is irresponsible and childish. Although he is expected to become the next [[Aub Ehrenfest]], he does not take his responsibilities seriously and often runs away from his retainers and tutors. In spite of his poor work ethic, he has a good memory and is a fast learner.

After his carefree attitude almost costs him his position as an archduke candidate, Wilfried’s attitude changes dramatically and he begins to take his studies seriously. The lesson is later reinforced when he loses the right of succession and is forced to take on some of his adoptive sister [[Rozemyne

Having become more mature, Wilfried now works hard to keep up with the expectations of his position. While he’s often exasperated by Rozemyne’s antics, he sees it as his responsibility to watch out for her and ensure that she acts in the best interests of Ehrenfest.

Wilfried is very earnest and trusting towards people, a trait that Ferdinand regarded as his precious virtue.<ref name=""P3V5C9"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]'' [[Light Novel]]. [[Part 3 Volume 5]]. Chapter 9: Wilfried's Punishment</ref> On a flip side, he is also gullible and has a poor judge of character, like when he doesn't realize that the actions and advices by his retainers are causing him to needlessly antagonize other nobles and archduke candidates, making him unpopular.

Wilfried was born as the first-born son of [[Sylvester]], the archduke of Ehrenfest, and his first wife [[Florencia]]. Although most duchies operate on a meritocratic system to decide the best candidate for the next archduke, Sylvester  changed the method of succession. Because he didn't want his own children to be driven apart by the fight for the archduke title like he and his oldest sister [[Georgine]] were, [[Sylvester]] decreed Wilfried as his successor the moment it was clear he had the necessary [[mana]] capacity for the position.

Determined to raise the next Aub, Sylvester's mother [[Veronica]] used her influence to take custody of Wilfried and raised him away from his mother, Florencia. As a result, Wilfried rarely saw his mother except during meals, and he felt a strong familial affection for Veronica, his grandmother.

Although Veronica claimed she would raise Wilfried properly, she gave him a free rein. He grew up spoiled and irresponsible, often ran away from his lessons, and soon fell behind in his studies as a result. His retainers were reluctant to reprimand him because they feared losing their position as servants to the next archduke. Even after he was baptized at age seven, Wilfried had trouble reading, was unable to do simple math, and could not play the [[harspiel]], all important skills that noble children are expected to learn.
However, his parents were slow to realize the severity of Wilfried’s situation, since Veronica had reduced their contact with their son to a minimum.

Upon Veronica's imprisonment Wilfried was told that his grandmother had fallen ill and had been moved to a far away place to recover. To justify why he could not visit her he was told that it was to make sure he didn't catch the illness from her.<ref name=""SSC1C12"">''[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]''. [[Short Story Collection 1]]. Chapter 12: Wilfried — Time with My Siblings</ref>

After Christine left the temple, her retainers were returned to the orphanage, where Wilma takes upon the task to look after the unbaptized orphans.

Zack has a competitive, enthusiastic demeanor. He is very confident in his skills, and he has the talent to back it up.<ref name=""P3V1C17""/>

Although Zack feels a sense of rivalry with his fellow smith [[Johann]], their talents and personalities make them an effective team. A gifted engineer, Zack can design efficient and workable blueprints based on very general instructions, while Johann has the skill to precisely execute those designs.
Zack was trained and works for the Verde workshop in [[City of Ehrenfest

Having worked as apprentice smiths around the same time and both being among the most talented apprentices of their age-group, Zack developed a one-sided rivalry with [[Johann]]. However is somewhat dismayed to learn that the title is not exclusive and that he will be one of several Gutenbergs.

column1: Originally Zack was supposed to accompany Lady Rozemyne to [[Kirnberger]] and help with the establishment of new workshops in the spring after her third year at the Royal Academy. Due to getting married this year however, Zack requests to be allowed to stay in Ehrenfest and the High Bishop gives her permission. At the same meeting [[Josef]] reports that his wife [[Heidi]] is pregnant and thus Rozemyne aquits them and have a replacement go in their stead. This gives her the idea to use this opportunity to foster the next generation of craftspeople and thus she requests that all the Gutenbergs either take along their chosen successors or send them entirely in their own stead.<ref name=""P5V4C12"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 5 Volume 4]]. Chapter 15: The Disciples of the Gutenbergs</ref>

Apparently the pair wanted to wait a bit longer, but with Zack's frequent and lengthy absences, due to establishing new workshops all over Ehrenfest, their parents lose patience and demand they either marry right away, or stop seeing each other.

The couple chooses the former and get married in the summer after Rozemyne's third year at the Royal Academy.<ref name=""P5V6C14"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 5 Volume 6]]. Chapter 14: The Trombe Hunt and the Starbind Ceremony</ref>

Zack is quite willing to just pledge himself to Rozemyne right away, since his wife expressed eagerness to accompany him on his journeys to other cities. column1: '''Zasha''' (ザシャ ''Zasha'') is one of [[Myne]]'s neighbours. He is the eldest of four brothers, and the older brother of [[Lutz]].
Zasha is a boy with violet hair and brown eyes. He has a strong body due to his work in a carpentry.

Along with his other brothers, Zasha occasionally does little tasks for Myne and Lutz for some extra pocket money, like carving the wooden parts for hairpins or engraving illustrations that Wilma drew on wood. Though the latter does not work very well due to them not having the proper tools and their regular knives not allowing them to be precise enough.
Unlike many other commoners of the [[City of Ehrenfest]], Zasha didn't have the opportunity to be blessed by the new [[Rozemyne
column2: High Bishop]]. When it was his turn, she was apparently otherwise engaged and thus another priest performed his coming-of-age ceremony.<ref name=""P5V6C9"">[[Ascendance of a Bookworm]]. [[Part 5 Volume 6]]. Chapter 9: The Spring Coming-of-Age Ceremony and Sylvester’s Departure</ref>
